Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What epic moment in history did you witness?
Answer: I’d like you to imagine a city of seven million souls, rising up almost as one. One day out seven million people, two million are out in the streets. It was eerie. Schools were empty. Shops closed. Students marching alongside teachers. Police officers, nurses, elderly grandparents hoisting granchildren onto their shoulders… words don’t really do justice to the sheer size of the 2019–2020 Hong Kong protests. Nor do pictures fully capture the massiveness of the seas of people gathered there… You’d be anywhere in the city away from the mass of protesters, and you would be struck by how… empty it was. Like a post-apocalyptic scene. It seemed as if almost everyone was out there, at first. Of course the authorities did all they could to lessen turnout, to thwart protesters and eventually beat them down by any means necessary. And as the months went by, crowd sizes went down significantly. But nothing I’ve ever seen will compare to those first days of protest. It was a whole city coming together as one soul. Speaking with what seemed like one voice. And saying, loud and clear: “We do NOT want to be a part of China and fall under China’s corrupt jurisdiction!” We all know what happened. How the protests were crushed and how — conveniently — Covid-19 arrived just around that time. Suddenly ‘mass gatherings’ were forbidden altogether. For public health reasons, the authorities said. Hong Kong had been promised autonomy and the right to elect its own leadership until the year 2047, but Xi callously rolled back all promises and brought the city-state to heel. A vibrant culture was crushed overnight. But I was there to see it’s defiant last stand. And it was spectacular.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which inaccuracies written about a famous historical figure have not been successfully corrected and for what particular reasons?
Answer: In 2022, Jada Pinkett-Smith, the bald wife of actor Will Smith, became famous when her husband slapped presenter Chris Rock in the face for telling a joke about her. In 2023, Pinkett-Smith struck again — this time by releasing a Netflix show about Cleopatra in which she was portrayed by a black actress . Even the country of Egypt itself was annoyed by the portrayal and many Egyptian viewers called in and wrote angry letters to Netflix to complain.[1] Because Cleopatra wasn’t black — she was the direct descendant of a Macedonian general of Alexander the Great, Ptolemy. Ptolemy himself being a rumored half-brother of Alexander. Greeks and Macedonians come in various shades, some being pale and others more olive-skinned. But none of them are “black”. Ptolemy took mostly Greek and Macedonian wives. And his family was rife with incest to ‘keep the blood pure’. Cleopatra wouldn’t have been black… couldn’t possibly have been black. But some people still cling to this weird illusion of Cleopatra being a black woman. They could have just done a little more digging and quickly discover that ancient Egypt had countless dynasties and that some pharaohs had been darker-skinned. But they can’t be arsed… it has to be Cleopatra because she boned Julius Caesar and Mark Antony and she was cool and glamorous…

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is feminism about hating men?
Answer: Not by design, no. It’s actually fairly straight-forward — feminism is about equal rights. At least on paper, that is. That doesn’t mean people don’t get… carried away. And that some feminists aren’t constantly talking about how awful men are. Because they do. It’s all many of them online talk about. They can’t form a proper sentence without throwing the word ‘men’ in it or ‘patriarchy’. Like a Pokémon repeating its own name. A lot of online activism is centered around the concept that “not all men are bad but all men benefit from the actions of bad men”. They have created this fantasy world in which any man who isn’t speaking out every second of every day about how awful women have it and how awful other men are, is somehow inherently “complicit” in this mythical beast called “the patriarchy”. As a result, modern day feminism is incredibly toxic. And it’s also incredibly performative, and fake. I should know this — I had a brief little love affair with a young feminist. And yes, she was lost alright. Personal issues drove her to say the things she said and half the time, she didn’t even truly feel that way… she just wanted the other e-activists to suck her proverbial dong for saying outrageously anti-men things. She eventually made a big deal out of wanting to come across as impartial, but it never quite worked. A lot of her more aggressive outbursts came from a place of anger, of being fundamentally broken on some level. She was fascinating. Complex. And a lost soul, like any of us. And that’s kind of how it always goes, isn’t it? In any movement for equality or ‘fairness’, the other gender or the other race or the other group that is ‘privileged’ lives rent-free in your head. You obsess over them. Because the “bad men” and the “bad women”, the “misogynist” and the “rabid feminist” are all the dual sides of a single coin. They need each other. Modern feminism needs bad men. And it needs all men to be bad as much as a medieval pope needs all women to be guilty of Eve’s love of apples.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the worst-case scenario for Russia?
Answer: For the last twenty years or so, Russia’s game plan has been to influence Western politics. Help influence elections in the EU and America to get people elected that will help Russia geopolitically. The worst case for Putin’s Russia would be Trump losing in November 2024. Because a Trump presidency is Putin’s final Hail Mary. The last trick up the sleeve of the Kremlin’s house elf. Either Russia has to deal with a Democrat in office who will continue to arm Ukraine with military aid packages and heavy equipment worth tens of billions of dollars, or a Republican gets in who will turn off the faucet and cut off supplies… Ukraine cannot effectively defend its territory and win the war without Western support. And by Western support, I mean American support — no one in the world has the capacity to produce military equipment that America has. Putin knows this. The worst case scenario for Putin, is his creature losing in November 2024 and Trump not taking the White House. If Russia manages to stay in the war until then and elect a friendly ally in America, they’ll probably win the war sometime in 2025. Kiev will be forced to sue for peace.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is your personal opinion of a white nationalist?
Answer: This isn’t a topic I’ve written about a lot in the past — for obvious reasons. It’s kind of embarrassing. And it doesn’t make me feel good. But as a teenager I dabbled in white nationalism, myself. As a result I have some… insider perspectives, you could say. I’ll write this piece from that perspective. Of someone whose “been there, done that, took some pictures”. It’s easy to hate the “white nationalist” and call it a day. But it’s more worthwhile to dig a little deeper and go into the uncomfortable why of it all. When I was in high school, there were many groups of kids. There were groups like ‘nerds’ or ‘stoners’ or ’sporty people’ that had members of all races. There were also groups for one race. “The black guys” or “the Arab guys” or “Asian guys”. Now if you did something bad to, say, the sons of Muslim immigrants? You’d get your ass kicked by the whole group. Same with the blacks, the Asians, you name it… But there wasn’t a group for the “white guys”. There was zero solidarity for someone on a racial basis if you were white. So basically, you couldn’t mess with a lot of these ‘minority’ groups. Because they’d stick up for each other. Whites never stuck up for each other. They didn’t have a “one for all, and all for one” musketeer mentality the way other groups had it. The only all-white groups that stood up for themselves were ‘bad seeds’… the skinheads, the Neo-Nazi’s, far-right folks. All the other racial groups shit-talked and bantered a lot of negative stuff about white people. And only the ‘racist extremist’ white groups did the same. It’s not hard to see why a young person would get sucked into such an extremist group. It isn’t something that you can predict, and it’s hard to prevent. You basically have a whole generation of white kids who are told from an early age that their ancestors suck and their culture is stolen and copy-pasted from other nations, they have no heritage and if they do, it’s a shameful one… all other groups are A-okay and should, by all means, be proud of their heritage. But not the white folks. Never the white folks. Because that’d make them a Nazi. Evidently, I grew up. Grew out of this uncomfortable phase of life. But I still see why. Why this movement has an appeal. Why the “alt-right” draws young white kids in. Corrupts them. And infuses racial pride with ‘Hitler was kinda cool’… it continues to appeal to people because both politicians, school administration and the authorities are too afraid to dig a little deeper. And ask uncomfortable questions. And white kids will continue to want to belong, to have words only they can use, spaces of their own. Any other group wants it and is granted such spaces and applauded for it… not if you’re white, though. Then you’re Hitler.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do looks really matter? How much of your life is influenced by your appearance?
Answer: Various studies have proven that handsome men and beautiful women are more likely to get hired for a job interview. They get better evaluations at work and get a raise more often, on average.[1] People always focus on dating, but even in one’s professional life, looks matter. Looks always matter. I won’t give you empty platitudes. Won’t insult your intelligence by beating around the bush — looks are incredibly important in this world. The picture above is the same man. One is just a fitter, more well-groomed version of the first. Which of these men is treated better by society? You know the answer. We all do — it’s the bearded ginger viking on the right. We have a reasonable amount of control over our looks. Through grooming, exercise, proper nutrition and styling, we can alter our appearance a great deal. And yes, we benefit from this. Some unappealing people are merely lazy and clueless about how to dress, how to carry their frame and how to wear their hair. And little changes, over time, add up. In a year or so, any man or woman can transform almost completely. And be reborn, in the eyes of the world. Do looks really matter? You bet. You can come up with anecdotal evidence about how you, personally, don’t care about looks. Or how your wife/girlfriend/boss doesn’t care. But society as a whole does care.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who among the former U.S. Presidents would you trust the most with your life savings, and what qualities make them trustworthy?
Answer: Most Presidents I’d trust about as far as I can throw them. But there’s a special place in my heart for the sort of man who, at the age of three, could meet a newborn baby next door. And telling his mother with his little shining eyes and the earnesty of a child that he’ll marry her some day… And actually doing exactly that… actually meeting that girl again, years later, and marrying her. That’s love. And it’s powerful. You could argue the little boy, once he grew up, wasn’t perhaps the world’s best president. You could just as easily make the case that his opponent, Ronald Reagan, broke the Logan Act in communicating with the Iranians behind closed doors and screwing the President over, thus winning the presidency… in the end, it doesn’t matter much — he’s got my vote in the “trustworthy” department. I can’t distrust a small town boy who knew exactly who he’d marry even when he could barely walk and talk. And stayed faithfully with her for 77 years. No man is a saint but Jimmy Carter wouldn’t screw me out of my life savings — he’d probably invest it and set up a peanut farm and dilligently keep track of profits.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is it a crime to be a Nazi/Neo Nazi in Russia? Why or why not?
Answer: Officially? Yes. In practice? Not one bit… See, Russia is ashamed of its WWII history. Not the actions of the Red Army during the later parts of the war, but their open collaboration with Hitler’s Germany in the years leading up to it. Below we see a man named Dmitri Utkin, commander of Prigozhin’s Wagner Group. In the middle of the group of five, we see Putin. Utkin was a Neo-Nazi. It is no coincidence that the private military group was called the “Wagner Group” — Adolf Hitler’s favorite composer was the talented but fiercely antisemitic Richard Wagner. A man Hitler admired so madly that he at some point tried to seduce and marry Wagner’s granddaughter just to get some of his glory to rub off on the Austrian dictator. Now if some random dude posts all day about Hitler being awesome, in Russia, he’ll probably be in some trouble. In Russian history, Stalin is good, Hitler bad, and this can’t be debated. Bringing up the fact that Hitler and Stalin were once best buds and invaded Poland together in a joint-effort to start WWII, won’t make you any friends in Putin’s Russia… But you can be a Neo-Nazi, if you want. And lead an armed group named after Hitler’s favorite composer. With little SS symbols tattood on your neck. And Putin will gladly pose with you and make good use of you… only to dispose of you when your boss, Prigozhin, gets a little too uppity. Prigozhin himself being part Jewish, for the record — make it make sense.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who is the smartest person in history? How do you know that he/she is smarter than others?
Answer: The grand-nephew of Julius Caesar, Octavian, was a frighteningly smart man. He was well-read, and incredibly well-educated. In Greece as a youth he studied, among many fields, astrology. Keenly aware that he was of the superstitious nature of Roman citizens, he used it to his advantage in a spectacular way… Declaring three days of national mourning following Caesar’s murder, Octavian timed the festivities in such a manner that a comet he knew would come, would appear on the third and final day. He then declared that the comet was his great-uncle Caesar “ascending to Heaven” and used it as further evidence that Julius Caesar was, indeed, a God. Octavian himself was the adoptive son of his great-uncle, and was now the son of a literal God in the eyes of his people. The clever young patrician even had coins minted starring himself and the comet, further capitalizing on the myth. It is no wonder that Octavian ended up becoming Emperor Augustus, first Emperor of Rome. He used knowledge as a weapon, and information as a tool to gain power. One of the most brilliant, scheming, calculating men in the history of this world.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How do you assess the arrest of Telegram's boss Pavel Durov by French intelligence services?
Answer: It sets a dangerous precedent. Because think of Mr. Durov whatever you want, Telegram as a service has value. It allowed revolutionaries to plan protests from Iran to Hong Kong, allowed freedom of speech to occur even under oppressive regimes… Honestly? I kind of love Telegram, its flaws notwithstanding. When Hong Kongers stood up in enormous numbers to Chinese oppression, it was Telegram that allowed them when other apps and communication channels had been breached. When Iranian women stood up to their brutal government, it was Telegram they used to plan it all… I say the guy who facilitated all that is a pretty swell dude, if for that fact alone. Now there are issues, of course — real, genuine issues. Some of the content floating around Telegram is questionable, to say the least. And not everyone on the site has noble intentions. It has criminals, too. Drug dealers. Even pedophiles. And I agree wholeheartedly with French authorities that the app ought to make more of an effort to remove such nasty elements and cooperate with law enforcement in such matters… But to arrest the CEO and actually float around the idea of banning Telegram altogether? That’s ain’t it, chief. I don’t like Durov particularly much. Nor am I fond of Zuckerberg or Musk. In fact all three of them are odious in their own unique ways. But I still love freedom of speech more than I dislike any of them. And I always will.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How do I know if celebrities are fake?
Answer: Just look at how a person treats his or her staff. Anyone “lower” on the societal or career totem pole than them, really. Look whether or not their off-camera actions match their behavior when filmed. I read this answer the other day about how staff for Meghan Markle and Prince Harry keeps quitting because they’re supposedly “very demanding” and rather mean.[1] Those sort of stories keep making the round — one royal household staff member with decades of service quit for this very reason, a few years ago. Now the on-camera behavior, of course, is usually a very different story… snappy photo-ops will show the oft-criticized celebrity hanging out happily with The Poors® and everyone will act as if they’re awesome and wonderful for this… and that’s kind of what poor folks in third world countries exist for, in the eys of rich Westerners — photo-ops to show they care. To deflect any criticism of the celebrity being out-of-it, living in a bubble, or being “mean”. Because surely no rich person photographed smiling brightly in a sea of poor folks can ever be mean, can they? If you want to know which celebrities are fake and which aren’t, look at how they treat their staff. Charity is easy enough; give a small percentage of your earnings away, set up some organization, take some pics, and you’re elevated to sainthood. Look at how they treat the ‘little people’ they work with every day… that’ll tell you all you need to know.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is China a fascist police state?
Answer: Another answer to this question is a rather cheap appeal to emotion — a young girl tried to drown herself, and killed a cop who was in the process of saving her, therefore “China isn’t fascist”… let us look strictly at the facts here of what fascism entails: “Fascism an authoritarian, ultranationalist political ideology and movement, characterized by a dictatorial leader, centralized autocracy, militarism, forcible suppression of opposition, belief in a natural social hierarchy, subordination of individual interests for the perceived good of the nation or race, and strong regimentation of society and the economy” China is undeniably authoritarian — it is ruled, and has been ruled, by a single party for over 75 years. No other parties are allowed to exist. Government is centralized, there is a single President and he has no term limits. There is no voting, and party big-wigs decide policy together. There’s “voting” on proposals but only high-ranking members of the party vote on these, and votes are ALWAYS unanimous China is fiercely nationalistic, and believes in some sort of “blut und boden” philosophy wherein any territory that was once Chinese, must be “returned to the Motherland”. Nazi Germany, of course, did the same with Austria and parts of Poland — history must be vindicated, and the ‘chosen people’ need their lebensraum. In June 2024, a Japanese couple and their child were attacked by a knife-wielding Chinese nationalist in Suzhou, China. A Japanese woman and hern child were injured.[1] Just a few days prior to the attack, an American student academic was randomly stabbed by a Chinese man for daring to bump into him — the Chinese man freaked out and stabbed him, nearly killing the man.[2] Which is ironic as China has been trying to boost tourism and get more people to visit their nation… tourist sector was hit hard by Covid-19 and China’s ailing economy needs the foreign money quite badly. I’ll be the first to admit — people are still people. In the Suzhou knife attack, for example? A Chinese lady actually tried to stop the attacker and was killed by him in the process. So not all Chinese people are crazed ultra-nationalists. Fact remains, for years the “wolf warrior” diplomacy has made Beijing throw its diplomatic, economic and military weight around. Foreigners and any non-Chinese were demonized. And opposition figures are either jailed, dead or fled abroad. I’d say if China isn’t a textbook example of modern-day fascism, I don’t know what country is…

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some cultural practices that are outdated and no longer useful in our society?
Answer: One thing that comes to mind is the concept of dowry — the family of a bride having to pay a substantial amount to that of the groom. Many cultures still do this, even moderately well-off and otherwise well-educated families. Parents, furthermore, are expected to pay for the expenses of lavish wedding ceremonies. And it seems so ridiculous to me. Because a lot of goverments are concerned about ever-shrinking birth rates… And one reason families get smaller and people often don’t marry — they simply cannot afford it. Parents, too, can’t afford to send children to college. And then when their child marries, they spend an absolute fortune on a wedding… the child then decides not to have children, fearful of not being able to give the child a good education and send them to a decent college… why didn’t the parents just forego the expensive wedding ceremony and not put the money in a fund for their future grandkids’ education? Cultural expectation dictates you marry and reproduce, but simultaneously archaic cultural expectations make it harder and harder for young people to afford doing so. You break your backs for a lifetime, and blast life savings in expensive over-the-top ceremonies… the next generation either repeats this mistake, or opts out altogether because they can’t afford to even produce that next generation to begin with. All that just to show off your opulence to the world. My grandfather used to joke about people in expensive jewelry and the finest clothes: “They look like a big shot,” he’d say, “but keep in mind — they wear everything they own on their skin and have nothing else left.”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What can immediately make a person unattractive?
Answer: A big one is body odor. If a person doesn’t smell right, attraction dies on the vine. I once read a story about a famous actor turning down Marilyn Monroe, despite her being rather into him and “ready to go”… he had her in front of him. Needed only to say the word. But she smelled bad. And she didn’t take care of herself. And any other man would have been able to overlook it — it’s Marilyn Monroe, after all. Of all people! A queen, no, a goddess amongst women! To the actor it was a dealbreaker. And I’ve seen this play out in life, in a way. A beautiful person with horribly decaying teeth? No way, José. A gorgeous face may lean in for a kiss and if the smell from his or her mouth is the foul scent of death… that’s the end of all attraction. Be clean. Be fresh. Smell right, so people will be eager to taste you, be near you, explore you. But smell like death and it’s the death of your dating life. Not to all people — desperation’s one hell of a drug — but to many.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What should I value most in life?
Answer: I’ll let Conan answer this question: “To crush your enemies, see them driven before you, and to hear the lamentations of their women.” Which doesn’t mean I am advocating you to go through life raping and pillaging, raising hell and burning cities to the ground — this is the year 2024, after all. What I am saying is: dominate. Be dominant, be assertive, know what you want and go get it. Time is incredibly precious. And incredibly fleeting. So many people are weak pushovers, doormats who just let whatever happens, happen. They don’t make a stand. They don’t speak clearly and honestly, with intent. But they bullshit their way through life. Walking forever on eggshells, doing the same old “don’t offend anyone, don’t rock the boat” song a dance. I say, DO rock that boat. Crush the eggshells. Dance around nothing, but barge right in. Grab life by the balls. You should value strength, energy, passion. And cultivate these qualities within yourself. The meek shall not inherit the earth — they merely have the earth stolen from them. Their birthright denied, their rights trampled and their protests drowned out of in the laughter of their betters. Dominate. Value strength. And use it for good.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some examples of casual racism that are hurtful and damaging, but that most people don’t think is a big deal?
Answer: Many children in well-off nation are told to finish their plates and not be wasteful. And do it “because there are children in Africa starving right now”. It’s a very casual line, used often and with gusto. It makes sense, too, on some level — the child is taught to think of the less fortunate. And the child is kind of guilt-tripped into finishing his food, finishing the veggies and other healthy but less-appealing parts of the dinner. The implication is, of course, that Africa is a backwards, poor, shitty place where kids are all routinely starving to death. How fortunate the Western child is not to starve. It completely ignores the fact that Africa is a massive continent, full of rich and vibrant cultures. And that it has wealthy cities, too. Wealthy people. That it has nations poor, and nations well-off. That it has entrepeneurs as well as starving peasants. From an early age, in the minds of many a Western child, this image is created of Africa as “that continent of the starving people”. That continent you must think of when you don’t feel like eating your meal. That continent that instills in you no admiration, no passion, no genuine interest… only a pang of guilt that makes you finish your Brussels Sprouts or your green beans. How is that not racist as hell?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What event surprised you today?
Answer: Read an article about Donald Trump being tricked by AI into believing Taylor Swift had endorsed him.[1] He also shared screenshots to a fake news story about “Swifties” turning around from liberalism and going right for him. I know some elderly people are a bit “digitally illiterate”, sure. And I know that Trump is 78 years old so far from a spring chicken. But I still hadn’t expected him to be dumb enough to be tricked this easily. This isn’t rocket science, either — Taylor Swift is pretty liberal. Her fanbase is, too. Like other major artists, she’s only ever endorsed Democrats. And much like the fans of Beyoncé, Swift’s dedicated legion of concert-goers and album-buyers tend to just go with her flow. She “yass-queened” herself into political relevance just by the virtue of her enormous popularity… I know the guy is desperate. I just didn’t know he’s this desperate. It’s like a scrawny kid photoshopping his own head on the body of the Rock and post it on social media, expecting his friends to buy it and compliment him on his “gains”. Pathetic.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What do French people think of Alain Delon?
Answer: No nation is ever a monolith — so “French people” don’t have a collective, shared opinion about Alain Delon. He was a great actor who died on August 18, 2024. Yesterday as I write this. He was a complicated man. Ridiculously handsome in his prime, almost like an AI generated image with the prompt “handsome guy”. He was also a dog in his personal life. Of the “any hole is a goal, if it has a pulse I’m boning it” variety. Politically speaking he was far-right, having served his nation in Indochina and being good friends with Jean-Marie Le Pen, a notorious Holocaust denier. Delon had a son with German singer Nico. A son who looked entirely like him. And yet he denied paternity, refused to have anything to do with the kid and left him to his own devices… he died a few years back, aged sixty. Wheelchair bound, addicted to drugs, a mess of a man. Delon senior lived to be 88. I can’t tell you what “French people” thing of Alain Delon. But I can tell you what I, personally, think of the man. And I think he was an absolute bastard. A fine actor, a cultural icon and a legend of the silver screen. But, much like Gérard Depardieau, he was a complete goon of a man off-screen. None of this diminished his legendary status as an actor — I seperate the man from the art. A fine artist, a shitty man.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What would surprise the founding fathers if they were alive today?
Answer: I figure things would be the hardest for Thomas Jefferson, a notorious appreciator of ebony beauty and a slave owner. He’d be mesmerized by this thing called the internet, and by the television. Some day he’d watch a music video come on. It’s African American rapper Meghan Thee Stallion. “Why is this woman referred to as a stallion?” Jefferson would demand to know, “she is evidently not a male horse, and very much all woman!” He would then inquire whether or not he could purchase her. And ask one of his aides whether or not 300 dollars would be a “fair price”. They would inform him that slavery has been outlawed for about 150 years and that, no, he very much cannot purchase Meghan Thee Stallion. Thomas Jefferson would be enormously disappointed. Popular culture would confuse him, the names of artists would be bewildering and his inability to purchase ladies he desires would be a continuing source of regret.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What's your most controversial opinion about relationships?
Answer: Most relationships are awfully transactional in nature. The value in a person isn’t just in who they are, innately, but in what value the person represents. Youth matters. Looks matter. Sex appeal matters, as does charisma and the way one dresses. Social status matters to many people. And, yes, so does income… when I look for someone I look for several things. And it’s about what she can offer me, as much as it about who she is, as a person. I was left by my first wife in no small part because I failed to live up to the expectations I had set for myself. I had “oversold” myself. And I simply didn’t meet expectations. Because I wasn’t as driven as I said I was, I wasn’t as focused, and I grew lazy and complacent. Under the initial conditions, I was more than acceptable. But when conditions changed, I no longer was. And I was left in the dust. Flaws can be forgiven. And the worst of the worst sins overlooked. Swept under the rug. But the initial “terms of agreement” must not be broken. What screws us up is this expectation we have for one person to have EVERYTHING. Unending passion. Bottomless patience. Looks, fitness, wealth, drive and ambition. Tantalizing intellectual stimulation, great value entertainment, a sense of humor. We want someone who combines the qualities of a mistress/lover, a best friend and an honorable parent. And love is killed when we, inevitably, buckle under the pressure.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Between men and women, who love sex the most?
Answer: When I was younger, I used to think men like sex most… and as I got older, I learned the truth — we both like sex every bit as much. But I just kinda sucked at sex. With the years I gained more experience, and as I did I became a much more capable lover. I was a useless, selfish lover for most of my life. Then I kind of “saw the light”. The thing about sex is, you have to make love to a woman’s mind, first. You can’t just whip out your dick and go at it. You need to tease. You need to really make her want it. Because she wants it. Also if you’re a handsome man or a well-endowed man, your good physique and looks alone won’t do the trick. Maybe at first, kind of. But initial excitement wears off. And you have to keep her on her toes. Men who believe “women don’t like sex” are men who just haven’t “cracked the code” yet. A man who knows what he’s doing won’t be plagued with a wife who suffers mysterious headaches whenever the deed is about to commence. But clueless men will continue to think all women somehow suffer from lower libido.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How have you experienced or witnessed societal obsession with fair skin?
Answer: For years I lived in the Philippines and the national obsession seemed to be how fair one’s skin was. Skin whitening products were everywhere. Special soaps, special shampoos, all designed to keep the skin light as possible or lighten it further. Women and young girls would wear little umbrellas on sunny days wherever they went out to keep their skins light. It didn’t help, of course, that 90% of all the models, actors and actresses were mixed race — they virtually all had at least one white parent or grandparent. Others may have a particularly light-skinned father from the Arab world. But few were “pure Filipino”. Aside from white skin, European features were seen as perfect. A “tall nose” as opposed to a “flat nose”. Large, expressive eyes, as opposed to small beady eyes. Some naturally had a lighter skin and more European features even without having a foreign parent or grandparent; but it is fairly rare. The legacy of colonialism comes into play as well, with quite a few Filipinos having Spanish, Chinese or American ancestors. Above all else, light skin was the number one obsession. It trumped everything. There was one girl in our neighborhood who had a plain face, but very fair skin. She was considered far more attractive than her sister, whose face was gorgeous but noticeably darker. When I had a son with a Filipina mestiza in 2023 he came out pale with blonde hair, green eyes, a pointed nose — the whole hospital freaked out and obsessed over him. Random strangers still obsess over him.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some life hacks that we can use in our daily life?
Answer: Read a rather fascinating article about a 93-year-old Irish man named Richard Morgan. He is an excellent rower, a world champion in the older-age competitions. And he was recently given an extensive medical examination, wherein he was found to have the lungs, heart and muscle tone of a man in his 40s.[1] Now the coolest thing about Mr. Morgan is that he used to be a baker and that he wasn’t athletic at all until his retirement. And that he didn’t pick up rowing until he was already 70. But when he did, he started going at it rather intensely. Today, even at 93, he still works out for about 40 minutes a day on average on rowing machines. He does weight training thrice a week, too. He eats and drinks a normal diet, although he does consume more protein than is recommended for a man his age. Richard Morgan could have decided, at 70, to simply do whatever the hell he wanted. Health be damned, fitness be damned. He may have had a jolly good time, but he’d have very likely be done. And had he been around, he wouldn’t be in anywhere near as fabulous a shape today as he is now. Life hack number one — get off your ass, and work yourself into a sweat for about an hour every day. What is one hour out of 24 hours in a day?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What was the reason for children in the Victorian era appearing younger than their actual age?
Answer: They were small. Malnourished. A small body doesn’t grow properly. I’ve seen it with older people who grew up starving. They didn’t grow “right”. My grandfather was an orphaned toddler, raised in foster families and orphanages. He received more beatings than nutrition. And I’ll never forget him sitting at the table with my father, his son-in-law. While seated, my grandfather looked like a towering giant. In fact his head and shoulders were above those of my father, who stood 6′3″. But once he stood up, my grandfather was a mere 5′9″. Because while his upper body was enormous. A massive ribcage. Long arms. Hands that looked like they could uproot trees without tools, wrists thicker than a normal man’s ankles. Yet his legs were almost comically short. He was built like a Bassett Hound — little legs, huge body. The way my mother explained it to us kids, grandpa was supposed to be a tall man. But he never got the right food. So he never “grew right”. Victorian England was just like this. The little chimney sweepers ate dust and cigarettes for breakfast. By twenty they had the body of a dwarf and the wisened old faces of an elderly man who’s seen some shit. Until fairly recently, kids would pick up smoking at ten, drinking hard liquor by twelve. They were worked to the bones, like slaves. Whipped and beaten up on a whim. Sometimes killed crippled by workplace accidents before they even reached twenty. By their late teens they had kids, by their forties grandchildren. They were lucky to see sixty… and their bodies didn’t grow the way they should. They were malformed, malnourished.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is there any women who arent Fake on here?
Answer: Several have come to me. They came to me because I didn’t care. I didn’t care whether they would come or go. One fell madly in love with me. And twice blocked me, followed me back, unfollowed me, blocked me again. That’s something you need to understand about life, about attraction, about love, and lust — the most powerful man is the man who doesn’t give a shit. The trick is simple enough — you do not let anyone hold power over you. It’s easier said than done. Matters of the heart are hard. Our hearts get heavy. But the most powerful man is the man who isn’t hungry or thirsty. He’s self-sustained. He realizes friends come and go. Women come and go. Lovers are won, and lost. And lust cannot sustain itself forever. Are any women online not fake? My friend, they are ALL fake. So are all men. We’re fake creatures. We all fake it until we make it. But we don’t make it. Yet we keep faking anyway. Go through life with the assumption that more likely than not, those we encounter are “fake” one way or another. Be stoic. Read Marcus Aurelius. Drink a lot of water, read good books, exercise. Steel your body and steel your soul. And guard your heart well. Don’t lose your head, until you meet The One. She’s that special girl you would freely give your head to, and open your veins for. You’ll know it when you meet her.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you name some of the most misunderstood or overlooked heroes in history and explain why they are often overlooked?
Answer: Not all “heroes” are necessarily heroic… but they are men, conflicted men, who play their part to move the story along. Marcus Junius Brutus was such a man. The story of Jesus needed Judas to betray him. Likewise, Julius Caesar needed Brutus. Brutus loved Caesar. Was loyal to him, but conflicted throughout it all. He took up arms against a man who was like a father to him — and may even have been his son, as Caesar had carried on an affair with Brutus’ mother for decades. So when Brutus sided with Pompey, he was forgiven. Whatever he did, he always was forgiven. And Brutus tried to see the good in Caesar but saw him gaining more and more power. And it concerned him gravely. So he once more plotted against a man he loved, in order to preserve the institutions he loved more. Marcus Junius Brutus betrayed his friend, his father figure and possible father, because he feared he would rule as a King. He then was hunted like a dog for the rest of his life, lost a battle decisively and took his own life, as Judas had done after betraying Jesus. But history needs its Brutuses and Judases much as it needs its Jesuses and Caesars… to go against one you love requires more bravery than to go against one you hate.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why are politicians always dishonest?
Answer: Politicians nowadays and for about as long as I can remember, are all about “the spin”. It isn’t about good proposals versus bad proposals… it’s all about “how can we spin this story to our advantage?” Just look at some headlines about the same exact proposals, as proposed by different sides of the political spectrum. You notice very quickly the dishonesty. And it isn’t even necessarily the politicians themselves, half the time — it’s the media. Who are owned by people with certain interests. Who want to portray their candidate positively, and all others negatively. Politics isn’t about right or wrong. Isn’t about good versus evil. No, it’s far more cynical than that… it is a bleak, depressing game of divide and conquer. Grown men and women acting like high school bullies. And sometimes one side will steal from the other side and pretend the idea was theirs all along. People buy it, too — because everyone is just in their own echo chambers. Surrounded by like-minded people where only one ‘official narrative’ is allowed and to speak otherwise makes one a “heathen”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What really really really scares you the most?
Answer: Being on my deathbed and realizing I have wasted the one life I’ll ever be given. Some of us are fortunate enough to reach old age feeling like legends, looking back on amazing memories… I have some of those, too. But far too few. Need to step up my game massively. You want to be able to say, at the end of the ride, that you squeezed every drop out of life. That it was a good ride. A worthwhile ride. My grandfather told me at 75 that he was “done”. He meant it, too. I sometimes think about the ending of Legends of the Fall. The great hunter has done all he could, all he must. And dies facing an enormous bear. He dies bravely, after a life well-lived. If I died today, what will I have left behind, in terms of a legacy? Some friendships. Some love affairs. Fleeting, hedonistic memories. A bunch of kids by different mothers. A Quora profile with a lot of answers about everything and nothing. But no great bravery, no great inspiration, no lasting legacy. Truth be told, I could die tomorrow and simply… disappear. You wouldn’t get another answer. I’d never publish the book I always say I want to publish. My children would miss me, my girlfriend would miss me and my relatives and friends. But life would go on. And none of them would look back at me as a legend — just another piece of drunken driftwood.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the chances of witnessing a historical event?
Answer: For most of us, they’re incredibly small. You basically have to either be a person of consequence, or have strong connections to people of consequence. Robert Todd Lincoln was both — his father was been President Abraham Lincoln. And he, himself, went on to serve as Secretary of State. While Mr. Lincoln wasn’t present when his father was assassinated — he had declined to go to the theater as he was tired that night, he had been close when it happened. Some twenty years later he was present when President James A. Garfield was killed by a deranged gunman. And when President McKinley was killed, he was present, too. After this, Robert Todd Lincoln refused all invitations to presidential inaugurations or events, saying: "No, I'm not going, and they'd better not ask me, because there is a certain fatality about presidential functions when I am present." If you’re just a random person, you’re not likely to Forrest Gump your way through history and be randomly present at various historical events. But when you’re a political figure, a presidential son or bodyguard, your chances of witnessing multiple historical events increases exponentially.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which is the most emotional scene?
Answer: I cannot share this one without some spoilers, so be warned… It’s about HBO’s excellent two-season epic, Rome. It’s a scene involving one of the main characters, Roman legionary Titus Pullo. Played by the wonderful late Ray Stevenson. He’s condemned to die in the area at the hands of gladiators. Given a small sword, Pullo is expected to at least put on a little bit of a fight. Give the audience a show. He doesn’t want to — he’s depressed and simply wants to die. Wants them to get it over with. So the gladiators begin to taunt him. They get no response until one of them mentions his legion, the thirteenth. He’s extemely attached to his legion. He loses it. And takes the gladiators completely by surprise. He fights like hell, and actually manages to fight off and kill many of the warriors. He is also stabbed and slashed repeatedly in the process, however. Pullo’s best friend, Lucius Vorenus, is watching from the background. And as Pullo gets wounded and more weakened by the fight, Vorenus gets noticeably upset. He’s a stoic man. A brutal man. A man who rarely, if ever, shows emotion and now he’s losing it… because he’s watching his only friend getting killed in the area. Finally, Vorenus has had enough. He just breaks. He cannot watch his friend being killed… when a particularly large gladiator steps into the arena to finish off a badly injured Pullo, Vorenus enters as well… he takes on the gladiator, a very tall man. Vorenus defeats the large gladiator. Kills him. And then walks his best friend out of the arena. The audience now cheers on both men, having been won over by their bravery and the display of brotherhood. It’s an amazing scene. One of the best I’ve ever seen, from what is easily my favorite show of all times. Just the fight. The epic, unevenly matched fight. A man watching his best friend getting killed before his very eyes… and stepping in to save him, despite the fact that he isn’t supposed to — Vorenus is a man of duty throughout the show. A man who does what he’s told. Doesn’t rock the boat, doesn’t intervene. I’ve recently started a rewatch of Rome again. It’s been ten years since I last saw it and my God, does it hold up well! It’s still every bit as funny, witty and well-acted as the first time I saw it. It doesn’t give its characters the morality of modern-day people, and takes its audience seriously by portraying them as real Romans — with all the bigotry, sexism and brutality of ancient Rome. But it shows, too, the bravery. The brotherhood of men who fought and bled together. The treachery of politics. Shit, I’ll go and watch another episode right now.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How would you describe your sense of humor?
Answer: It’s pretty dumb. Nothing fancy. Dumb memes. Dumb films — think American Pie films. Scary Movie, White Chicks. The first Borat film, before Sascha Baron Cohen became all “political” and preachy about his stuff. For that matter, all his early stuff is pretty hilarious. Loved Ali G, even The Dictator. Sometimes I’ll be a bit cynical, in my sense of humor. Other times, I’ll be dry. It is kind of all over the place. I like things a little dark and twisted, from time to time. To spice up the dish a little. Because only dumb shit alone won’t always cut it. Though most of the time, it does. I don’t know what it is that makes this type of meme so funny to me. Perhaps it’s the fact that I’ve been a father for a while. “Dad jokes” are a part of me, at this point. Seeped into the very fabric of my being. So what if it’s a little corny… I love it. I would describe my sense of humor as, for the most part, pretty simple. Not very complex or sophisticated. When it comes to jokes, I’m a man of simple tastes. And I don’t like my humor to be preachy, or overly intellectual.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How don't people find aging scary?
Answer: Just looked at a collage of pictures from the oldest person in recorded history, Jeanne Louise Calment. She lived to be 122. The photos show her between the ages of 111 and 122. Now she kept her good spirits about her, evidently. This lady who was born when Billy the Kid still roamed around the Wild West and lived long enough for Justin Bieber to be born. But there’s one terribly sad part of living from 1875 until 1997 — you have zero guarantee that your loved ones will live as long as you do. Calment’s husband died. Her daughter died. Even her only grandson died before her. Even when she was 90, she still had 32 years ahead of her. And she didn’t know, of course. But by the time she would die, no one she grew up with would still be alive. Not one person she could share those memories with. Hell, her father had a little art supply store when she was a kid, and once a “dirty old drunk” came in. It was Vincent van Gogh. Didn’t mean anything to her. And it’s cool, on some level… living to extreme old age, that is. But you have to be made of some stern stuff to handle it. It reminds me of the 108-year-old guy from The Green Mile who lost everyone…” Time takes it all, whether you want it to or not. Time takes it all, time bears it away, and in the end there is only darkness.” Few things are as scary as aging, aside from the alternative of never getting there. But to get there, you’ll have to watch everyone else go.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the worst example of unfair treatment in history?
Answer: There are too many to count — I won’t even “go there” because there have been more genocides in our species sordid history than I have fingers on my hands and toes on my feet. One horribly unfair tale is that of the Chinese Indonesians. Below, we see President John F. Kennedy with Indonesian president Sukarno. Following a failed coup attempt by Indonesian communists, Indonesia went after communist insurgents and sympathizers in a major way. Which is cool — you don’t want to have a bunch of commies causing trouble, right? But the problem is, very few Chinese Indonesians were actually part of these communist parties. Indonesian Chinese folks were largely traders, peaceful and entirely apolitical. But because of Red China meddling in the affairs of many of its neighbors, ALL citizens of Indonesia with Chinese heritage were targetted. Some were dragged out of their houses, sometimes thousands at a time. Shopkeepers were beaten to death in front of their families, their shops burned and their wares stolen… Throughout the 1960s, there were anti-Chinese pogroms in Indonesia. Largely because of jealousy — much like the Jews in the West, the Chinese diaspora in Asia was hard-working and thrifty, often saving up a solid fortune, and sending their kids to good schools. And people just couldn’t deal with that… they hated them for their success. The picture above shows anti-Chinese riots in Jakarta in 1998. Again, Chinese businesses were targetted, people dragged out of their houses, their families and workers brutalized, their shops looted… People have a nasty habit of hating those who do well. Those who excel in whatever field they have chosen. And yes, they will punish you for your success, whenever they can. There’s few things in this world as nasty and bigoted as a riotous, bloodthirsty crowd of people unhappy with their own lives…

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is there a long history of women being targeted in India?
Answer: If we strictly look at statistics for a moment and forget about fearmongering and sensationalism for just a minute… we find that there are several countries with a higher percentage of rapes and sexual assaults per percentage of population than India.[1] We find, for instance, that 27% of Chinese women who are married or in a relationship have experienced physical or sexual violence.[2] There’s this knee-jerk response in much of the world — they think of India, and they immediately think of a nation of perverts that defecate in the streets. It’s a grossly racist depiction, and it doesn’t hold up in terms of statistics. Because sure enough, Indian women are victimized on a daily basis. They are raped, assaulted, injured and have their honor besmirched by nasty creatures… but the same happens to women everywhere else, the world over. Even prosperous Sweden has a Sweden has 63.50 rape rate and around 5,960 incidents in per 100,000 citizens, to name another example… but Swedes aren’t stereotyped as a nation of rapists, last I checked. Nor are Chinese, or Jamaicans, or Americans. And yet in all these nations, sexual violence is rampant. Truth be told — India does not have a “special history” of women being targetted. Not anymore than other countries. India is both a huge country with 1.4 billion inhabitants, and a country that hasn’t outlawed protests. So when a high profile rape case happens in India, tens of thousands of angry women take to the streets. In China the same rape could happen but the protest would never take place or spread, because the state wouldn’t allow it. And in the West, all you’ll see is some performative celebrity outrage, but no tangible policy changes.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the most interesting “what if” scenario in history (the alteration doesn’t have to be for the better, just interesting)?
Answer: A fascinating thing to ponder in terms of what-if scenarios… what if the Africans had found America first, before Columbus? And before you go to me and say: “No way, Jean-Marie, that is WAY too far-fetched…” Think again. Because an African King around the year 1300 did exactly that.[1] Launched a massive fleet and decided to cross the Atlantic. In other words, that whole “Wakanda Forever” meme of the Black Panther world being real, of some sort of super technologically advanced African nation being around today? It could have happened. All it takes in life is one dreamer. One person who dares to venture out into the unknown and gets there. Christopher Columbus got where he got, in no small part due to having better ships at his disposal. Another element is that of luck — he wasn’t even looking for America, yet he stumbled onto it. History is full of stories like this… whoever gets somewhere first, gets the prize. Winner takes it all. One bad storm, one moment of supremely bad luck, or supremely good fortune, can make or break a man, a nation, and a people. Fortune favors the bold, but many bold men died because Lady Luck turned her face from them at the very last moment… And what fascinates me is this what-if scenario… a version of history in which the King of Mali, and not Columbus, had discovered the New World. You’d now live in a world completely different from the one we live in. One in which subsequent rulers of Mali, like Mansa Musa, would have perhaps entered some alliance with the Arabs and colonized the Americas. And the internet would be full of poor whites and asians writing angry thought pieces about “dark privilege” and Africa would be the wealthiest continent.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How did learning history change the way you think?
Answer: As a teenager I was rather racist. And while I loved history, I didn’t really dive into it deeply enough to not be stuck on some weird notions. I used to feel, for instance, that it was the European race to which I belong that first travelled the seven seas, exploring the Atlantic and crossing it to America. I didn’t know yet of Mansa Musa’s predecessor. An African King who literally dropped everything he was doing to cross the Atlantic and discover America.[1] Mansa Musa himself, of course, became enormously famous. He was fabulously wealthy and a legendary ruler of the Mali Empire. But the man before him wasn’t interested in ruling… he had an adventurous spirit. Kind of like Richard the Lionheart who didn’t give two shits about ruling and just wanted to fight in the Crusades and be a warrior-king. This fellow, instead, wanted to be an explorer-king. He reportedly launched a fleet of a thousand ships and simply… disappeared off the face of the earth. The great Mansa Musa, himself, wasn’t impressed — he felt his predecessor had “forsaken his duties to his country”, his expedition being unwise and impulsive and a rather selfish endeavour. Only a single ship reportedly returned, the rest sunk or stranded in the Americas. Did the African expedition really reach America, and get stranded there? Did they mingle with local population, did some of them take local wives and live out their days among strangers, eventually becoming part of their civilization? What strikes me is some statues discovered in Mexico have distinctly African features… it seems that what Christopher Columbus did, the Vikings and Africans did, too — they just didn’t come back to tell the tale.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can trust ever really be fully restored after being broken?
Answer: A sweet girl once gave me her heart. I was 20 and she was 18. I was immature, in many ways. And I was selfish… I had a mentality of “any hole is a goal” and I wasn’t faithful. And yes, that broke her trust. I never fell in love with someone else, never planned to leave her. But yes. I didn’t keep it in my pants, either. On several occasions. And that broke the trust. And guess what? Trust lost, is trust lost. Forever. It won’t come back. Never fully. When someone gives you their heart, it’s a beautiful thing. A wonderful, powerful thing. It’s a great gift. A great responsibility. And you cannot be careless with it. You start out with trust, with respect, with mutual admiration. And with just one decision you can shatter it. Shatter it to a point where there’s no coming back. I learned this the hard way. Because younger me was an irresponsible asshole. People may say “trust can be restored”… and maybe it can. But never fully. Never completely. Trust is fragile, far more fragile than most of us can imagine. It’s like a little tree that’s easily trampled. And it won’t grow back. It’ll never be a great towering oak — it’ll just be a little dead stump. Even if you cover it up with flowers, and make it look good… it will be dead.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How can an absent father affect a child?
Answer: An absent father can either inspire greatness in an individual, or cripple a person for life. It all depends on whether or not a child has other positive male role models growing up. The photo below is the only known photograph of Barack Obama and his father, Barack Senior, taken in 1971. Barack Senior was a “rolling stone” — wherever he hung his hat, was his home. He had a lot of wives, and a lot of children by those wives. And he simply wasn’t around as a father, let alone as a father figure. As a result, Barack Junior had to look elsewhere for positive male role models. He found them in his maternal grandfather, and in the Indonesian stepfather his mother later provided him with as she remarried. These men stepped up and were there for him when his father wasn’t there. Children who grow up without a father, will look for guidance elsewhere. If there are good men in their lives, they’ll turn out alright. But if, in their desperation to replace the father they never had, they encounter a bad seed… things tend to go South. When Dad isn’t there, a little boy acts like a duck — whoever he sees first and sticks around for the ride, is now “Dad”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What effects do you think the current refugee crisis inside Russia will have on the war and Russia internally?
Answer: When about 200,000 Russian citizens have to flee their homes because Ukraine took over a large chunk of Russian lands, this puts the Russian government in a tough position. Have a look at the map, to visualize it — just look how close Ukrainian forces are to Moscow right now. Most of Russia’s armed forces are currently engaged in Ukraine. There are some troops defending important borders elsewhere, and some who defend Moscow. And very little else is left. So Putin can either get troops from Ukraine, weakening defensive lines there, or he can send in young, inexperienced recruits from inside Russia and lose them to the experienced Ukrainian troops already entranched in Kursk. But whatever he does, or doesn’t do, he loses. Loses prestige, ‘face’, reputation… the Kremlin never looked more impotent in recent years. When hundreds of thousands of citizens are evacuated, they have to be housed elsewhere in Russia. The Moscow region is awfully close and some of the refugees will come there. Some have family in other parts of Russia. Stories will spread — and fast. Stories of incompetent border guards, overrun, overwhelmed, surrendering in droves. And with NATO missiles at their disposal, Moscow itself is now in range.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are today's challenges for young people worse than they've ever been?
Answer: Young people alive today grew up watching amazing fiction… one of the best things I ever watched as a teenagers was the Lord of the Rings trilogy. It’s quite nice, seeing Mordor on screen… a hundred years ago, Mordor was real. J.R.R. Tolkien served in the trenches of WWI. In no-man’s land, between the trenches, he watched as his friends were blown to pieces. Bodies dropped too far away from safety would be left behind between your trench and that of the enemy. Soon, a sea of rotting corpses melted into one another. A goo of comrades and enemies alike. You’d go to war with boys from your own town and community, friends you’d have grown up with. And watch many of them die. Some instantaneously, others gruesomely slow, of infections and preventable diseases… The trenches of WWI became the land of Tolkien’s barbarous Orcs, Mordor. Tolkien wrote from what he knew. And the world he knew is nothing like anything we see today. Not for most of us, fortunate souls, anyway. That doesn’t mean life today is a walk in the park for young people — it isn’t, for many of us. But for most of us, being sent to literal Mordor isn’t written on our bingo cards. The world is still FAR from fair and perfect and reasonable. And life is challenging. But to think for even a moment that young people today have it worse than young people in history, is absurd.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who is the most fake celebrity that everyone likes?
Answer: An interesting example would be John Lennon. He was a social activist, involved in left-wing causes and sympathetic to Marxist and Trotskyist groups… the FBI even investigated him for this in the 1960s — they decided that he would be “ineffective as a revolutionary” because he “is constantly under the influence of narcotics”. That FBI assessment about sums it up — John Lennon was all talk, no game, as far as activism goes. The picture that best shows it is him and his wife Yoko Ono, doing their famous “we’re staying in this bedroom until there’s world peace” shtick. A maid comes in and fluffs Lennon’s pillows for him. He casually stands aside, taking a little break from his activism-cum-performance-art so the maid can tidy up the room a little… then he goes right back, imagining there’s no money. But there is money. And Lennon was a wifebeater, a violent man and a selfish drug addict who just happened to be gifted with a great voice and the ability to sing moving songs. He was a great artist. But he was a fraud, too. All his stances, all his opinion, all his public statements, were an act. A performance, just like his concerts.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was Septimius Severus a black African?
Answer: A lot of people have claimed Emperor Septimus Severus was a “black African”. In actuality, he was of Italian and Punic (North-African) heritage. Which means he likely was of a more North-African appearance and hue. Oh, and there is one anecdote about Severus involving race. And it’s… hilariously racist. Once, on campaign, Septimus Severus encountered a very dark-skinned African man. The Emperor complained that the man was “too dark” and that his black skin color was “ominous”. He considered the man’s presence a bad omen, and sent him away. It’s just weirdly funny to me: “Get this dude away, he’s too black, he’s bad luck!” The bust above, for the record, is Septimus Severus’ son and heir, Caracella. He appears to have a pretty North-African, Arabic phenotype. Although to be honest, I have seen some light-skinned Ethiopians over the years who have somewhat similar facial features. We can’t really be sure what the ethnic background of historical people was. Not without mummified remains we can DNA test, anyway… Still, Septimus Severus’ response to a dark-skinned, as per the Historia Augustus, leads me to suspect he wasn’t a “black African” himself. Because the biographers and historians of his era certainly would have made mention of it. Not to mention that, had he been a dark-skinned man, the Emperor would have considered his own presence “bad luck” which seems far-fetched.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some examples of events that could be considered "witnessing history"?
Answer: A large number of young Russian recruits surrendering in the Kursk region of Russia during Ukraine’s invasion of Kursk. They’re young men from the Moscow area — the type of young lads that Putin couldn’t send to Ukraine because their families are reasonably well-off. Young ethnic minorities like Tatars are sent in their place to die in the trenches. The well-off families still have to deal with mandatory service, of course — if only just to keep up appearances. But there was an unspoken understanding that the “Moscow boys” would do the easier tasks… the less dangerous ones. Like protecting the Russian-Ukrainian border. I mean, who on earth would ever be crazy enough to invade Russia? No one had done so since the 1940s and the German expedition had famously ended rather badly for them… It was unthinkable. And then, Ukraine did make the move. Took up to 70 Russian settlements, captured over a 1000 square kilometers of Russian land and sent 200,000 Russian citizens fleeing. And it took thousands of young, relatively well-off Russian recruits prisoner. For the first time ever, the privileged elites of Moscow are hit personally by the war.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What does beauty mean to you beyond the surface?
Answer: Someone physically unattractive can have a beautiful soul. We all age, and we lose our looks and our strength as we do. But some old people have this thing, this special thing. A twinkle in the eye. A certain warmth in their voices. You meet them and you’d have no clue what they did, what accomplishments they have under their belt, as you see them stand in line at a store. Take for example the old man below. His name was Norman Borlaug. And he was a beautiful soul. Mr. Borlaug was an American scientist behind enormous increases in agricultural productivity — the so-called “Green Revolution”. It is estimated that because of Mr. Borlaug’s research and his ability to help farmers maximize their output, he saved over a billion human beings from death by starvation. Just imagine that number for a moment — a billion. That’s more people than reside in all of Europe. Almost as many as there are in all of India, China or the entire continent of Africa. Norman Borlaug was just one old man. No one would have turned his head and looked at him as he walked down the street — he wasn’t an ‘influencer’ or a Hollywood hunk. And yet he was a far more beautiful soul than any human being that ever graced the silver screen. You just need to go beyond the surface.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do you think that a racially homogeneous country is better than a racially diverse one?
Answer: I don’t. Objectively speaking, if we look at racially homogenous countries, they’re not some sort of Utopia just because everyone happens to look alike. Japan is a relatively racially homogenous country. So is China. So is Taiwan, and so are South and North Korea both. And all of these countries I just mentioned have issues, suffer from devastatingly low birth rates and would rather die out together than “mix” their precious races. Is this a virtue? I don’t think it is. I have several mixed race children myself. And my current girlfriend is a lady from another race as well. So my all descendants are absolutely not “racially homogenous”… but they are prolific. There are a lot of little Mini-Me’s out there. And several more of them planned to soon make their appearance. I’d much rather live in an ethnically diverse country with a healthy birth rate than in a country that is “racially pure” but slowly dying out. I also love diverse people — and diverse cuisines! — and if I can find all that without having to leave my own town or city, what’s not to love? I’m pretty sure the future of us all is diverse, whether we like it or not.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How can an unattractive man attract women, realistically?
Answer: The man on the photograph below has twelve children by four different women. All of his girlfriends and wives have been exceptionally beautiful, some were actresses, others were models, one is a famous singer and the latest is an executive lady with strikingly blue eyes that could pierce a man’s soul. Yes, he looks like the propped up corpse of a sun-bleached walrus. But he’s a billionaire, many times over. One of the world’s richest men — perhaps the richest, I don’t keep track and the top three of richest people keeps changing constantly. That’s all it takes. Money. Wealth. Influence. You can attract women by being a total stud, which takes effort. Or you can attract them by being amazingly charming and having wonderful social skills. Which, again, takes effort. Or you could just try being filthy rich. Just, try it. Give it a go. Be filthy rich for a moment. It’ll do wonders. You just have to visualize it. Close your eyes and repeat the mantra: “I’m rich. I’m rich. I’m rich.” It’ll come to you. Jump out of a mirror like Beatlejuice.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why was Tim Walz's tampon bill controversial?
Answer: The bill Minnesota governor Tim Walz proposed stipulated all schools in the state to keep a stock of tampons for female students who would have their periods. He felt feminine products should be freely available, the way toilet paper is. This seems like a pretty sensible and perfectly reasonable stance to take. Now here’s where it gets weird, to use one of the favorite words of Mr. Walz — schools were required to keep tampons not only in female bathrooms (which would have been perfectly reasonable) but in the boys bathrooms as well. Of course boys don’t menstruate. Unless maybe it’s a transgender (girk-to-boy) pupil. Of which there are very, very few. Like, my own daughters go to a fairly large school. Haven’t seen a single “trans kid”. So yeah that’s a bit odd. Still? It’s one of those stories where the issue being decried is what I would call a “victimless crime”. Is anyone actually hurt by the presence of tampons in school bathrooms? I doubt it. Is it a little strange to place them in boys bathrooms? Yes. But “a little strange” isn’t the same as “harmful”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some of the current beliefs held by former US presidents?
Answer: One interesting post-presidential career has been that of Jimmy Carter. He wrote and published a book in 2008, called Palestine: Peace Not Apartheid. Carter considers Israel an “Apartheid state” similar to South Africa in the 20th century — one in which different groups have different rights and aren’t allowed in certain areas of their own country.[1] Every US president to date has been fiercely pro-Israel. Some have been critical of individual Israeli leaders (Netanyahu in particular) but all US presidents have been major supporters of Israel. Jimmy Carter stands alone in this. He’s the only former US president who is critical of Israel to such an enormous degree. Certainly none are as outspoken, or have written books about it. It’s kind of fascinating. Of course, detractors have labeled Carter an “antisemite” for his views and for the book he’s penned, for his pro-Palestine activism… Of all living former Presidents, Jimmy Carter is the most outspoken and the most daring — for better or worse. You may agree with the man. Or disagree with him strongly. But he’s got some balls, as a lot of what he says is political and social suicide for any public figure in America.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some good examples of "life isn't fair"?
Answer: In the year 1958, the last surviving Confederate veteran of the American Civil War lay dying. Walter Williams was about 116 years old at the time. Country singer Johnny Horton came and visited the elderly man, lying in a room full of wartime mementos his blind eyes could no longer see. Horton sang to Williams his song, “Johnny Reb”, which he had recorded in honor of the veterans of the Confederates. The word “Reb” refers to rebels, as the Confederate soldiers rebelled against their country. Aged 33, Horton was a healthy man and in the prime of his life, a married father and a hard-working recording artist, traveling across the land, performing and recording songs… In 1959, Walter Williams died. The last of the Confederate ‘rebels’. And Johnny Horton, himself, died just a year later, in 1960 — a car crash took his life, aged only 35. Not the ending Mr. Horton could have ever envisioned for himself when he sang a song to a 116-year-old veteran.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do we really want a woman president in the United States?
Answer: I haven’t heard of a lot of Americans wanting a woman president, for the sake of her being a woman. I mean that’s a ridiculous concept. I mostly just hear people repeat the same line, over and over again: “I just want someone who isn’t old as hell.” Former presidential hopeful Nikki Haley said it best: “The first party to replace its 80-year-old candidate wins…” She said this back in early 2024 when she was running against Trump and others to become the Republican candidate. Haley, of course, didn’t make it. But her words still ring true. The other guys did replace their elderly candidate… and saw an immediate surge in energy and popularity as a result. It could have been Nikki Haley. Now it may be Kamala Haris. What these two ladies have in common isn’t their gender — who cares, really? — but their age. They’re relatively young. They have energy. Now, Kamala has momentum, too. And on November 4 the world will know, if the US really wants a “woman president”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What changes one's perspective?
Answer: Personal experiences change one’s perspective. You have to feel it. Really feel it. Take for example Brittney Griner, an American basketball star. She used to “take a knee” and refuse to stand for the American national anthem when it would play during sports performances in the past. Then she spent time in a Russian prison before being returned home to America in a prisoner exchange… and whatever she experienced in Russian captivity changed Griner. Altered her perspectives forever. The national anthem of her country used to remind her of racism, of the historical oppression of her ancestors and people. She was angry, and refused to stand for it. In taking the knee, she showed her defiance to the world. But that same country she used to dislike saved Griner. Brought her back from a brutal Russian prison colony. And in a lot of ways, it humbled her. Suddenly she associates good things with the anthem she didn’t used to associate with it… in fact she owes her life and her freedom to the institutions she used to criticise. So when her anthem played, she stood proudly, with tears in her eyes.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is it unusual for women to riot?
Answer: It depends entirely on where you live. For example here in Europe where I live, I rarely hear of women rioting. But in India I know from time to time gangs of women get together and attack a convicted rapist in unison. Sometimes they whip the man or even castrate him. In some cases, rapists have even been killed by a mob of women. The reasoning behind such mob attacks is that the rapist keeps getting away with his behavior, or merely gets a slap on the wrist. So sometimes ladies band together and take justice into their own hands. On the other hand, there are also cases of false rape accusations destroying the lives of former husbands or partners — the Indian courts have become rather anti-men in recent years to ‘over-correct’ the previous gender bias against women. Still, sometimes a guilty man walks free. And the powerless are often awfully powerful when in large groups. One woman, alone, can’t harm a man. But with dozens or even hundreds of her sisters by her side, she can rip any man to shreds as easily as a tiger would a mouse.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you share some of your favorite unsolved mysteries or conspiracy theories that you believe in?
Answer: One of my favorite theories involves Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and former Cuban dictator Fidel Castro. Here we see Mrs. Trudeau, Justin’s mother, with Fidel Castro and Justin’s younger brother. Mrs. Trudeau went to Cuba several times in the 1960s, includin around the time her future Prime Minister son would have been conceived… Now we can do a little side-by-side view of Justin Trudeau and Fidel Castro, for good measure. The noses, the jawlines and bushy eyebrows are almost entirely identical. Both men are tall and lanky, have the same height, the same build. Pierre Trudeau, Justin Trudea’s legal father, was considerably older than his wife. He was nearly sixty when Justin was born. Is it a far-fetched theory to believe that a much younger wife might have had a little dalliance with a handsome and still fairly young Cuban dictator? Fidel Castro reportedly slept with thousands of women, for the record. The guy was a major stud in his prime. Sleeping with the young wife of a Western head of state would have been a lovely treat for Fidel. The Trudeau family, of course, denies all relation. But I’d love to see a DNA test, myself…

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some reasons that teenagers decide to be trans?
Answer: That’s not really how it works. And this isn’t coming from some sort of pro-trans activist, as anyone who has read my Quora can attest to… Being trans is fucking brutal. Imagine being born as a boy. And hating your own body so much you want to die. You want to chop off your balls. And have your dick fashioned into a makeshift vagina by plastic surgeons. You want to go on puberty blockers and hormone replacement therapy that leaves you permanently infertile, short and with brittle bones for the rest of your life. And no, there is no going back, either… Look, I’m a man. And there is very little I love more in this world than waking up, having a shower and admiring that big beautiful pair of bouncy testicles dangling around between my legs. Or making my mighty penis swing around like helicopter blades. God, I love my junk! Love it to bits. Me and my junks, we go way back. We’ve had some crazy adventures together… so as someone who LOVES his body. Loves it to bits. And is intensely motivated to keep it ‘intact’… I try to put myself into the shoes of someone who is wired exactly opposite to myself. Someone who hates his (or her!) genitals as much as I love mine. Who detests his or her gender as much as I am fond of mine. Who wants to chop off what I’d rather commit bloody murder for just to maintain… someone crippled by dysphoria. Who on earth would EVER “choose” to be that way? No, man. Being transgender isn’t a choice. And if it is, that’s an incredibly demented choice to make. So I try to be compassionate. And yes, I fail. But I try.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do you think overweight people are attractive?
Answer: Some people are beautiful in spite of being overweight, but I’ve never known anyone who was attractive because of it. Still — I try not to be too harsh on people.
