We all have our struggles and I, myself, have a habit of overeating when I am depressed. The way some people starve themselves when sad or overworked, others among us cope with the struggles of life by eating more than we should. The thing that always gets me when it comes to overweight people — inside any unattractive obese person, there’s a potentially very attractive fit person hiding. Strip away the double chins and you’ll find jawlines well-hidden. Remove the chubby cheeks and find cheekbones to die for. Remove the love handles and find a waspish waist. Strip away excess lard in any area of the body and lovely curves find their way to the surface… it’s true for men, it’s true for women, it works for everyone. I’ve never known an obese person who lost some weight, started eating less and more healthy food and didn’t become more attractive as a result. That doesn’t mean there aren’t any heavier folks who still have pretty or handsome faces — but this is a rarity. Nine out of ten times, fat is the cruel centuries of neglect that turns great castles into haunted ruins.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some examples of 'mind over matter'?
Answer: In February 2023, Jimmy Carter entered hospice care. He did so with his wife, Rosalynn Carter, by his side. Unbeknownst to the world at the time, Rosalynn had been diagnosed with dementia. Carter, although dying at the time, vowed to stay alive at least until after Rosalynn would pass, so she would not have to suffer the pain of losing her husband after 77 years of marriage when in such a fragile mental state… And against all odds, he did indeed survive her. As much as it broke his spirits, he stuck around for her sake. He then continued following the news — Carter is very involved in international politics and the war in Gaza haunted him. He wanted to see it come to an end. And then just recently, he found another reason to stick around… he wants to live until November. Because he wants to vote in the election. He wants to vote for his party’s candidate, Harris.[1] So he’ll stick around for that, too. Which means that although he entered hospice care in early 2023 at age 98, he may just make it to his 100th birthday on October 1, 2024. He’ll have to, if he wants to vote in November. President Jimmy Carter is a fine example of “mind over matter” — his powerful mind, stuck in a frail and failing body, keeps finding another goal to reach. And somehow, by some force of near-otherworldy strength, he perseveres.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Single gender schools are not better for students academic and morals. Why?
Answer: Entire books have been written about the subject, studies done on it. And they basically all agree — when you segregate students by gender, you don’t actually help them from being ‘distracted’… no, they will simply seek their distractions elsewhere. Historically speaking, all-boys and all-girls schools are hotbeds for homosexuality. I mean put a bunch of hormonal teenagers of mixed gender in one class, for hours on end, day in, day out? They’ll get horny. Especially when gym class comes around, or they go swimming. Puritans the world over have come up with the same half-assed “solution” since times immemorial — make the boys all study together. And the girls, too. Seperate the genders. And all it does is redirect the hormones elsewhere. Which is why all-boys and all-girls schools have higher rates of homosexual activity. Morals come and go. They change over the years. And academic results can be debated and explained any way you like. Fact remains, teenagers are easily distracted. Remove one distraction, and they’ll find another. No, they’re not pure as driven snow. And no matter what you do, they’ll seek their own corruption. Humanity is wired this way. You can run from sexuality, but you can’t ever hide.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are good practices that make people live longer?
Answer: One thing that really helps is having a goal — something you want to do before you pass. Like Jeanne Calment who made a deal with her rotary André-François Raffray in 1965, when she was 90 years old… in exchange for having the right to continue living in the property, she’d sell the apartment to Raffray, for him to use after she passed. He sure felt he’d made a pretty sweet deal with the little old French lady… Only Calment didn’t die… she kept living. And living. And living. By 1995, Raffray had already paid Calment many times the value of the property she was living in. A piece of property he legally owned for some 30 years but couldn’t sell or make use of. He died, in 1995. And Calment, 120, continued to live for another 2 years, finally dying in 1997 at age 122 with Raffray’s widow and children continuing to pay her generously for her refusal to meet her maker. Calment lived another 32 years after reaching 90, and it made her a fortune in her day’s currency. She was paid generously just for being alive, despite continuing to smoke and drink and live merrily. “Sometimes in life, one makes a bad deal,” Calment simply said. And sometimes, people make mighty good deals.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some controversial opinions, like very controversial?
Answer: A big one would be Holocaust denial. I had a high school teacher once. He taught history. He told us: “Do you know how many gypsies the Nazis killed? Between 250,000 and half a million…” We were amazed, of course. He continued: “There is a margin of error there — a margin of error of 50% imagine that!” “We are so certain of the figure of six million! It is a holy number. No one may touch it. No one may question it. For to do so would be blasphemy. Meanwhile no one can agree how many gypsies Hitler killed. No one can agree how many people Stalin killed, how many people Mao killed. But we ALL know that Hitler killed six million Jews. That number is all-present. You can never escape the six million…” We were fifteen years old at the time. It was just one lecture, one little segue in the whole year we had this guy teach us history. But it always stuck with me. A very respectable guy. Very eloquent. And he planted this little seed of doubt so effortlessly, so casually… I wonder how many men like him there are.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is the US using excuses to interfere with Chinese athletes' performances at the Paris Olympics?
Answer: Just now, I watched as 17-year-old Olympic diver Quan Hongchan dove a perfect ten score. So perfect was her dive that when she gracefully hit the water, she hardly made a splash at all — her body just cut through the blue liquid below like a knife. It was quite beautiful to see. And it dawned on me — who the hell cares? I mean I get it… I’m critical of the Chinese government. Many people are, and with good reason. But I haven’t forgotten the many doping scandals in many other nations of the world. And it seems odd to single out China. Just as it seems odd to single out Russia’s athletes and forbid them from competing, when there are Americans, Chinese, Indians, Syrians, Israelis, Pakistanis, Palestinians, all allowed to compete. I’m all for “let the best man or woman win”. If the best athlete happens to be Chinese, so be it. I’m kind of over the whole fear of Chinese domination in sports. Focus on fields that truly matter, on the defense industry, economics, soft power, innovation and tech. Beat them there. Never mind sports. Paranoia helps no one, and gets you nowhere. It is not at all far-fetched that a nation of 1.4 billion souls that heavily invests in its athletes, will have some outstanding performances. In fact it would have been odd if they didn’t. And these athletes just live for their sports, the way any athlete does. They’re not political figures. Just talented young men and women. Dreamers. I say, let them dream. Let them shine. Seperate the athletes from their nations.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the implications of gender-neutral parenting?
Answer: In July 2024, an American father named Harrison Tinsley won sole custody of his four-year-old son, Sawyer Tinsley. Sawyer’s mother had been trying to raise their son as non-binary and “gender neutral”. She even made the little boy wear dresses some times, and would put makeup on his face. Whenever Harrison would pick the boy up, the little lad would cry, as he felt uncomfortable in his get-up… At the same time, children have this inate sense of loyalty towards both their parents… so they tend to go along with things, nine out of ten times. Sawyer’s mother herself identifies as a “non-binary lesbian”. Anyway, Harrison Tinsley reported the case child protective services and noted the little boy was clearly unhappy with the lifestyle forced onto him by his mother, who appears to be some sort of weirdo ideaologue. Was it ever about the best interests of the child? I doubt it. As soon as neutral observers from government agencies got involved, it is very telling how soon the child was removed from his mother’s custody.[1] What are the implications of “gender neutral parenting”? It comes from an ideology that the parent(s) adhere to. One in which no things ought to be ‘gendered’ and a child ideally should go by gender-neutral they/them pronouns until the child “figures out what he or she is” later in life. It’s never about what is best for the child — it is about ‘progressive’ parents living vicariously through their children and showing off how ‘forward thinking’ they are.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What’s the most famous unsolved question?
Answer: What always gets me are the blurry pictures. The vague stories. The far-fetched tales of “what-if”… Hitler surviving WWII is a major conspiracy theory I’ve always been intrigued by. It doesn’t help that the allies spread images of what he would look like without a moustache, or with a full beard, or with a shaved head. Neither Stalin nor the American government believed, initially, that Hitler truly died in that bunker… There were the supposed ‘dental records’. Traces of a skull, taken to Moscow by the Soviets — later testing would reveal they belonged to a woman in her thirties. No DNA testing has been done, to my knowledge, and there is no ‘smoking gun evidence’ of Hitler’s death in Berlin. That said? It’d take the whole entire bunker, every guard, every secretary, to have been “in on it”, with none of them ever slipping up for decades, even in old age. And there’d have to be a body double that was killed… someone who would have disappeared around the same time Hitler died. Then there is the escape itself — awfully risky that would have been. Bormann tried it, too, and was killed trying to leave Berlin. Would a 56-year-old dictator, ill with Parkinson’s disease and wide variety of other illnesses, even have made it out of Berlin alive, let alone to Argentina? That said, if he did get out, shaved the moustache, his hair lost or turned grey, he’d be just another old German dude living in the sun. You wouldn’t look at him twice.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Does slavery still exist?
Answer: There are many Indians, Africans and Filipinos who are worked to the bones in Dubai or the Gulf States. They’re dirt poor and have few rights — in fact they could be ejected from the country any moment. Why? Their employers take their passports. So on paper, officially? Many of them aren’t even there. A wrong look, a wrong word, and you’re done for. I knew one Filipina who was imprisoned — her employer had taken her passport, and refused to pay her. She eventually tried to file a police case against her employer for non-payment. Her employer then filed a case against HER for being “illegal” as she “didn’t have a passport”. When the employer had been the one to take the passport! There are millions of cases like these. We don’t call them slaves… we call them “migrant workers”. But what’s the difference? You know who provides the cotton for the cheap shirts many people in the West wear? Uyghur prisoners in concentration camps in Xinjiang, China. Nike. Adidas. Shein. Temu. Just a few of the many brands brought to you by slave labor.[1] We do not call these people slaves, either — they’re called ‘terrorists’ or ‘dissidents’ by the Chinese government. Or maybe just a “troublesome minority”. Slaves picked cotton in the American South before. And would get punished for not picking enough. Many of these ethnic minorities aren’t paid a dime. Many of them are, in fact, incarcerated because they’re “seperatists”. Which is basically just a fancy way of saying “someone who doesn’t like the central government very much due to their efforts to erase their culture and race.[2] Then we also have Bangladeshi factories. We have sweatshops in Latin America, in Vietnam, India, Pakistan. We have illegal workers, exploited, throughout the world. American prisoners put to work for a few cents an hour, doing mind-numbingly stupid work. And NONE of these people are called ‘slaves’. But how is it not slavery when a worker has zero rights and is unable to refuse the work for fear of severe repercussions, retaliation or a loss of livelihood?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How prevalent was "buck-breaking" during the USA slavery?
Answer: It wasn’t a thing. During the 19th century and before it, sodomy was a major no-no. The buck-breaking story comes from a viral ‘meme’ created in 2010. It suggests there was a tradition of white male slave owners sexually abusing “bucks”, young black male slaves. And by raping them, making them more ‘docile’ and breaking their wills… Now were there no instances of male owners raping male slaves? Certainly it happened. But it wasn’t some sort of widely known ‘traditional’ of sorts that happened openly and was common knowledge. In reality, most of the instances of slaves being raped involved female slaves. Sometimes very young female slaves. Sometimes children, yes, and sometimes men. But rarely so. No serious historian has ever written on “buck-breaking” as an actual phenomenon that happened. There were whippings. And mutilations. Humiliation was a near-constant companion for slaves of either gender… But people seriously underestimate how badly 18th and 19th century men HATED sodomy and how badly they didn’t want to be labeled as homosexuals. White men in the upper echelons of Southern society would never have gone around routinely sodomizing large numbers of black male slaves. It’s not a thing that happened — it’s a meme.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is JD Vance's remark about childless women controversial and offensive?
Answer: It’s kind of a bandwagon people all jumped on — myself included. J.D.’s wife, Usha Vance, recently gave an interview in which she clarified her husband’s stance a bit. And, oh shock of shocks, there’s some nuance in his argument. He doesn’t hate childlessness.[1] But J.D. Vance is concerned. He’s concerned because he feels that modern culture has become quite anti-child, anti-family. This is a legitimate concern. I’m not sure how he suggests to fix the issue aside from making abortions and birth control harder to obtain — the idea of giving “hand-outs” to poor families, struggling young newlyweds or providing kids with free school lunches are something Vance’s own Republicans are allergic to.[2] He wants people to make more babies. But where are the policies he suggests, to make this a more easy life choice for young couples to make? I’m not seeing any. He wants a cultural shift in how we see children, how we see families. This is a noble motivation. But when you don’t put your money where your mouth is, it all rings rather… empty. I’m actually 100% in agreement with Mr. Vance that dwindling birth rates ARE a problem. And that we should not look as children and having a family as a burden, but as a blessing. But in order to relieve that burden and make raising a family feel like a blessing again, major policy changes are needed. Policy changes Vance and his ilk would no doubt denounce as “socialism”. This guy is all talk, no game. A rich man, married to a rich woman, insulated, living in a bubble.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Foreigners, how are you viewing the removal of Sheikh Hasina from power? What do you think about the protests going in Bangladesh?
Answer: To me, the image gives me goosebumps. Bangladeshi protesters standing on top of the presidential palace of Bangladesh. Holding the flag of their nation. This is the equivalent of American protesters forcing the US president to flee the nation, and taking over the White House. That’s power, right there. I’ve heard from Bangladeshi people online for quite a while, as the mass protests waged — “our president is corrupt, our government hates us, we have no future,” they’d tell me. Always the same complaints. Always the same criticism. And it seemed the young folks were, collectively, just done. Tired, and dome. So they rose up. And they drove out the president. To tell you the truth, if any mass movement gains such enormous support, and a government falls or is driven out of power? That’s grand. I support it. If tomorrow American, French or Chinese students did the same, I’d be all for it. If Nigerians did it, I’d applaud them. If it was the Russians, I’d be amazed. Governments all too often forget they rule over people. And they have a mandate of power, but it is by virtue of their citizens that they rule. Not because they, themselves, are so perfect, so all-knowing, so flawless… people placed you where you are. And if you screw up, the same people who gave you power may very well take it from you. Let it serve as a lesson to leaders everywhere.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What makes an actor's performance feel more realistic than another? Why is it so hard to achieve that level of realism in acting?
Answer: You have to be slightly obsessed with your work for things to feel truly real. Daniel Day-Lewis is the best and most commonly cited example of this — in Scorcese’s Gangs of New York, Day-Lewis plays Bill the Butcher, who has a glass eye. He had his eye covered in prosthetic glass, and learned to tap it with the tip of a knife without blinking. Which reportedly took quite a while because instinctively, we want to blink desperately when the tip of a huge knife comes in sight… there’s a noticeable difference between real acting, and the type of CGI green screen trash that Marvel has been putting out for years — no need to actually do anything, learn anything, if you can just make a computer render any animation you desire and save the efforts… Day-Lewis’ character was a former butcher, by the way. So he worked in a butchershop for a month prior to filming. In order to handle his knife the way a butcher would, and cut meat in a believable manner —because it WAS believable. Realism isn’t hard to obtain, but it takes genuine commitment. It’s the same reason we went from great renaissance paintings to ‘artists’ lazily and violently flinging paint on a canvas and continued to call it ‘art’.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did anything bother Abraham Lincoln during his presidency?
Answer: More than anything, it was Abraham Lincoln’s wife, Mary Todd Lincoln, who bothered him. She was what was called in her day a “manic-depressive”, or rather a sufferer from bipolar personality disorder in our current lingo. Mary Todd would move between moments of great loving care, and extreme cruelty. In her manic episodes she would serve imported oysters and prove a passionate lover, in her depressive states she could be cruel, even physically abusive to her husband and sons. Abraham Lincoln, despite being an exceptionally strong 6′4″ man and a former athlete of some renown, was a complete slave to his mentally unstable 5′2″ wife — a wife who would, at times, abuse and degrade him in public, much to his considerable humiliation. Often she would cruelly make Honest Abe sleep on a hard couch or even the floor when they’d have a fight. He was every bit the stereotypical “henpecked husband” one would later see in sitcoms. When the two were in good spirits, things were truly great. And when they were not, things were truly horrific. Violent moodswings would catch the Lincolns off-guard at the most inopportune of moments. And the President suffered greatly from the ensuing uncertainty that followed him wherever he went. There have been moments where Mary Todd Lincoln’s mental state declined to such a degree that Abraham wanted to have her committed to an asylum. The death of their beloved sons further drove Mary Todd to the very edges of reason… and as she drifted in and out of sanity, her husband suffered most of all, as he carried on his shoulders the weight of the nation and failed to find refuge even inside his own home.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is there any way to justify the forcible internment of Japanese Americans during WWII?
Answer: There is one photograph that perfect illustrates for me how awful the Japanese internment camps were… the photo shows a Japanese-American WWI veteran arriving at the camp. He decided to put on his old Navy uniform, medals, signs of rank. And arrived in them in order to make a point. He wanted the people imprisoning him to see that he was a loyal American, as American as any of the men hired to guard him. He wanted to remind them that he had fought for his country, too. Now his pension was forfeit, his sons lost their jobs, his grandchildren and their mothers were ending up in a camp and he, too, had to endure the humiliation in his old age despite never having been anything other than a patriot. So he wore his uniform. The uniform for the country he would have willingly given his life for. That now decided to imprison him solely because his parents had been born in Japan, and Japan had attacked America. Can this be justified? You tell me.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What do you think about racism and ethnic bigotry?
Answer: To me, racism is kind of like sports fanaticism. You root for your team. And sure, that’s okay. I mean you want “your guys” to win. But then, that also means you kind of want the other guys to lose, or else, there’s no victory is there? And when your guys lose, you get mad. You say the referee was biased. Or maybe someone bought off the goalie. Also, just like with sport fanatics, you have to get it into your system at an early age… I mean if you get into sports at the age of 25, you’re probably able to see the silliness of it a lot better. But get into it at age 5, watching your parents, your grandparents, drunk uncles, red-faced older brothers, all screaming at the same little TV screen? You’re doomed. It’s imprinted in you far too strongly to easily rid yourself of such an affliction. Of course you’ll scream at the TV, too… Of course you will hate the other team. Of course you will identify with your team. Make their victories yours, and take their losses as a personal slight… racism it’s a mental form of learned helplessness — learned stupidity.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did Quora have any impact on your life? Did you get any new perspectives that helped you in your life
Answer: One interesting connection I made was with a young Filipino man who was part of a cult. I wrote about our connection in another answer, years ago. He was faced with a devilish dilemma — either leave his fiancé of several years, or persuade her to join the cult for him. She didn’t want to, and he didn’t really want to make her do it. But if he didn’t, her eternal soul would be forfeit. And if he left, so would his. He wrestled with this moral dilemma for years as he remained loyal to the INC (Iglesia ni Cristo). He came to me for some advice on the matter. We talked. And talked. And talked. We talked for weeks. And finally he came to see my point of view — that true love means you would never force someone to switch faiths just to make things “easier” on you. He also came to realize, and accept for himself at long last, that the church he was part of was, indeed, a cult. It controlled what he spent money on, what he ate, drank, even controlled his political votes because the church leaders would get bribed by politicians and would then tell all cult members to “vote in unison” because “unison is Biblical”… I swear, you cannot make this shit up. Through our conversations he came to finally see and accept the absurdity of his faith. And decided to leave once and for all. His parents, sadly, were penalized for this and lost some standing in the community; that’s another way a cult can hold its wayward members emotionally hostage. In 2022, my friend and his lady, on their way to marriage, invited me to a nice resort in Boracay, the Philippines. They treated me to nice food, to island hopping by boat, snorkeling and endless buffets. He was a free man, now. Grateful for my help. We’re still in touch, every now and then. Quora gave me friends for life, and one of the best vacation I’ve ever had!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why does JD Vance wear eyeliner?
Answer: Nobody aside from Mr. J.D. Vance himself knows the answer to this question. Aside from, perhaps, his wife Usha Vance. It is funny, though — male makeup is seen as unmasculine in the current zeitgeist, and Vance belongs to the party that claims to be all about masculinity. Things weren’t always like this, however… Historically speaking, makeup was a manly affair. From the French kings to Giacomo Casanova himself, everyone wore powdered wigs and all faces were powdered to such a degree it’d put a geisha to shame. And these weren’t wilting flowers — 17th and 18th century men were hardcore drunks and womanizers, the lot of them. Going back to a more recent time, we find the glamrock stars of yore. From Alice Cooper to the guys from Kiss, Bowie, Jagger, all of these fellows got around. A new lady every night. Sometimes a dude. Who cares, it’s that special type of sex, drugs and rock ’n roll lifestyle. A lifestyle as rough and tumble as it is strangely forgiving. But in the year 2024, a man who sometimes wears eyeliner is now “suspicious”. Especially in the circles Mr. Vance finds himself in. I think he’s just trying to make his bright blue eyes ‘pop’, to tell you the truth. His best buddy and the man responsible for funding Vance’s education and political career, gay billionaire Peter Thiel, might just like his eyes that way — fierce.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What, in your opinion, is the greatest government conspiracy or cover-up in history, and why?
Answer: In 2018, Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was brutally murdered inside the Saudi embassy in Istanbul, Turkey. Mr. Kashoggi was rather critical of the Saudi government, in particular of its de-facto leader, Crown Prince Muhammad Bin Salman (MBS). Many people think this is the only reason the journalist was killed. But the story goes… a little deeper. What few looked into is the particular story Mr. Khashoggi was working on at the time of his murder — it had to do with Jared Kushner, son-in-law of then US president Trump. Khashoggi had unearthed a connection between the two men… Kushner had been selling classified documents to the Saudi’s, and MBS used the information thus acquired to rid himself of rivals within Saudi Arabia. Some were arrested, some had ‘mysterious’ and awfully convenient helicopter crashes… After Trump left the White House following his 2020 presidential defeat, Kushner received an investment of 2 billion(!) dollars to his equity firm. With Kushner, himself, overseeing the money.[1] This was the blood money he received. The value of his silence, his cooperation. And this lucrative partnership and the priceless information thus acquired, is why Khashoggi had to go… The American government was quick to label the murder of Khashoggi “an outrage” but little else happened. Because they knew exactly what the man was up to, and why he had to go. Jared Kushner sold state secrets and classified information to the tune of billions, and the man about to expose him was chainsawed to pieces while still alive for it. And “certain people” do NOT want you to know about this, for obvious reasons.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do you believe in the saying, "Be careful for what you wish for in life, because it just may come true"?
Answer: I mean, the Olympics just proved it once again. French Olympic pole vaulter Anthony Ammirati lost out on a medal. No part of the athlete is supposed to hit the wooden bar. But he knocked it over with his penis, and thus was disqualified. You can have either a big dong, or a gold medal. But you can’t apparently have both. Because the same exact incident happened before, in 2016 — Japanese pole vaulter Hiroki Ogita, too, knocked over the pole vault bar with his manhood. And he, too, lost because of it. In Olympic pole vaulting, there are two kind of men — those with nice shiny medals. And those with magnum dongs. Still a pretty solid consolation prize, as far as consolation prizes go. But rather unfortunate for the athletes.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Have you ever realized you were mistaken about something you were certain of?
Answer: Definitely! Just yesterday, in fact. I did a whole answer about an Algerian boxer named Imane Khelif.[1] She failed a gender test a few years ago, and due to her rather mannish appearance, people simply assumed she must be a dude — even though the Olympic committee did allow her to compete as a woman, and she had been born a woman, too. Photographs were shared of Khelif as a child. She’s the little girl on the right, in the picture below. The one in pink, looking very much like a girl: Years of boxing and being punched in the face endlessly in sparring sessions have left tall and gangly Khelif with a rather masculine face and body. And who knows, maybe there is something chromosomally wrong, maybe there’s some intersex-situation going on, something akin to the Caster Semenya situation years ago in another Olympics controversy… But yeah, I was kind of being a major dick about the whole thing. The whole internet was. We basically just went full-circle and got so caught up in the fear of transgender athletes invading women’s spaces and competions, that the whole internet just collectively bullied some poor Algerian boxer for not looking “girly” enough.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What’s a controversial issue in which both sides have valid arguments?
Answer: A couple of months ago, a man chatted me up on Messenger. I knew his last name, vaguely, as I was Facebook friends with a younger fellow by the same name. He said he was the father of this friend of mine… but I quickly determined he wasn’t who he claimed to be — he was a Nigerian scammer. And when pushed, he admitted to this readily. So I got to talk to the guy. And his life really was bleak… as of me writing this answer, there are protests going on in Nigeria. Protests aptly named “End Bad Governance in Nigeria” — a very to-the-point name. Basically, there aren’t any jobs. Salaries are low. Cost of living just keeps on rising and even a degree isn’t a guarantee for work. Not to mention the fact that to get an education is often unaffordable to begin with… So we have a whole generation of young men, scouring the internet for little old ladies and lonely old men to scam out of their hard-earned money. Sometimes, mercifully, they end up talking to someone a little less vulnerable, like yours truly, and they don’t get a single cent. But all too often, they cheat and finesse someone abroad out of their life savings. When I confronted the scammer about this, he basically just told me he’s broke as hell, he hates himself for doing what he does, but how else can he feed his daughters and wife? And that just kind of breaks my heart. Because what these people do is, objectively, awful. They screw people over. Innocent people who don’t deserve to be screwed over. At the same time, these scammers have been screwed over by their own government for as long as they’ve been alive.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the worst holidays?
Answer: The President of Turkey, Erdogan, just announced that August 2 is a “day of national mourning”. Why did he declare this as a day of national mourning? Because his friend, Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh, was blown to smithereens.[1] He wants to “honor Haniyeh’s martyrdom”. It’s just about the most stupid holiday idea I ever heard of. It’s like Germany’s chancellor Olaf Scholz declaring April 30 a national day of mourning, “because Adolf Hitler was martyred that day”. Or maybe a Pakistani President declaring the death day of Osama Bin Laden as something special, something meaningful. Children not going to school. Little Hamas flags waving around. How on earth do you even come up with such a demented idea? I had to check the story, read multiple sources, to see if this isn’t some sort of sick joke… Yeah, I think August 2, the “day of the martyrdom of Ismail Haniyeh” is a pretty damn dumb holiday. This was a dude who literally starved the people of Gaza for money, took 20% of all imports as personal tax, who lived like a billionaire sheikh while his people suffered. A man who brainwashed and radicalized an entire generation of Palestinians into believing nothing is more noble than to die fighting… and now he’s got a whole holiday from a nation that wants to join the European Union and portray itself as respectable and civilized?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who is viewed as America's most womanizing president?
Answer: There are quite a few Presidents up for the title of “biggest womanizer”. There’s Warren G. Harding who is primarily known for his naugthy leaked letters (he nicknamed his manhood “Jerry” for some odd reason) and for the fact that he may well have died of a heart attack in office and mid-coitus, aged 57. Then there’s JFK, of course — Kennedy famously slept around a lot. Among his famous conquests we find none other than Marilyn Monroe, who sang to him suggestively on his birthday. His poor wife Jackie suffered a lot from Kennedy’s notorious lack of subtlety. And then there’s Lyndon B. Johnson who would often brag about how he “had more women by accident than Kennedy did on purpose!” I’m not even going to bring up Bill Clinton or Trump. Frankly, America has had it’s share of crass leaders. Johnson may just take the cake — he nicknamed his presidential tallywacker “Jumbo”. It was of prodigious size and he would whip it out at random moments just to prove a point. Once he did so during a meeting with senators about why America ought to stay in Vietnam. Johnson opened his zipper, let Jumbo hit the desk with a thud and said: “This is why!”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How do you think the participation of transgender athletes will be handled at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
Answer: On paper, they’re not allowed to compete. In practice? The waters are a little… muddy. The athlete below is named Angela Carini. She’s a 100% biologically a woman. Within 46 seconds she had lost her first fight against an Algerian opponnent. She broke down in tears, being hit hard in the face. In her first comment post-match she said she was hit “so hard she felt she would die”. And that’s what boxing is all about, right? You either hit the other guy or gal, or you get hit and lose. No big deal. But let’s look a little closer at who Carini lost to — Algerian boxer Imane Khelif. Khelif was previously banned from competing as a woman in sporting events — she apparently failed to provide evidence she was a biological woman, and was tested to have male chromosomes. Officially, Khelif is a woman. Competes as a woman. But there is very real doubt about whether or not she isn’t transgender… The 2024 Olympics are officially excluding transgender athletes. But in practice, things get a little complex when you’re also trying to be the “most inclusive” Olympics ever. Because even when science disagrees, who are you to tell a lady boxer she isn’t a lady boxer, if she feels that way?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why are most black women unattractive?
Answer: How foolish of you. You’ve obviously never seen Michael Jackson’s music video for “Remember The Time” starring Somali super model Iman, have you? I did. I was just a kid. But you may say, in a sense, it made me a man. My first celebrity crushes had been white or middle eastern women. And this video opened my eyes to the beauty of Africa. She exudes CLASS, in her every pore. Her jawline, her nose, divine. Her eye shape, her eyebrows. That skin, so flawless, so smooth… and of course her body is amazing, too. Those eyes… Iman, for the record, married David Bowie. Another man of culture. He recognized that beauty. Wasn’t blind to it, and what man ever could be? They made a gorgeous couple. Stayed together until he died of cancer. Still miss that brilliant man. Just recently, I fell in love with an African girl, myself. She’s from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. And she’s absolutely gorgeous, too. Even her handwriting is pretty — she wrote me a letter, and scanned it and sent me a copy of the photograph. And her voice, too. On video calls, it’s like some dream sequence where I’m talking to an Angel come to earth. Yeah, I know. I sound corny. But that’s how love works, isn’t it? She’s just so damn regal. And no, I know — not every African girl is regal, and gorgeous, and a super model. But plenty of them are absolutely stunning. Every ethnic group, every race and nationality has it’s good and less good-looking members. Me, I’ve never been able to deny the allure of ebony. I understand perfectly why King Solomon fell for the Queen of Sheba.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is Islam the most toxic religion in the world?
Answer: It’s kind of a tiresome line of reasoning, and not one I am very fond of. As far as criticism goes, Islam gets its fair share — and rightfully so. But it’s “low-hanging fruit” where I’m concerned. Take for instance Mormons. Below we see a photo of a group of Mormon polygamists imprisoned in a facility in Utah, in 1889. Islam limits men to a maximum of four wives — and they may only marry a second, third or fourth wife if they are financially well-off enough to provide the same lifestyle for the additional wives as they can the first and primary wife. They must treat these wives well, and have relatively relaxed divorce laws compared to some other faiths. By contrast, some Mormon sects allowed, and still allow, their male faithful to marry a near endless amount of women. I once read the grandfather of Mitt Romey was a polygamist and has tens of thousands of descendants alive today… We can single out Islam. Barbaric, backwards, treats women like cattle… Go ahead ahead. It’s your prerogative. But let us not delude ourselves — religion, in general, has a pretty lousy track records where it comes to human rights. Furthermore, there’s no such thing as one universal Islam; there are some Muslim nations that are quite liberal, and some that are incredibly regressive. My best friend married a Malaysian Muslima who smokes, drinks and hasn’t worn a hijab in ages.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Have any of the Republican’s line of attacks stuck against Vice President Kamala Harris?
Answer: The most nasty accusation thrown at Kamala Harris by Trump and his followers is that she “slept her way to the top”. There is some truth to the rumor, too. In the early 1990s, Harris had a brief relationship with San Francisco mayor Willie Brown, a man several decades her senior. Kamala’s own career was only just taking off in those days, and Brown was a powerful man in local politics. Did her dalliance with Brown help Harris, politically? It certainly can’t have hurt her, career-wise. The “diversity hire” accusation backfired with likely voters as it was deemed ‘racist’ by quite a few people in the public. But the “sleeping your way to the top” argument is fairly effective when there are actually pictures out there of a young, remarkably pretty Kamala Harris hanging on to the arm of a wealthy politician old enough to be her father. It’s kind of a low blow, especially coming from Trump, a man who famously would bang a refridgerator if you put lipstick on it and a blonde wig and told him it was made in Eastern Europe. There’s also the “Kamala Harris was in charge of the border” line of attack — this one kind of backfired when the Harris team kept pointing out that there was a bipartisan border bill that Republicans nuked at the behest of Trump, specifically so he could keep hammering immigration as a talking point for the November elections. So they’re stuck with “Kamala has a weird nervous laugh” and “she slept her way to power”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you name an example of bad parenting?
Answer: When I was in elementary school there was one girl whose mother was one of those “Tiger Mom” types. Always reaching for the stars. Only the best was good enough. And we barely noticed it, at the time. Because her daughter did well. She was the type of girl who was quick to catch on, had a near-photographic memory and excellent recall — school would have been fairly easy for such a girl either way, even without a mother always kicking her butt to do more. Her son, however, was a different creature. He wasn’t the bookish type at all. So he got grounded. A lot. Got scolded a lot. It wasn’t ever good enough. Even a grade that, for a guy like him, was pretty solid? Wasn’t good enough. Because it wasn’t the highest. Because wasn’t the best in his class. His classmates would go on schooltrips and he’d be stuck at home, studying. The only thing he truly loved was sports. Athletics. He excelled in them, and he was particularly good at hockey. Only on the field was he free to be himself, if only for an hour or so. His sister, meanwhile, continued to perform outstandingly — by the time she finished high school, she went to an American university on a scholarship. No doubt grateful to be away from her overly involved mother. The brother wasn’t so lucky. One day in his final year of high school, he came home with a failing grade. Math, I believe it was. His mother told him he couldn’t play the hockey championship finals, as punishment. The one game he’d trained for the whole year. He lost it — in one flare of anger, he hit her with his hockey stick. It hit her temple. She fell down the stairs. And died. Kid was tried as a juvenile, I believe he wasn’t yet eighteen. No idea what became of him. But you may say, his mother’s ambition and desire to live vicariously through her own children is what killed her. She kept pushing a boy into doing things he wasn’t built to do. Into excelling in fields and areas he wasn’t made to excel in… Too many parents make this mistake — they try to mold their children, like clay, to become exactly what they want them to be. Their ambition is limitless, their disappointment and insults a neverending reservoir of bitterness. They push and push their little puppet. Until the child either succeeds in realizing these lofty dreams the parents have dreamed for it… or until the child, unable to secure victory, breaks.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are your thoughts about JD Vance saying that the country is run by "childless cat ladies" who don't have a "direct stake in it," specifically naming Pete Buttigieg and AOC?
Answer: A few months ago, I wrote an answer where I made fun of childless people who claim pets as their “furbabies”.[1] Like J.D. Vance, I described it as a societal problem. Like Mr. Vance I, too, am concerned with dwindling birth rates. As is any serious economist worth his salt, or just about any other human being who looks at the bigger picture and where we’re heading as a society… That said? One lady who followers me on Quora came out and said she was a bit hurt not just by what I said, but how I said it. She reminded me of how a lot of people are childless by choice. And that you cannot attach judgements of value to people who have versus people who don’t have children, because you’re assuming things. Vance is assuming an awful lot, about “childless cat ladies”. Sure some are that way by choice. But many others have spent a fortune on IVF or suffered countless gut-wrenchingly painful miscarriages. They would love to have a family, but can’t. And Vance is just rubbing salt in the wound, for no reason other than because he can. So what are my thoughts? I think Vance’s comments came across short-sighted. He identified a very real societal issue, but addressed it very bluntly, without any finesse or subtlety whatsoever, and without taking into account the complexities of the issue of childlessness. I have made that mistake, myself. And I was humbled by some of the responses. He should be, too, if he has any decency.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What photos look Photoshopped but are actually real?
Answer: At the Paris Olympics, the French national basketball team took on the Japanese. At some point, French player Victor Wembanyama ran past Japanese player Yuki Togashi. It looked like an almost surreal image, as if it was done by photoshop. The sheer difference in body sizes between the two men. But what you see, is what you get here — Wembanyama stands 7′4″ and Yuki Togashi is a mere 5′4″. We’re a funny species, humans. Kind of bred the way dogs are… some of are Mastiffs and Great Danes, and some of us are Dachshunds and Chihuahas.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What act of Israel establishes it as indisputably the most badass nation on earth?
Answer: I’ve written a ton of answers in the past about the enormous death toll in Gaza, and have been critical about Israel’s actions there. But what the media often neglect to mention is that the violent October 7 terrorist attack that claimed the lives of hundrdeds of Israeli women, children, elderly and civilians, preceded it. Ismail Haniyeh is the leader of Hamas, the guys behind that attack. Is, or I should say, was. Because Ismail Haniyeh went to Iran for the inauguration of Iran’s new President. And while in Teheran to watch the event, Israel took him out together with one of his bodyguards. And blew Mr. Haniyeh to smithereens, right in the lair of the lion. At the peak of his power, and in the midst of their enemies, they took him out. Because they don’t give a shit — he’s a terrorist, leader of a terrorist regime, and thousands died in his name. And now, he’s dead. Finally he’s a martyr himself, after having driven countless young vulnerable youths to be martyrs for him… Ismail Haniyeh lived a lavish life. Conned the Palestinian people out of billions and strolled around like a King all over the Middle East. And now, he’s dead. The man who considered himself untouchable is no more. Far too many Palestinians needlessly gave their lives for lousy leaders undeserving of it — and in one fell swoop, Israel took out the head of the beast.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Were there more "white" slaves than "black" slaves in America?
Answer: An interesting photograph I saw the other day shows an American slave named Preely Coleman, posing for the camera in 1935 at age 85. Mr. Coleman has straight white hair and a full beard, a straight Roman nose and while hard work on the plantation has turned his skin several shades darker, it was rather fair in his youth. Mr. Coleman was the son of one of his master’s sons, and his mother herself was half-white herself. Which is why, as a young lad, he could easily pass for one of the master’s fully white grandsons who also ran around on the same fields, played underneath the same sun and ate the same food. The difference, however, is that Preely was his master’s official property, whereas his other sons and grandsons were just family and fully free to come and go as they pleased. Preely Coleman was freed in 1865, at the age of thirteen. There were many men and women just like him — some were only a quarter black, or less. The majority of slaves in America, however, were of mostly black ancestry. Still on every plantation you’d encounter a fair amount of slaves who looked (and were!) almost entirely of white heritage.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do any Hollywood actors, directors, or writers intentionally act unintelligent in order to gain more roles or create better movies?
Answer: One man in Hollywood who is far smarter than people give him credit for, would be Arnold Schwarzenegger. With a reported IQ of around 130, the Austrian Oak is a remarkably bright individual. His persona in movies, at least in the early era of his film career, was that of a musclebound brute, not necessarily a genius. But the journey he took to get to that point was a remarkable one, and his subsequent moves every bit as brilliant. Schwarzenegger maximized his time like no other — when he wasn’t working out, or sleeping around (he was always pumping, either iron or ladies!) he’d read. Read, study, or set up businesses. Even as a young bodybuilding champion he would take his earnings and start buying up and fixing real estate, hiring his fellow bodybuilding comrades still struggling to make it big as workers and giving them a percentage of profits. In the evenings after working out he’d take acting classes, and while already an actor he began studying the world of politics. Oh and he got together the niece of President John F. Kennedy, too. He met her parents at a social function, told her mother “your daughter has a great ass!” and he STILL managed to get her and marry her. Within a decade, Arnold was the governor of California. Not bad for a small-town boy from rural Austria who came to America without a penny to his name, speaking only broken English.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who was the most powerful US president and why?
Answer: None other than Franklin Delano Roosevelt, better known as FDR. He was in office longer than any other US president before or after him — for twelve years, from 1933 until 1945. And he died in office, too, sitting for a portrait. Had he not died, he could have had another term. Or another. Dude was enormously popular. And enormously controversial. FDR was a fascinating character — he set up huge public works, in order to get the American people working and earning again following the Great Depression. Got involved in WWII and kicked some major German and Japanese butt. He oversaw some of history’s most consequential moments. And he was ruthless, too… hell, he even agreed with Stalin at Yalta that Germany, following Nazi defeat, should be wholly demilitarized and turned into a medieval feudal society so as never to risk the chance of a rising and powerful Germany. We’re talking full-on burning down factories and forcing people out of cities into rural communities levels of social rearrangement. Thankfully, Churchill talked some sense into his co-conspirators. Franklin Delano Roosevelt was an enigma. He was ruthless, efficient, and his enemies still don’t know what to make of him — some called him a fascist, some called him a socialist. Some called him far-right, some far-left. He was radical. Above all, he was radically different. And then he died at the height of his power, just a few days before Hitler, who reportedly celebrated Roosevelt’s demise. What he refused to realize until the last moment, however, is that Roosevelt already had him beat even in death.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: The far left is to be blamed for the rail sabotage in Paris, the interior minister says. What do you think?
Answer: It’s possible. Authorities seem to lean this way following an investigation.[1] Now of course the far left is far from a unified front. One other theory that is being floated is that the attacker who destroyed vital parts of the French railroad network may have been in cahoots with the Russians.[2] The Russian connection seems like a fairly believable one — the far-left in France is quite pro-Kremlin, as is the far-right for that matter. Everyone made a huge deal about Le Pen’s pro-Russia party losing the recent elections. In order to stop the radical right, French voters en masse moved towards ANY party that stood a chance to stop them. Which then ushered in a victory for socialist Jean-Luc Mélenchon. Question: Who are some famous intellectual badasses?

He was the real deal. And he didn’t give a damn about what society thought of him — he was the very rarest of creatures: honest, genuine and true intellect expressed with eloquence unmatched.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Where do names of cities originate?
Answer: In the year 15 A.D. in what is now Germany, Agrippina the Younger was born while her father was on campaign. He was a grandson of the Emperor Augustus himself, making Agrippina a great-granddaughter of the Emperor. Likewise, she was an adopted granddaughter of Emperor Tiberius. Of course she had no idea of her high birth — she was just a little girl, after all. Her father Germanicus was all too aware. To honor his daughter’s blessed arrival, General Germanicus named the encampment were she was born Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium. Colonia Claudia, for short. What started off as just another camp, grew into a city. Germanicus built walls. He would soon die, but his son Caligula became Emperor a few years after. And after Aggripina herself would be the mother of yet another controversial Emperor — none other than Nero himself. The line of Aggripina, of Germanicus, Tiberius and Augustus, perished. Their dynasty ceased to exist. But the walls of Colonia Claudia survive until today. Colonia became Cologne (Köln), Germany.

Question: What were the greatest last words in history?
Answer: In the Salem witch trials of 1692, 81-year-old farmer Giles Corey was falsely accused of witchcraft. They placed him on the ground, put wooden plates on him and covered these with large rocks. This would slowly break his body and make it harder for him to breathe. For two days they kept increasing the weight, as each torturer would ask him in between rounds of torture, whether he would like to confress… Each time, Corey said only two words: “More weight!” He kept it up. Even when the weight got so heavy that his ribs began breaking, blood coming out of his mouth. At one point, his tongue was pressed out of his mouth, an one of his tormenters pushed it back inside the old man’s mouth with the tip of his cane… They asked him, one final time, to confess. Giles Corey smiled and screamed out: “More weight!” They obliged him, and finally the weight of the rocks crushed his chest entirely, killing Corey after two days of excruciating pain.

Question: What leaders in history have stepped down from positions of power?
Answer: The Roman consul and general Lucius Cornelius Sulla marched into Rome, killed his enemies most brutally and installed himself as Dictator. For two years he held near-absolute power, restoring the Republic, filling the nation’s coffers with the money taken from sold off assets of his rivals, enemies and any nobleman who so much as looked at him the wrong way. Question: Why do artists love more than other people?
Answer: I’m artist myself — I weave words. But do I feel love more than others just because words come easy to me? An Indian day laborer loved more deeply than any artist I can think of, myself included. His name was Dashrath Manjhi. His wife got into an accident in 1959. She fell from a mountain. That same mountain then made it impossible for her to get medical attention on time. She died. So Dashrath Manjhi cut down that mountain. Stone by stone, rock by rock, he took it apart with his own two hands. All he had was a hammer, a chisel and two strong hands. Twenty-two years he carved away at his monumental task. All alone. Authorities had ignored his pleas, and no help ever came. By the time he was done, a road was carved. And traveling to a hospital, which would have taken 55 kilometers, now took only 15… "When I started hammering the hill, people called me a lunatic but that only steeled my resolve,” was all he said on the matter. You tell me which artist loved more deeply than Mr. Dashrath Manjhi. I know many artists, and romantic and sentimental as we are, none of us took on the mountain that killed our wife. And won.

Question: Are modern humans stronger and more fit than our ancestors?

Question: Has there been a decline in intelligence in America over time? What factors may have contributed to this decline? Can measures be taken to prevent it from happening again in the future?
Answer: One big difference in recent years? People stopped reading books. I’m talking about real books. Real, physical books you can touch and hold. The smell of paper. The weight of the cover in your hand. Mr. Theodore Roosevelt, on the picture below, read about 500(!) books a year. That’s more than one a day. He did so even throughout his eight years of being President of the US. Now many people don’t even read one book a year. Two, or three, if they’re particularly hungry. We say we don’t have the time — but back in the “olden days” even presidents, generals and mighty warriors managed to find time. Alexander the Great was a voracious reader, for example. So were Julius Caesar and Cleopatra. Now this may be strictly anecdotal, and forgive me if it is of no use to you. But the smartest people I know, are readers. My grandfather was a seaman, and not a particularly educated man. But even when he was at sea, working ten hour shifts under rough circumstances, he’d still retreat to his hammock at night and read big books about Native American history and culture. Why? Because he could. And because he genuinely wanted to learn all about them. Nowadays, if we want to know some more about any given subject? We just Google it. And we learn a thing or two, sure. But much of that knowledge evaporates like snow in the sun. In one ear, out the other… Fifty years ago, even your plumber might retreat at night and read about Roman history. Your sunday school teacher may read detective novels in her free time. Today? Everyone just scrolls their phones. It’s not the same. People aren’t necessarily more stupid. But they’re lacking in specialized, concentrated knowledge about one or more specific fields. It’s all generalized, very widely applicable, and only scratching the surface of most subjects. Knowledge became widely available… but intensely shallow.

I’m sure there will be many people in the comment sections — most of them Indians — who will remind me of her countless mortal sins and those of her family. But still? She was power personified. Indira Gandhi was in power in India from 1966 until 1977, and again from 1980 until her death in 1984. She ruled over a nation of hundreds of millions of souls. She fought wars, and won some of those wars decisively. She centralized power greatly. Henry Kissinger, a man himself known for his ruthless Machiavellianism, declared Indira “the Iron Lady”. In her own words: “I am not a person to be pressured — by anybody or any nation.” The photo I used to illustrate this answer shows Indira Gandhi inspecting the Indian army. The Indians had just decisively beaten Pakistan. The Iron Lady looks out over her troops. Love her or hate her but she had more balls than most male statesmen over her era, and most alive today.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: People sometimes say that times have changed, but have they? Have times changed or have people changed? If times have changed, then what is meant by the word times?
Answer: On March 31, 1968, President Lyndon B. Johnson announced to the people that he would not seek re-election. He was feeling too old and had a sense that he would die somewhere in the next turn. Johnson felt he simply lacked the energy to run a nation. Lyndon B. Johnson was just a few months shy of 60. And he already felt “too old” to do the job. His feeling proved to be prophetic — he did, indeed, die about four years into retirement, aged only 64. The amazing thing? No one “pushed out” Johnson. He just left by his own free will. In fact, when he announced he was leaving, no one had seen it coming. It was like a burst of thunder on a clear, rainless sky… People have more hubris nowadays. They feel they’re invincible, unstopppable. Particularly people in power. We used to be different. We used to have this sixth sense, almost like a farm cat who knows it’s time is through and crawls into a far corner of the barn to die. Nowadays old leaders just keep loudly denying their mortality and cling to any sense of power until pushed out or defeated.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who was involved in the JFK assassination?
Answer: When it comes to conspiracy theories, the “crown jewel” of them all this is thing called the Deep State. Shadowy forces within the US government that wanted Kennedy gone. If the shooter, Lee Harvey Oswald, was merely a loon unknown to authorities, I’d have believed he truly was the ‘lone wolf’ radical they made the man out to be… Fact is, he wasn’t unknown to authorities at all. Oswald was a US marine who defected to the Soviets. Was allowed back into America. He was a known traitor to his country, a man who fled to the Russians in the middle of the Cold War. There were huge files on the guy — he was a known foreign asset, spoke fluent Russian, had a Russian wife. He was being followed, was being listened to, his phones were tapped. In other words, authorities knew who Lee Harvey Oswald was. What he was doing… …and yet, they did nothing. They just let him do his thing. Kill Kennedy. Then when he was arrested, a random guy walks up to him — while he’s in police custody! — and just, shoots him dead. Just like that. This can only lead me to two conclusions: one, Oswald was a Russian asset and the US government was incredibly incompetent. Two, they knew perfectly well what he was up to and just let him do his thing because the government itself wanted Kennedy gone.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What makes the YouTube celebrity Mr. Beast so controversial?
Answer: People are just bitter assholes, nine out of ten times. Someone doing genuine good will be hated for it just as easily if not more easily than someone who genuinely sucks. Mr. Beast isn’t a bad dude. The only thing I dislike about the guy is probably his near-chronic inability to close his mouth in thumbnails. A phenomenon dubbed as “soy face” in some internet circles. That’s literally all I got, as far as criticism goes… this guy literally delivered up to three million in aid to Ukrainian refugees. Planted 20 million(!) trees and counting. Delivered more than 5.5 million pounds of food to the homeless, gave 300,000 poor people 4.5 meals, feeding them for over a week. I mean sure Mr. Beast is worth 500 million(!) dollars. He’s the richest or one of the richest YouTube influencers out there. But he isn’t exactly the vapid, useless type of influencer you usually see. No, this dude delivers. Puts his money where his wide-open gaping mouth is. And yes, I respect that. But there are a lot of people who have this twisted desire to bring down others. They see someone doing good in this world and begin combing through old posts, looking for flaws… this guy infuriates the negative nancies — there’s no “dirt” to be found. Literally got famous doing dumb shit like making “counting to 100,000” videos. He’s a harmless internet person who makes a ton of money selling stupid merchandise and gives a ton of his earnings away to good causes.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some examples of true sportsmanship?
Answer: Two boxers fought a match in a low weight class. A Japanese man named Keita Kurihara and a Filipino man named Renan Portes. When the match ended, Kurihara was declared the winner “on points” despite Portes having landed some of the hardest punches in the fight. "I didn't win!" Kurihara shook his head in disbelief and broken into tears immediately after the score was read out. Afterwards, he took the microphone in the ring and bowed deeply to the audience, saying, "I was treated as the winner in the end, but I lost. It's embarrassing that I was declared the winner. I'm really sorry… My punches missed their target and I was spinning around. I got hit quite a lot. It was the worst possible situation and I was completely defeated. My countermeasures didn't work. I felt that I hadn't grown at all..” Kurihara went to the locker room after the fight and apologized to Portes, declaring him the “real winner” of the fight. The Japanese fighter wanted to win only in a convincing way, with honor. Having not landed the hardest hits and having been unable to knock down his opponent despite losing his own footing, he felt he was undeserving of victory.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is the Kennedy Family not fully behind RFK, Jr. and would rather support Joe Biden? Do they have shares in big pharma?
Answer: If you want to understand politics? Follow the money. The man below is a billionaire banking heir called Timothy Mellon. He donated 75 million dollar to a pro-Trump super PAC. He also donated 25 million dollars to RFK’s campaign at the same time.[1] In other words? The same people funding Trump are also bankrolling RFK jr.’s political campaign. There’s all sorts of conclusions one can draw from this. But the most likely explanation is that RFK serves as some sort of ‘Trojan Horse’ candidate designed to steal votes from whoever the Democratic nominee is, and help increase the likelihood of a Trump victory. I’m not sure it’ll work — the only thing “Democratic” about RFK jr. is his last name. He’s a Kennedy. But the other Kennedy’s aren’t too impressed… they see their family’s eccentric uncle who believes vaccines cause autism and who’s in bed with the Russians for what he is: a charlatan with literal worms crawling around his brain.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How often were female slaves punished?
Answer: They were punished twice over, in a sense. On the one hand, the slave literally belonged to the master, who could therefore have his way with her any time he pleased. On the other hand, the master’s wife was aware of this — and would at times be particularly cruel or unkind to the female slaves, in particular the pretty ones. Today, about 19.6 percent of African Americans are of at least 25% European ancestry — roughly the equivalent of one fully white grandparent. These statistics reveal a rather harrowing fact… the majority of enslaved women were subject to systematic rape and sexual abuse. As a result, in virtually every single African American family tree, we find a white ancestor. A foreman, a plantation owner, some passerby who fancied her. She couldn’t resist. Not even if she was already married to an enslaved man on the plantation. And yet in spite of the fact it wasn’t her choice, the mistress of the plantation would still blame her. And punish her for merely existing and being attractive. The fact that one-in-five African Americans today is at least a quarter white, is a statistic that tells a frightening tale. You cannot overstate the degree to which slaves utterly lost their dignity. Interracial marriages being illegal for most of US history until only about fifty years ago, virtually all of this white ancestry is the direct result of brutal rape.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is there nothing a human being won’t do?
Answer: In Mel Gibson’s great movie Hacksaw Ridge, Andrew Garfield plays a pacificist named Desmond Doss who went through enormous efforts in WWII in order to never pick up a gun or harm another human being — but who nonetheless managed to save the lives of many of his comrades. They had to tone down some of his heroics for the film as they were deemed ‘hard to believe’… At one point during the war, Doss was pinned down under heavy enemy fire, his arm half removed by grenade shrapnel. He had saved the lives of seventeen men at that time. Medics came and carried him away on a stretcher — the already badly damaged Doss then spotted another wounded man, worse off than him. He insisted they pick that man up instead of him; the medics ignored his protests. So Doss rolled off the stretcher. And had them pick the other man up… Desmond Doss said he’d wait. Was hit by a sniper in the other arm. Damn-near lost it. But crawled on for three hundred meters in his half-dead condition to the safety of another trench. It didn’t even make it to the film. Human beings are a beautiful species. For all our wickedness, capable of unending greatness.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Will America elect a black woman?
Answer: It depends. First things first — America is really weird about who is and isn’t “black”. Kamala Harris is the daughter of a Jamaican professor with partial black, partial white ancestry. Her mother, meanwhile, is 100% Indian. If Kamala were to take an ancestry DNA test, it would show she is, at the absolute most, about 35 to 40% black You could call her multi-racial. Or even biracial if we are to ignore the fact that her father, Donald Harris, wasn’t of fully black ancestry. But America has this odd obsession about labeling its black citizens one thing or the other. Now, can she win? It’s too early to tell. Polling isn’t that great for her, but it may pick up some steam. There will be some mental gymnastics taking place, of course — for years now, the Republicans have been pushing the “Biden is too old to run” narrative. Whereas the Democrats have been in major denial mode about Biden’s age. Now this will switch. And, perhaps, it will backfire on the Republican side. They’ve made age into this huge dealbreaker. And now, they’re stuck with the oldest nominee in American history.[1] In a hypothetical scenario where Kamala Harris remains the Democratic choice, and debates Trump? It *might* just turn the tides. She’ll say many of the same exact things Biden said in his debate with Trump. But she will say them clearly, and coherently. All the while driving home the fact that her opponent is too damn old.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What does love feel like?
Answer: It absolutely consumes me. I compose letters for her — a simple message won’t do. I want to move mountains for her. Climb them, if I need to. Dedicate books to her. Make her my muse. She’s everything. Love is an addiction. I’ve only felt it a few times. It’s always crazy intense. This girl, she has the eyes of a cat. When she is mad, she’s a demonic force. When she smiles the sun shines, my heart beats faster. When I look upon her body my desire could rip straight through my jeans like a guided missile. Suddenly there’s… hope. There wasn’t hope, before. Not like this. She’s brought it to life. Brought me to life. In the absence of her love, I was a sturdy bush — weathering storms well enough, planted firmly in the ground. Now, I’m no longer a little bush. Now, I’m a mighty oak tree. I stand upright. Now even a typhoon could not bring me down, thunder a mere tickle, the greatest tsunami a joke to me. I can deal with it all. Handle it all. Come what may. Things I felt were true before seem hollow now. Some dreams fade. Others morph, change. I change, and I change gladly. For her. I want to be like her. I want to be with her. Be there for her. Somehow, all my words are right. Like a fine musician, they hit all the right notes. It all makes sense. Every dot connected. Who am I, who was I before? I hardly know. Who do I want to be? Just a man, like any other. But better — because I’m hers. What more could I ask for? Love, what does it feel like? It feels insanely good. Like I’m drunk and high. But somehow still clear-minded. Somewhat. Suddenly, I want to be a better man. A more productive man. For her. For me. Love is great — not only do I love her, but I love myself more. After all, of nearly eight billion souls in this world… she’s chosen me.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is it true that Biden has actually decided not to run for President in the US 2024 Presidential race?
Answer: Yes, it is true. He just pulled the greatest “Uno reverse card” trick of all time… everyone said he was too old to run. Hell, even in 2020 he was already too old at 78. But now, the other guy is the old geezer. Biden just completely flipped the script. After all the talk of him being senile and done for, it’s kind of a brilliant final move, if you ask me. Every think piece, every opinion collumn in every magazine for the last months has been about how Biden is “too old to run”. Now he isn’t anymore. And the spotlight changes. If Kamala Harris truly does take over — and sticks with it — that makes her, at 59, young enough to be Trump’s daughter. Part of me still thinks she’ll be pushed out before or during the Democratic Convention, however. A convention shaping up to be an absolute circus. But that’s just me. I could be wrong. I’m frequently wrong although I *did* predict Biden would drop out following the debate. The biggest thing Trump’s allies trolled Biden with over the last few years was his age. Now, they can’t. People in retirement homes for the elderly shouldn’t show rocks, as the old saying goes. In one fell swoop, all the “old and out of touch” commentary will now switch — Sleepy Joe replaced by Sleepy Don. The game is afoot.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is President Trump the new Theodore Roosevelt?
Answer: Don’t be ridiculous. Theodore Roosevelt was a 250 pound mountain of self-made muscle who gave a speech, got shot into the chest and, spitting out blood with a smile, told the alarmed crowd: “It takes more than that to kill a bull moose!” He then proceeded to give his speech anyway as if nothing had happened. It’s the type of scene that would make people roll their eyes in an anime series and say: “Gee, those Japanese cartoons sure are over-the-top bombastic and unbelievable!” When Theodore Roosevelt was born, he was weak and sickly. Doctors said he’d surely die. His father believed otherwise. As soon as his son was old enough to understand, he told him: “God gave you a strong mind, but not a strong body. So you must build that body yourself.” He nodded and internalized that message. Started a fitness regimen of insane intensity, including calisthenics and bodyweight exercises. He climbed mountains. Fought in multiple wars. Knocked down several men at a time in bar fights, and rode horses and trekked through the roughest of terrain. His band of men was called “the Rough Riders”. About as close as a 19th century politician could be to being in a biker gang… When Theodore Roosevelt was nearly assassinated he survived with a bullet lodged in his chest for the rest of his life. It did not, in any way, shape or form, slow the man down. His very first concern, after telling the crowd he was fine, was for the would-be assassin — he told police not to rough him up too bad. If the shooter had merely nicked his ear, Roosevelt would probably have asked him to come up close and said: “Mediocre! Come, have another go!”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the historical basis of the legend of Vlad the Impaler?
Answer: He was literally a real person. Vlad the Impaler was a ruler of Wallachia from 1448 until his demise in 1477. To his enemies in Hungary, Turkey and the German countries, Vlad was an evil villain. To Romanians, he’s a national hero who stood up to powerful forces and prevailed against all odds. Vlad was, first and foremost, an insanely cruel man. His name “the impaler” refers to his greatest joy in life — to impale people. As in, to stick a sharpened piece of wood into a man (or woman’s) backside and slide it through the entire body so that it sticks out on the neck, shoulder or mouth. It would be done in such a manner to keep the victim alive as long as possible. The wooden pole would then be erected and the victim, wriggling, screaming, crying and begging for death, would be witnessed in his or her agony by passerby’s for their sick pleasure. There was a technique to impaling people, a technique perfected by Vlad — the trick was to make the stake follow the spine and not travel through other parts of the body, therefore missing vital organs. By slowly pushing along the length of the spine, a victim’s agony could be delayed for as long as, in the worst and most pitiful cases, several days. Once, just to intimidate the Turks, Vlad impaled 20,000 men in a forrest. Near every tree, a dead or dying man on a stake, as far as the eye could reach. So his enemy knew what fate awaited him. It is no wonder that legends arose of this man. He signed his letters with “Drakulya”. Or Dracula in English. He wasn’t deliberately trying to sound evil, but changing linguistics didn’t help Vlad — his father had been nicknamed “Dracul” or “the Dragon” in medieval Romanian. But in modern Romanian it means as much as “the Devil”. And to his enemies, he was exactly that.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What would happen if Joe Biden dropped out of the presidential race?
Answer: We’re about to all find out. Because he just did.[1] This Sunday, July 21, President Joe Biden dropped out of the presidential race. In a letter to the American people he stated that it had “been an honour to serve as president” but that, “in the interests of his nation, his people and his party” he had made the painful decision to no longer seek re-election. Biden is passing on the baton. It is a brave decision. Not an entirely unexpected one — he initially declared “only an act of God” could get him to step aside. Biden then softened this stance somewhat to “a medical emergency may do the trick”… and the same day he softened his stance, he was diagnosed with Covid-19. Exhibited mild symptoms, took some rest. Continued to meet with senior members of his party. And continued to hear, time and time again, that they had lost faith in his abilities. Former President Obama, a close Biden friend and ally, recently stated he felt Biden looked incredibly disoriented at a recent fundraiser.[2] Perhaps this was the final nail in Biden’s political coffin. Then again, it was one of many. Major donors began withholding donations. Allies began speaking out, even powerful and well-connected ones. And Biden’s future in Washington began looking more and more bleak and uncertain, although doubts about Kamala Harris’ popularity remain. And now, he’s dropped out. After weeks of intense speculation. The circus is about to begin, right before what will no doubt be the craziest, most intensely followed Democratic convention in all of American history. Biden is out. Who will now take over and run against Donald Trump in his place? Time will tell — but I, for one, respect the hell out of Biden for his decision.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was Cary Grant gay?
Answer: People are rather obsessed with identifying famous folks as “either this, or that”. Cary Grant wasn’t this, nor was he that — he was almost certainly both. There’s a word for this. It’s on the tip of my tongue… ah! Bisexuality. Below we see him with the actor Randolph Scott, a man Grant lived with for twelve years. Before Scott, he shared a house for six years with designer Orry-Kelly. At the same time, Cary Grant would later marry five different times, to five different women. And he fathered a daughter as well, when he was already in old age. He would later remark to friends that his secret to staying in shape was: “Doing everything in moderation… except for making love!” This makes Mr. Grant seem like a rather naughty fellow, not shy of some hanky-panky every once in a while. And not particularly particular with whom. Cary Grant came from a working class British background. Adopted his upper-class American mannerisms and sense of style through his “close friend” Randolph Scott.
