In later life, his biographer asked Grant if he’d ever been in love. “With Scott,” said the aging actor, “have you ever heard of gravity collapse? It was like that.”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is there a universal truth about money that is commonly accepted? If so, why would anyone ignore it?
Answer: One universal truth about money? It makes unattractive people suddenly attractive. Look at Harvey Weinstein below with his now ex-wife… she was an actress and model named Georgina Chapman and she was about thirty years younger than him. The couple had two daughters. Had Weinstein not been rich, would she ever have even looked his way with anything other than disgust or disdain? I mean, maybe, if he was her father or a neighbor with a heart of gold she’d have been fond of him… but attraction? Don’t count on it. But as powerful movie producer and movie mogul with hundreds of millions of dollars on the bank, she was suddenly able to overlook both his repulsive appearance as well as his repulsive behavior (he was a notorious serial rapist and this was a very badly kept secret in Hollywood)… Everyone always falls over one another backwards to make excuses for shameless golddiggers. “Oh, maybe he’s got a great personality!” No. Incredibly successful people are often rather ruthless and sociopathic on top of rather old (it frequently takes decades to truly make it to the big leagues). Money is the only thing that makes such a person attractive. Same with the “toy boys” of rich women like Cher — dollar bills in the eyes, baby. Don’t lie.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What's the future of Cuba?
Answer: Future prospects are incredibly bleak. Cuba is suffering from two major threats simultaneously — extremely low birth rates of about 1.3 child per woman and still rapidly falling. And, at the same time, a full-on exodus of epic proportions.[1] In the last two years alone, a million people have left Cuba. That’s 10% of the total population, to put things in perspective. And those are Cuban government statistics, for the record. So Cubans aren’t reproducing. Many of them are starving. And now, the youngest and most productive Cuban citizens are fleeing in overwhelming numbers. In other words, Cuba is stuck in an incredibly dire and dramatic situation. A demographic death spiral that puts Japan and China to shame. It seems the “socialist experiment” of Castro has failed, and failed spectacularly. Cuba is a failed state, falling apart at the seams, as the government attempts to put proverbial bandaids on gaping, gushing wounds, hoping no one will notice and the doctor gives the patient a clean bill of health… The history of Cuba is a sad one. One where, for decades now, people just seem united by a sinular desire — to get out, and get out as soon as possible. It’s funny to me because the other ‘top answer’ to this question by a self-described “Marxist-Leninist” from China claims Cuba’s future “looks bright”… don’t make me laugh, it’s Mad Max: Tropical Edition.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the best examples that shows Life is Unpredictable?
Answer: In 2014, Clint Eastwood started a relationship with Christina Sandera. He was 84 at the time, and Christina was 51. Eastwood had been in many relationships before and fully expected this to be his last rodeo. He was quite done with it all. Fast forward ten years, Eastwood is now 94. He and Sandera did, indeed, stay together. But now sad news was just made public by the Eastwood family — Christina Sandera died, aged 61.[1] You don’t get into a relationship in your fifties, with a man in his eighties, with the expectation that he will be the one to bury you. You probably won’t like to think much about it, but that’s not exactly the most likely outcome that’ll be on your mind… Life is incredibly unpredictable. We have expectations and we think we have a lot of certainties, but really? We don’t. We just trick ourselves for the sense of comfort into believeing we know the outcome of things ahead of times, but in actuality we never quite do.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some of the best examples of irony or nostalgia in history?
Answer: It’s the things we give up, in the name of progress. Take the picture below — swimmers in a river in Japan in the year 1915. They’re bathing. And no, there’s no electronics. The houses are largely made of wood, not awfully sturdy and perhaps not as safe as houses are today, and less comfortable. But people are alive in a way we aren’t today. A little digging and some research reveals what the same spot looks like a hundred years later — it is a residential area. The river has long since dried up, and roads now cover the places water once ran through. Not only are the people in the photograph long gone… so is the world in which they used to live. It’s every bit as dead and buried as they are. We give up a lot and call it progress. We make more money, but everything also costs more money. We have infinitely more options on how to spend our free time, and yet that free time has decreased enormously. The sky is the limit, in theory, but in practice? We waste so much of our time, and are burned out and exhausted far too much… And I look, at photographs such as that of the bathers in the river in 1915. And I experience this sense of nostalgia for an era I’ve not only never been a part of, but never will. Because that world is long gone. In a near-infinite number of ways? Life did improve. And yet we still feel that little pang of regret in our chests. This sadness. I know I do.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is racism worse in Europe than it is North America?
Answer: In 1943 there were many American troops stationed in the United Kingdom. The American army commanders insisted they be segregated. They even tried to segregate local pubs so that there would be “whites only” and “blacks only” pubs.[1] The American officers were angry when their black soldiers would fraternize with British lads and ladies, make friends and date… the Brits, however, couldn’t be arsed and didn’t care one bit. Things eventually came to a head with riots breaking out. In some insistances, British pubgoers would even come to blows with white American troops, aiding their black comrades. All throughout America at the time, Jim Crow laws were in place. Society was divided along clearly defined color lines, lines not to be crossed without severe penalties. And the Brits just weren’t having any of it.[2] That is not to say they weren’t also sometimes racist — one needed only ask their then-commander in chief, Winston Churchill, his opinion of Indians! — but the prevailing thought seemed to be “we’re all in this together, lets kick some Nazi butt”. So, no, I don’t think historically speaking we can say racism was ever “worse” in Europe than it was in America. It was there, sure. It existed. But not on the extreme level witnessed in pre-Civil Rights America, or Apartheid era South Africa. If England had been as racist as America in 1943, American officers wouldn’t have gotten beaten up by British citizens for forcing local pubs to racially segregate.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the darkest cartoon conspiracies?
Answer: There’s one theory people always seem to talk about online. It’s become somewhat of a meme, but it’s quite dark. It speculates the main character of Pokémon, Ash, is in a coma… he’s fantasizing about a magical world where he’s travelling around with his buddy Pikachu, an electrically charge mouse-like creature. He battles other magical creatures. Everything is bright and fun and every day brings another brand new adventure. Only it’s all a lie… there are no magical creatures. There are no adventures. Not for him anymore, anyway. All there is for Ash are the machines keeping him alive. Liquids going in and out of him, preventing organ failure. No one talks to him but his crying mother. Pikachu doesn’t exist — and why would he, he’s a yellow upright-walking mouse that endlessly repeats his own name… where on earth could such a ridiculous creature exist but in the fever dreams of a comatose Japanese kid who watched one too many weird anime shows? It’s kind of a cop-out. Very unfulfilling. Dark. Shows do it sometimes when a strange sequence takes place, shocking or unbelievable things happen — at the end of the episode, or at the beginning of the next, they have the main character wake up and go: “Oh, it was all just a dream, how silly!” Only in this theory, the dream now is the reality. And Ash will never leave the hospital alive to find out it is all a lie.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What’s the wildest conspiracy theory you’ve heard that someone actually believes?
Answer: Some people I know believe Mark Zuckerberg is not a real human being. But, rather, a reptillian. Cold, dead eyes. No life in them. No sparkle. No shine. The eyes of a shark, if you will. A creature risen from the depths of the primordial goo of the earth. Or, perhaps, even otherwordly. And I have to say… they make a convincing case. I mean sure he’s human. But human beings come in all shapes and sizes. And it takes all kinds of us to build and maintain this world. Ever seen “American Psycho” starring Christian Bale? Great film. Bale’s Patrick Bateman has some superficial charm. And he is, of course, infinitely better looking than Zuckerberg. But they have some things in common. The routines. The working out. Obsessions. A near superhuman focus on goals. Goals of power, goals of domination. The problem with conspiracy theories? People take a feeling, a vibe, and they take it to a far-fetched, out-of-control conclusion. Some people give us the creeps. A certain part of our brain warns us. The hair in the back of our neck stands up… often, with good reason. We find explanations outside of ourselves. Outside of this world, even. We come up with crazy conspiracy theories. Aliens. Ethereal beings. The occult. Because this allows us not to recognize ourselves in what makes us uncomfortable. It gives us an “out”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is President Trump one of the toughest men alive today?
Answer: You know who are tough? Firemen. Like Mr. Corey Comperatore who was shot and killed a week ago. He would run into burning buildings to save people’s lives. He’d get burned, he’d be covered in smoke as far as the eye could see and still would keep going. It’s one of those jobs that takes a lot out of a man. You put your life on the line, day and night, to save the lives of others. At any hour of the night the call can come — and you’ll jump out of bed and, within a minute, are on your way to the fire station. No time to rest, no time to wake up properly or contemplate the risks involved. You just, go. No hesitation. Never hesitation. Corey Comperatore was such a man. And Corey Comperatore was the man who caught the bullet meant for Donald J. Trump at his rally. You want to call the 78-year-old pampered son of a New York real estate tycoon “tough” because his ear got nicked by a sniper? A 78-year-old philandering billionaire draft dodger and a conman? Don’t make me laugh. A lion died so a worm could live.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the best country to move to if Trump wins?
Answer: It kind or reminds me of that great old Kennedy quote: “Ask not what your country can do for you, but what you can do for your country”. You’re not much of a patriot if, the minute a leader you dislike emerges, you bail on it all. The neat thing about America would be the fact that there are huge differences between states. Each state is almost like a country on itself. So if you don’t like the way things are going in your “red state” you move to a solidly “blue state”. Republican states may be emboldened by a Trump win and strip away more rights from certain groups — abortion comes to mind. But why would a Democratic state do so? No, you do have options. You always do. Still — talking about a race as if its over when it isn’t even ran, is ridiculous. You do have options. You do have choices. And chances are, even if you say you’ll move? You won’t. You have bills to pay. People that depend on you. Friends, family. Will you leave it all behind because a mean old orange man with a guinea pig for a haircut took over the White House?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why do some Presidents not get re-elected the second time around? They got elected once, they can get elected again, no?
Answer: When a President wants to be re-elected to office, the one thing he needs to do is project strength. Perception and optics are everything. In 1992 George Bush senior attended a state dinner with Japanese prime minister Kiichi Miyazawa. Bush had been feeling a little under the weather recently, and his personal physician had warned him to skip or postpone the event. Bush would have none of it — aged 68, he wanted to come across vibrand and strong. And he had to. Because the guy he was running against was 46-year-old Bill Clinton. Clinton, Arkansas governor, saxophone player, cigar-smoking womanizer. Younger than him. Stronger than him.More energetic. Bush absolutely had to come across strong, too. So he “manned up” and attended anyway. Only to throw up all over Prime Minister Kiichi Miyazawa.[1] And then pass out in Miyazawa’s lap… Needless to say, Bush lost the 1992 elections. Bill Clinton stayed in the White House for the next eight years. In politics, perception is everything. The moment sharks in the water smell even a whiff of blood, you’re done for. And politicians are nothing but human-shaped sharks in suits.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why are many people mad about student debt forgiveness?
Answer: The US appeals court just blocked Biden’s entire student debt relief plan on July 18, 2024.[1] Some people applaud this. Others are angered, and understandably so. Those who are angry about student debt forgiveness don’t understand how it works — they’re misinformed. They think it means “students won’t have to pay their student loans/fees” anymore and will be set free entirely. This is patently false. What it really does? It is designed in such a way that it allows students and graduates to make manageable payments based off their income — and pay off everything they owe without runaway interest adding to their principal as they do so. They’re still paying. Every last dime. But it is restructured in such a way to make sure debt doesn’t cripple them straight out of college. No, they won’t take the taxpayers’ money and “give it away” to the “lazy college kids”… they’ll just stop the interest rates from continuing to accumulate needlessly. Student debt forgiveness is incorrectly named — nothing is “forgiven”. No debt is removed. Everything still has to be paid. But it will be done in installments without interest continuing to rise for years. It’s a fair proposal. The people I know who are most fiercely opposed to such plans and go into segues about “taxpayer has to pay for it” and “muh immigrants!” are in 9 out of 10 cases wholly uninformed about that the plan really entails.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are there any famous hoaxes that have been disproven?
Answer: A fine and particularly distasteful example would be that of Emma Sulkowicz, who was better known as “Mattress Girl”. In 2014, prior to the rise of #MeToo, Sulkowicz claimed she was “raped” by a fellow student. She carried to campus the mattress on which the assault supposedly took place, just to prove a point because justice wasn’t done. It made for a pretty powerful visual, and a great conversation starter… The sad thing is, though? It was mostly just made up. Sulkowicz did had a sexual encounter with her supposed attacker.[1] But he was notoriously into rough sex, and she willingly supplied it, even asked for it in subsequently leaked private message. A lot of doubts arose regarding the story of “Mattress Girl”… she didn’t help remove doubts by actually creating a sex tape shortly after re-enacting the supposed rape, in order to further “raise awareness”. It was bizarre.[2] She called it an “art project” and gave it a name in French: Ceci N'est Pas Un Viol ("This is not a rape"). Because things sound more fancy in French, or something? She then did some strange public BDSM performances. Changed her pronouns to (briefly?) become non-binary. And stopped taking any and all questions regarding the supposed rape when too many holes kept getting poked in her stories. Emma Sulkowicz very likely ruined an innocent man’s life by her sick desire for the world’s attention. Mercifully, her fifteen minutes of fame are now up but my goodness was it painfully awkward...

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is one aspect of Tony Soprano (from "The Sopranos" TV show) that showcases why Tony is the perfect, most realistic sociopath in television history?
Answer: It’s in the smile. That’s where the late great James Gandolfini carried all his charm. Tony Soprano is a big kid. A huge, three hundred pound kid who does horrible, terrible things. Then talks about it with this little twinkle in his eyes. Almost innocently. Like a kid, he lies — not wanting to be found out, discovered. Not wanting to get in trouble. Like a kid, he plays games. High-stakes games. Games that could get him and the people he loves, killed. Like a kid, he endulges himself — food. Lots and lots of food. Drugs. Drinks. Women. Cars. Property. Even while shooting the show, Gandolfini got lost in bad habits. He’d eat real food on-set. And continue eating off-set. Some of his co-stars later speculated it may have led to his untimely demise… but yes. Tony Soprano acts throughout the show like a child would if you snapped your fingers and gave him a big, strong body and you took away all rules. And told him: “Go out there and have your fill… the world is your buffet, boy!” And yes, he takes that quite literally. Over, and over, and over again. He’s the ultimate hedonist. But throughout the show, he’s also warm. Fictional sociopaths always get that wrong — they make their characters cold. Sinister. Or capable of only the most superficial charm to get something done, lure someone in… truth is, people are far more complex in real life. Someone can be a horrible, self-centered asshole. Destroy lives. Break and ruin everything he touches. And STILL be incredibly likable. Still have that twinkle in their eyes. That warm smile. Tony Soprano is a horrible person. But you still kind of want to be his friend. You still believe, looking at the show, that you’d have a great time hanging out with him, if only for a night. Drinks would be on him. Food would be on him. He’d get out some big cigars, and you’d have a ball. Yes, there would be a “favor” eventually. There would be consequences. But you’d still say yes. The devil is in the details. And Tony, he’s the Devil. But only Gandolfini could make the Devil seem like a friend.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are Americans viewed as rude tourists in Europe?
Answer: An American tourist recently became a source of controversy in Florance, Italy. She rudely acted out various lewd acts on a statue of the Roman God Bachhus. Made a friend film her, and the images went viral on Italian social media… Italian citizens were outraged — they called for stricter laws to be implemented, such as the “zero tolerance” policy authorities maintain with misbehaving tourists. Foreign tourists, in particular American tourists, are rather rude in Italy. The younger generations in particular see even the most priceless of artefacts as “props” to make humorous photos or videos with. Everything is a joke to these people. They give about as much respect to 1000 year old artworks and statues than they would to a state of Mickey Mouse. “For years our government has tried to turn Florence into some sort of Disneyland to draw in more tourists,” one commentator said, “and now they’ve got exactly what they wanted.” A spokesperson for the department of tourism spoke of: “repeated manifestations of rudeness and senseless brutality”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is a famous quote of democracy by Abraham Lincoln?
Answer: Abraham Lincoln’s timeless quote on democracy goes as follows: “Democracy is a government of the people, by the people, and for the people.” It’s powerful. And to the point. A government elected by the people of a nation, that contains citizens of the nation and is there, first and foremost for the people of that nation. Powerful, and applicable pretty much universally. It is also, in many places, pretty much an illusion. Look at the weight of voters per state in America, for instance: You’ll notice that, for instance in the electoral collage, in some states a vote carries far more weight than in others. They call this system “fair” but it means, in essence, that a voter in some less-populated states has a vote that has as much influence in the outcome of the election than two or three votes in a more heavily populated state. There’s a similar divide seen in each state when we compare rural votes to city votes. Democracy is, indeed, a government “of the people, by the people, and for the people”… but it is one in which a candidate can have the support of the majority of citizens overall and still lose because to paraphrase Animal Farm, “all voters are equal but some voters are more equal than others”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are man's greatest fears?
Answer: Just the other day I read a story of the ship the Britannia, which had been sunk by the Germans in 1941. So picture this… 249 men are dead and your ship lost. You’re floating on the South Atlantic. Everywhere you look around you, you see nothing but this vast mass of water… a man named Raymond Edmund Grimani Cox, a Lieutenant, was in a small boat with some other soldiers, having survived the disaster. And then a giant arm comes out from the side of the boat. An enormous slimy tentacled arm, and another, and another… they’re several meters long, thick, and covered in huge tentacle suckers. Lieutenant Grimani Cox is grabbed by one of the monstrous arms, and left profusely bleeding even after he manages to stab it repeatedly until it lets him go. Another one of his friends isn’t so fortunate — he’s lifted in the air, then dragged kicking and screaming down in the deep with the monster. One moment he’s there, shouting, fighting for dear life… and then, he isn’t. He’s gone. The giant squid is gone, too. All that’s left is the wounded men, the battered boat and that enormous ocean, now deadly quiet… There’s hardly anything as scary in this world than the ocean, and the monsters that lurk in its deepest depths. Whales have been found with the scars of enormous squid tentacles, scars that, by their size, suggest specimens far larger than any of the creatures ever discovered and measured with human eyes. Nothing on God’s green earth frightens me more intensely.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some of the most badass last words in history?
Answer: I loved the last words of Dutch partisan and resistance fighter Willem Arondeus. Arondeus bombed the public records office of the Dutch government that contained personal, ethnic and religious information of all citizens. It was the year 1943 and the Netherlands were under Nazi occupation. The Nazis caught Arondeus and began to torture him brutally — they were very angry as burning the records had made it much harder for them to round up Jewish citizens. No matter what they did, the Gestapo could not break the 48-year-old fighter. He gave up no names, and betrayed no one. Eventually they gave up and decided to execute him. They asked Willem Arondeus if he had any last words. And Arondeus, who was openly gay, said: “Tell people that being gay does not make a man weak!” The Germans subsequently executed him. Arondeus’ lawyer, who was present, later relayed his final words to his family.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was the Civil Rights Movement "woke"?
Answer: Not one bit. Because people had very real issues back in those days. Very real reasons to fight. Just today I learned about a lady named Rosa Lemberg. She was the daughter of a Namibian woman and a British merchant, adopted at birth by a Finnish couple — she was the first black person in Finland, in fact. Lemberg was born in 1875. In Finland, she experienced no racism. She had friendships, formed relationships. Eventually she got engaged to a Russian doctor. But much to her great sadness, he took his own life just weeks before their planned wedding… heartbroken, Rosa sold all her belongings and moved to America at the turn of the century, trying to start a new life. Once in America, she discovered there was such a thing as racism… but she hated being seen as anything other than Finnish — she was a Finnish person first, her partial black ancestry didn’t come into play. Rosa Lemberg married a Finnish-American man. Was active in the Finnish community. When she died, she even died in a retirement home for Finnish-Americans… Yet when Rosa Lemberg died in 1959, she died in a country where some areas were off-limits to her because of her skin color. Something she had never experienced before in life. She should not have been forced to hide into a cocoon of other immigrants from the “old country” just to feel safe and be herself… but she was. Because the Civil Rights movements was extremely necessary as far as movements go. To call it “woke” is to belittle it.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What kind of influence does Usha Vance, JD Vance's wife, have over his career?
Answer: She’s a lawyer at a rather impressive law firm, Usha Vance. Resigned the moment her husband, J.D. Vance, was announced at Trump’s vice presidential pick for the November 2024 elections. She studied law at Yale, where she met her future husband. A woman of the world, Usha lived in Guangzhou, China for a year where she taught history.[1] Usha and J.D. were classmates and shared a professor — Amy Chua, famous as “The Tiger Mom”. An interesting lady, this Chua.[2] She’s known for pushing her daughters to perform excellently in school, no matter what. Only the highest grades would do. The most extreme example of the ‘tiger parent’ stereotype of Asian parents. And not content just running her own daughter’s lives until the most minute details, she also loved to play matchmaker for her students at Yale, as well… …and with success — she picked a winner for Usha. Writer, lawyer, marine, and now possibly the Vice President of the United States of America. The two are in an interfaith marriage — Usha remains a practicing Hindu and Vance remains a practicing Christian with neither having converted to one another’s faith. The two would be the first millennials to serve as Vice President and Second Lady.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did donald trump fake his assassination?
Answer: He has some experience in acting — he’s been quite involved in professional wrestling matches and in America, “professional wrestling” is code word for “acting”. He’s not very good at it. At acting. At faking emotion. And if there’s one thing we saw at the shooting… it’s actual emotion. The initial shot, first taken after the bullet hit? That’s arguably the most human I’ve ever seen Trump look. Ever. He’s just in a state of shock, his ears probably buzzing with the sound of the shot still ringing in his damaged ear. Political commentators and “internet experts” go back and forth on Trump a lot — some days he’s “stupid”. Other days he’s a “master manipulator who would order his own fake assassination”. You can’t be both stupid and a masterful evil genius playing 4d chess moves, always ten steps ahead of your enemies… I would speculate, personally, that the assassination showed gross incompetence on behalf of police and security detail involved in planning the event, more than anything. I would also suggest that Trump’s response in that moment was rather brilliant — he recovered from his initial shock incredibly quickly. Regained his footing, and found a way to spin the story to his advantage. Turning a moment of weakness and human frailty in one of power and defiance. His response was “too good” so now people think it’s fake.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which story in American history is hard to believe?
Answer: One story I’ve always found hard to believe is that of Lee Harvey Oswald having acted completely alone. People tend to forget that the guy defected to Soviet Russia for about a year. He renounced his citizenship, and worked for the Soviets for a while, who sent him to Minsk. Oswald went back to America because, as he wrote in his diary, he “found the work drab”. Soviet Russia was no fun. So he returned to America. How! How on earth did a US citizen defect to the Soviet Union and just… return. Like it’s no big deal. What the hell? He married a Russian wife, they have two daughters. Settle in America. Oswald, for the record, is a former marine. He’s an excellent marksman (finest in his unit) and for two years, he’s left completely undisturbed by US authorities despite having defected and worked for their enemies for a year. And, when he was just 24 years of age, he goes and — allegedly — kills President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas. It’s hard to believe an American citizen defected to the number one enemy of America in the middle of the Cold War, was allowed back to the United States without trouble, only to assassinate the president and get killed almost immediately after by a random citizen while in policy custody.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is your opinion of J.D. Vance?
Answer: Here’s what the man wrote just a few years ago — the opinion of J.D. Vance on the man whose running mate he has now become. Trump is either a “cynical asshole like Nixon who might be useful” or he’s “America’s Hitler”. Fast forward a couple of years and now Vance can be seen shaking hands with the same man, smiling, looking gleefully happy. Notice the bandage on the man’s ear, shot by another man who likely considered him “America’s Hitler”. There’s a name for the sort of man that J.D. Vance is. We call such men “shameless opportunists”. Still, the internet never forgets. Anything you throw out there is remembered, and carefully recorded. Now watch him turn himself into a million twists and turns as he applies Olympic level mental gymnastics to justify how he was “brainwashed by the evil media before”… No, he wasn’t “brainwashed”. The media didn’t trick him. J.D. Vance studied political science and philosophy. He’s a writer and a former US Marine. He’s decidedly NOT a stupid man. But he’s a shameless opportunist. It never fails to amaze me how fake people are. But I guess in today’s politics, being fake is part of the job description.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which celebrities have crazy conspiracy theories surrounding them?
Answer: The one I always see floating around is about Jamie Lee Curtis being born a hermaphrodite. People share this constantly. How she was born with both male and female genitals and how her parents had to “pick a gender” and decided to go with female… Literally the only reason people say it? She looks kinda “mannish” in the face. That’s it. That’s all. And they really get worked up when you question the theory. “But, her children are both adopted!” they will say. So what? Plenty of ‘normal’ women struggle with fertility issues. It’s no joking matter. Just because a woman adopted her children doesn’t make her a hermaphrodite. That’s insane reasoning. Why, she’s not a “real woman” because she couldn’t give birth? Preposterous. The Jamie Lee Curtis is a hermaphrodite theory is the craziest I have heard about celebrities. It’s also incredibly insensitive to other women with adopted children. Not to mention absurd because the lady is 65 years old and neither her nor anyone in her close family circle has ever made mention of this and yet the internet experts are 100% convinced.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How do you think history will judge Donald Trump's handling of the assassination attempt?
Answer: He’s the most image-conscious man alive today. Years of being in reality television has taught him well. So he knew immediately after being shot, that he could not cower. Could not appear weak. Not for even a second. So there’s that defiant fist-pump. And it’s dumb, in that moment — he’s making himself to be an even bigger target. Had there been a second shooter, this could have been a perfect time to take out Trump with a second, well-timed bullet… But he doesn’t care. He’s got the Devil’s luck and he’s completely confident that he will survive. And in that moment, all that matters to Trump? Image. So he played his cards. He wrestled against his own security team, stood up, and raised his fist. Face bloodied. Lips mouthing: “Fight! Fight! Fight!” Because he’s a fighter. He wants to be seen as one. As that Churchillian bulldog. The John Wayne. The unbendable, unbreakable, conquering hero. A man whose ego is truly larger than his sense of self-preservation. And in that moment, he was brave. Foolish, but brave. He released a statement, too. And it was remarkably measured. Calm. Not fiery, not passionate, not unhinged… but it read, for the first time in a long time, like the statement of a man who has listened to advisors. And has toned down his rhetoric somewhat. Time will tell if this will remain the case. It is known that President Joe Biden reached out to former President Trump the very same evening, and that the two men talked. Biden’s team even pulled some of the strongest anti-Trump ads off the television. It was a remarkable show of (relative) unity in a divided country. One that caught me by surprise to tell you the truth. What will history remember? It depends entirely on how the next days and weeks play out. Goodwill won is lost easily with a few ill-timed statements or actions. Trump could use the attack to his benefit in the campaign. And the Democrats, meanwhile, will keep hammering the fact that the shooter was a registered Republican gun-nut who used the same automatic assault rifle their party had wanted to ban for civilian use… which narrative will win? We’ll find out on November. Now, to use Trump’s own words after a school shooting in Iowa six months prior: “Get over it!”[1]

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is there an actor or actress that is widely loved but you personally dislike their acting? What makes you feel this way about them?
Answer: Let me throw in something pretty controversial… Keanu Reeves is barely better as an actor than Steven Seagal. He’s stiff, wooden, and he always just plays some cool-dude version of himself. The difference between Keanu and other stiff, one-dimensional actors like Seagal, is that Keanu is infinitely more likable as a person. People feel (rightfully so) that he deserves his fame because he’s just such a chill dude. He’s also handsome, like a multi-racial Jesus mixed with an easy-going surfer. But yeah, as much as I enjoyed the John Wick films, or the Matrix trilogy… he’s just not all that great as an actor. He’s not very versatile. And at times his delivery is kinda lousy, and bland. His voice kinda flat, not conveying much if any emotion. You don’t really tune in to Keanu to watch Oscar-winning performances — he doesn’t have that in him. No gut-wrenching monologues from this guy. Just “imma shoot up 1 million Russian mafia dudes because one of them killed my dog” type of films. Turn off your brain. Enjoy. And whatch what is essentially the human equivalent of a cardboard cutout of a handsome man on your screen as he competently but uninspiredly entertains you for 90 minutes or so. Keanu Reeves is a chill dude. He is by all accounts enormously friendly and generous in real life. But his acting is rather lousy and robotic, like an AI-generated animation more than a person of flesh and blood. He has the presence, the physicality, the looks… but can’t really sell me on the lines. Even Schwarzenegger in his eternal thick Austrian accent puts more emotion in his lines than Keanu ever does.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why would a registered Republican shoot Trump?
Answer: Not every Republican is pro-Trump. There are also “never-Trump Republicans”. They are right-leaning but find Donald Trump to be a nasty caricature of their party. Some consider him a RINO (Republican In Name Only). Because for many years, Trump was a registered Democrat. I still remember the photos, some twenty years ago. Trump had just gotten married to Melania. And at the wedding, who were prominent guests? Bill and Hillary Clinton. Smiling, joking, having the time of their lives with Donald and Melania. And sure, many Republicans today love Trump. But there are also those with long memories. Who have a distaste for fake people, lying to your face and denying their own past with gusto. They know the circles Trump used to run in. The Clintons. Epstein.[1] And they don’t buy his denials, they don’t buy his excuses… and find him a grotesque and distasteful individual. Some even outright hate him. The countless affairs, and how he bragged about him. The allegations of sexual misconduct, some of it with minors. Whether true or not, some are bound to believe it. You often hear about the deranged people on “the other side”, with their TDS (Trump Derangement Syndrome). They can’t stop talking about how wicked and awful the guy is… sure, those exist. But never underestimate the passionate white-hot hatred of a true believer. It is far more powerful than the hatred of someone who was never in his camp to begin with. Because for the true believer, the hatred is marinated in genuine disappointment — they wanted, hoped for and expected so much more from “their guy”. Disappointment, desillusionment, slowly morphing into hatred… No, if you’re a genuine Republican. A fierce and passionate one? You may just hate Trump even more for how he’s turned your party into a shadow of its former self. How he’s packed the ranks of the RNC with yes-men, clapping dutifully along with eyes glued to his puffy orange face. The party of Abraham Lincoln. The party of Ronald Reagan. Such a man may buy an assault rifle at age 20 — a year before he can legally drink. And try to kill what he saw as “the enemy from within”… it’s really not hard to imagine.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What do voting records reveal about Thomas Matthew Crooks, the 20-year-old man who attempted to assassinate Donald Trump?
Answer: They reveal that Thomas Matthew Crooks was a registered Republican. The picture below shows Mr. Crooks mere seconds before a sniper blew up his skull with a shot to the head. He lived just barely long enough to know he missed Trump and failed to assassinate him. Crooks is a bit of a mixed bag, politically — he appears to have been a registered Republican. But he also donated to Democratic causes as well. At the same time, he held white supremacist beliefs. So he’s kind of hard to figure out. What to make of the guy’s political leanings? A bit of a mixed bag. Right-wing in some areas, left-wing in other areas. He came from a conservative area, and was born into a conservative family. And politically he was all over the place. A confused young man who may have wanted to “save” his country from Trump. And by his deed (and lousy aim) only made a Trump victory more likely. Thomas Matthew Crooks was neither this, nor that. He appears to have been a rather miserable individual, and a lone wolf. He had some personal hatred for Trump, but on what grounds we do not know. And with his brain splattered into a million pieces, he won’t ever tell us his motivation. I doubt it’s an “inside job” as some conspiracy theorists claim — the CIA has far better aim.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What do you think of the assassination attempt on former President Donald J. Trump?
Answer: More than anything, I feel like this is the moment we watched Donald Trump win the 2024 elections. The mugshot after his arrest already went viral. But the picture of him with a bloody ear, holding up a fist in defiance as his secret service agents rush him off stage to safety? That’s downright iconic. Iconic photos win elections. Drama. And above all — the newly enforced civility. Because no one on the other side of the aisle wants to be accused of “fanning the flames” or “creating an atmosphere of hatred”. It’s bad optics. Trump will ride this one out like a champion. Because he’s fine, physically. A bullet grazed his ear and he no doubt had the fright of a lifetime. But he’s alive and well according to all reports. And he can now paint, with much more accuracy, his political opponents as extremists and radicals. He can, and he will. What do I, personally, think? I’ll spare you the theatrics, the “thoughts and prayers” and empty-hearted half-assed handwringing. I just think it’s a historical moment that very likely decided the outcome of the 2024 presidential election, because it made it next-to impossible to “go hard” after Trump. I fully expect more unhinged rallies, heavier protection of venues and another seismic shift in the polls.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Were the real native Americans black?
Answer: You need only look at photographs of pure-blooded Native Americans from the 19th century and tell me how “black” they look. You’ll find that they are people of primarily Asian admixture, who have moved to the Americas tens of thousands of years ago. Their closest relatives alive today are found in Siberia. Now let us compare some Native American tribesmen to a Siberian native tribesmen on the photo below. Some of the beads and ornaments are similar in both people. Some of the facial features are, too. The Siberian natives are somewhat shorter-limbed and paler-skinned, as they live in a colder climate. The Native Americans are a bit more darker-skinned, due to the warmer temperatures of the Americas. They have pointier noses and sharper features, too. This is the thing, though… people adapt to their surroundings. The way Nepali mountaineers developed much greater lung capacity than those who lived in the lowlands. And the way some tribes of Indonesian and Filipino fishermen developed over time the ability to hold their breath longer than anyone else alive, in order to dive for pearls more effectively and fish in the deep of the ocean. Travel Asia and you will notice that there are very dark and very pale people. Part of this is genetic, part of this lifestyle — a Chinese accountant living in the city will be more pale-skinned than a farmer living in a rural community, whose skin may be quite dark. The same would be true in India, Malaysia, Indonesia. Native Americans weren’t “black”, but some of them were very dark-skinned because Asian people have more melanin in their skin and can get a very dark tan without getting noticeably sunburned the way a European person would.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Should everyone be given forgiveness?
Answer: No. Some people are too far gone and do things that are too wicked for there to ever be forgiveness or redemption of any kind. Child molesters, for example. What good is there in such a person, and what good is there in keeping them alive a minute longer? Forgiveness is a beautiful thing. I’m all about forgiveness. I can forgive just about anything. Stealing can be done out of hunger. Theft can be forgiven, so can cheating when one is sincerely sorry — that doesn’t mean the relationship itself can be salvaged, but you can forgive former partners and be on good terms with in spite of what led to your breakup. Life’s too short to hold grudges. Even a killing, when done in self-defense, can be forgiven. But not kiddie-fiddling. That’s where I draw the line, personally. Most of society does, in fact — if you were to lynch your local pedophile, no one would care all that much. Most people would even applaud you for it.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What recent news story has affected you the most?
Answer: I’m baffled by the amount of decadence of the ultra-rich. Below we see Anant Ambani and his wife at a pre-wedding dinner. They’re joined by Justin Bieber. They put down millions of dollars just to have Bieber at their dinner party. There are countless celebrities expected at the actual celebrations. The total cost of the wedding is estimated to be between 11 billion to 13 billion rupees, or rather, 132 to 156 million dollar… It’s obscene. The amount of money wasted on this nonsense. The obsession of people, salivating at their mouths at the grandeur of others they’ll never taste, experience or feel. The glory they’ll never share, the success they’re no part of and never will be. All over the world there are people struggling to put food on the table. People struggling to feed their kids. Fathers and mothers who go to bed hungry because they rather suffer than watch their kids suffer… I once gave a poor old man ten bucks to buy glasses — he never had glasses before despite needing them. He cried. The whole circus is an almost surreal parasocial exercise in “living vicariously through others”. Many in the general public defend the outrageous extravagance, and so so passionately.[1] I fully expect them to show up in this answer’s comment section, excusing the moon-sized ego of these people showcasing their opulence for all the world to see. To be marveled at and admired like Gods come down to earth as they get the government(!) to block roads for their limousines and wedding parades. These fuckers throw over 130 million dollars away on a party. Because they want Justin Bieber to eat dinner with them and serenade them as they shovel caviar into their fat mouths and wash it away with the fanciest of champagnes. All because they want to show off how good they have it. Our world once had Kings and Queens, Emperors and Empresses. And some lost their heads, others their thrones and now we delude ourselves into thinking they’re gone. But they’re still here. The new nobility is called billionaires.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why do people care about celebrities lives and go to war for them on the Internet and in real life instead of living their own life, and maybe doing something that’ll make them a celebrity?
Answer: Because people have this tendency to live vicariously through others. The same energy that causes people to obsess over celebrities and sports teams, is the energy that motivates “helicopter parents” screaming at their children for having grades that aren’t high enough… the parent failed. His or her parents weren’t good enough. So now the child must succeed. So that some of the child’s success will rub off on the parents, and they’re receive praise for raising a “successful child”. It’s the same with celebrities… you may never be a billionaire in your twenties. But if Kylie Jenner does, and you can contribute to it by buying her makeup products, you’re kind of “part of it”. Your brain tricks you into believing you’re instrumental in the success of the celebrity. You watch the movies, play the music. Now you’re part of it. You are the celebrity. The celebrity’s success is yours. Their failings, yours. You obsess. In some misguided believe that the glory achieved by your heroes will, one day, be yours… Then you grow up. And instead of obsessing over celebrities, politicians or athletes, you obsess over your children. Their success is yours. Their failure is yours. Only the highest grades, the best schools, the highest income will do. Because you’re a loser — living through others is the prevailing mindset of losers the world over. It’s an admission of “it’s over for me… so I’ll just obsess over those who still have a shot.”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the worst cases of racism, bigotry, and sexism in history and the writing or presentation of world history?
Answer: The last full-blooded Tasmian Aboriginal man, William Lanne, died in 1869. A certain doctor named William Crowther asked permission to examine and dissect the body — this wasn’t granted. So Crowther simply broke into the hospital and began cutting away, anyway. For this he faced zero repercussions, as Lanne was seen as “barely human” by most locals. Doctor Crowther cut off Lanne’s hands, and cut off his feet. Extracted his bones and did so in a rough manner. He cut off his genitals, which he declared as “like those of an animal” — he famously fashioned the scrotum of Lanne into either a wallet or a tobacco pouch. He then took out the brain… and said it “looked remarkably like the brain of a white man” which surprised him. Crowther came up with a theory for this… “the brains of the lesser races will, when raised among the higher races, morph into theirs.” Lanne had been raised in an orphanage alongside white children, which is why Crowther said he could not find “abnormalities in the brain” the way he had expected. There’s this scene in Django Unchained where DiCaprio’s racist slave-owner character breaks apart a skull to show how it is “servile” in shape. It’s a great scene and an entertaining one. What’s weird is how shockingly accurate it is for 19th century attitudes towards race — the brains, bodies and skin of “other” races were, indeed, nothing but a curiosity to scientists and doctors… Years later, William Lanne’s common-law wife Truganini died as well. She begged to be buried, traumatized by what had happened to her former partner. And she was, initially, buried. Only to be dug up again, examined and having her body displayed in public until the 1940s. Racist 19th century scientists were the absolute worst.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What video game music (or any music) goes hard in your opinion?
Answer: Right now, more than anything… Ummet Ozcan. Mongolian throatsinging, remixed. In the lingo of today’s young folks, it definitely “goes hard”. Like holy shit this stuff is so incredibly catchy, I love it: There’s something about this type of song that really stirs the blood. It gets you up and going. I immediately dropped to my knees and did thirty push-ups. It’s like a testosterone injection through the ears. Cannot recommend this stuff enough. My typical workout routine nowadays — Mongolian throat-singing remixes and push-ups, pull-ups, sit-ups. Everything you do becomes more awesome, more powerful, more impactful with this. Like how any movie needs a fine soundtrack, so do our lives. Make it one to dominate. So you dominate whatever you do.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: George Clooney urges Biden to step aside or he'll lose, saying he's clearly declined. Why do other Democrats deny Biden's clear decline?
Answer: People are quick dismiss George Clooney as “just an actor”. Who cares for what a Hollywood star says? But he IS kind of a big deal — Clooney, just in June 2024 alone, raised 30 million dollars for Joe Biden in fundraisers. He’s invested, personally, in a Biden victory. And now he no longer believes it can happen. He urged Biden to step down in an opinion piece. Then yesterday, Biden had another painful gaffe, Biden helped drive Clooney’s point home when he introduced Ukrainian president Zelensky as: “Ladies and gentlemen… President Putin!” Holy shit. That’s a bad one. George Clooney’s opinion piece is particularly interesting because top Democrats are gaslighting the public, lying through their teeth that Biden was “just jetlagged” or that he “had a cold” at the debate… but Clooney went out and said, and this is significant: "It's devastating to say it, but the Joe Biden I was with three weeks ago at the fund-raiser was not the Joe 'big F-ing deal' Biden of 2010. He wasn't even the Joe Biden of 2020. He was the same man we all witnessed at the debate." Our eyes do not deceive it. No more bullshit excuses — it’s time for the man to retire if his party wants to hold on to power. Or go elect Trump, abandon your allies and present Putin with Ukraine on a silver platter.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some of the most bizarre coincidences you have found?
Answer: In 2007, a photoshoot was taken in Spain — football legend Lionel Messi was given a baby to hold. It was some sort of charity event, for UNICEF. The baby Messi was holding was the child of teenaged refugees that had fled their country for a better life in Spain. Fast forward 16 years and the baby is now a young man. And like the man who held him during the photoshoot, he has become a great footballer himself. Aged only sixteen, he now plays for the Spanish national team. His name? Lamine Yamal. Lamine Yamal is a phenomenon. He’s still two years shy of adulthood and already scored for his team in major games. In a few days he’ll play the finals of the European Championship football. Sixteen years ago, when he was a baby in Messi’s arms, no one could have predicted this coincidence. But it’s a remarkable one.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are your thoughts on "Project 2025"? Is it something we shouldn't worry about and should just disregard, or something that warrants talking about?
Answer: A few years ago, during the George Floyd protests, I heard a lot of activists on the left shouting: “Defund the police!” or even “abolish the police!” and of course, like most other sane people, I shook my head… Project 2025 is kind of like the extremist right-wing cousin of those goons wanting to defund or abolish the police. The Heritage Foundation, the think tank behind it, wants to abolish the department of education, among other ridiculous proposals. The foundation behind the project isn’t new… it’s been around for decades. This is the group that got Ronald Reagan elected, to name one famous example of the type of man and the type of policies they’re after — someone charismatic who will rubber-stamp whatever they come up with. Donald Trump denies he’s involved with Project 2025. Of course he would… but he’s copying a lot of the lingo. LIke his bizarre little tangent on the CNN presidential debate where he claimed Democrats want “post-birth abortions”… Project 2025, just to be on the safe side of things, wants NO abortions at all. Project 2025 leader Kevin Roberts recently said he wants “a new American revolution”. He also said it will be bloodless. But “only if the left allows it to be”.[1] How on earth does this not sound incredibly ominous? Trump was perfectly fine adopting many of Project 2025’s talking points until very recently. Was perfectly okay with the Heritage Foundation’s continued support for his candidacy. It is only now that he’s discovered the whole thing may be his Kryptonite that he’s started backing down, downplaying, even weakly disavowing the whole thing… You could believe his words, of course. If you’re gullible and naive, that is — the man is a notorious liar. Fact remains, Project 2025 wants to reclassify virtually all government jobs as “political appointees” and replace the whole government apparatus with loyalists and yes-men. And then do whatever it takes to turn back the clock to, say, 1925-ish. If you don’t like the sound of that then, yes, you should probably be worried.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What aspect of society scares you the most?
Answer: Just how incredibly rapidly progress can be lost. In the picture below, we see a woman cutting a birthday cake. She’s not a Western woman — she’s Iranian. It is the year 1973, five years before the Islamic Revolution. Her clothes are somewhat revealing, her legs bare, her hair freely shown… Five years later, the woman would be forced to cover he hair. Cover her legs, her arms, her cleavage. She would lose many of the rights she no doubt felt would be hers for life, as she cut that birthday cake five years prior, free of concerns, not a worry in the world… there are people, right now, even in the West, who want this type of future.[1] Women in the kitchen. Covered up. Stripped of their rights. Life returned to the state it was in fifty, sixty, seventy years ago. We always take for granted, the rights we have. Or whine we don’t have enough of them. What we forget is that any right any of us have, anywhere, is hard-won. Was fought over, suffered for, demanded and taken, never given. And with one snap of the finger… all can be lost. Don’t get too comfortable.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is an example of a recent archeological discovery that has caused controversy among scholars?
Answer: The famous Hasanlu Lovers of Iran. These two skeletons were discovered in the 1970s in what appeared to be an intimate embrace — they seemed to be kissing. The city of Hasanlu was destroyed by an invader, as of yet unidentified. Inhabitants of the city were killed on the spot. And this couple shared a final kiss, it appears, from the way the bones are positioned. Archeologists dubbed them “lovers”. It was assumed right away that the skeletons must be male and female. But when subsequent testing of the bones revealed both skeletons were likely male, the story changed all of a sudden… historians fell over backwards to explain that the bones were probably just “randomly placed that way” because SURELY they couldn’t be — oh shock of shocks! — gay, could they? The Hasanlu Lovers are an enduring mystery. When first discovered, everyone immediately dubbed them lovers, a couple, embracing one final time before death. But they’re two dudes. So that couldn’t possibly be the case, could it? Surely no Ancient Iranians could be of the homosexual persuasion, could they? It’s funny how quickly the story changed.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why are leftists so angry about Project 2025? The way I see it, it will eliminate corruption and put America back on the right track. Are leftists just afraid they will lose their grip on power?
Answer: They aren’t angry… they’re scared. Project 2025 is a collection of proposals by the “Heritage Foundation”, a conservative far-right think tank. It seeks to do many of the things right-wing politicians and the billionaires backing them have wanted to do for decades. Only it is far more organized than ever before. Project 2025 believes “cultural marxism” has infiltrated the school system. To rectify this, it seeks to abolish the department of education altogether. Project 2025 wants to stop the “LGBT propaganda” in schools. Teach children that family values are most important, that morality matters and that there are only two genders — male and female. It places God at the center of the world, back into houses and classrooms. It promotes traditional values. But it does something else. Something other conservative think tanks never managed to do… Project 2025 made a list of potential public servants and judges to be appointed. Tens of thousands of possible candidates. And it seeks to replace the entire government with loyalists, if Trump wins in 2024. Meaning that NO candidate who isn’t fully on board with extremely conservative Evangelical christianity could ever be appointed to so much as sweep the floor in a post-2025 government. America has long had a tradition of “picking the best man/woman for the job”. At least there was this illusion of impartiality. Project 2025 pulled off the mask, and stopped pretending — it wants the government to be filled and ran, top to bottom, with yes-men who will rubber-stamp and sign any proposal put before it. This, combined with a Supreme Court that already leans far to the right and presidential powers and immunity greatly enhanced, will essentially turn America into a Christian nationalist theocracy.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who is an actor or actress that you find physically unattractive but is still successful due to their acting skills?
Answer: The man himself, Steve Buscemi. He’s an awesome dude, and an amazing actor in spite of looking like some unholy cross between a reanimated bog body and Gollum. I love everything I’ve seen Mr. Buscemi in, so far. He was amazing on Boardwalk Empire. Loved him in the Sopranos. He makes even the smallest parts memorable. On top of this, he’s a firefighter as well. Was well for a long time before even making it as an actor. And during the terrorist attack on 9/11, he donned his old firefighter attire and worked on the line, right in the center of it all going down. He’s a brave man. He’s a genuinely good guy. And he’s donated millions to firefighter causes post 9/11 as well. But yeah, he’s also rather… unique looking. Those huge blue bug eyes. His expressive face a perpetual meme no matter what he says or does. I love this man, he’s easily one of the best dudes in the business. But that face! If you didn’t know he was such a chill guy, you would NOT want to run into him in a dark alley.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are your favorite historical conspiracy theories?
Answer: Won’t do something boring here like “moon landing is fake” or the earth being secretly frisbee-shaped… no, how about the history of the kilt, a far more funny tale? I once read that the traditional Scottish skirt-for-males wasn’t worn all that much until around the 19th century. Along comes Queen Victoria. And she insists on men wearing a kilt. She’s unusually fond of it. Because Queen Victoria is kind of a naughty lady at heart — her husband Prince Albert and her had a whole bunch of kids and the “Prince Albert piercing” is famously named after him. Now this is something I just ready, somewhere, long ago. But it’s just too funny to me not to share it. I choose to believe it, because it cracks me up. Anyway, as the ‘conspiracy theory’ goes, Queen Victoria popularized the kilt. Not just that, she insisted on it being worn without underwear. So she could, at times, get a glimpse of men’s dangly bits. Queen Victoria, inspite of all the puritanism the age named after her is known for, was quite a mischievous lady!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can any politician or political leader in America be fully trusted?
Answer: Depends on the man. I wouldn’t let either Biden or Trump babysit my daughters, for example. Not to mention Bill Clinton — not in a million years. But Jimmy Carter, or Bernie Sanders? Probably. They just don’t strike me as perverts. Call it intuition. Some people are good eggs, and some people are bad eggs. And some people are capable. And others aren’t. As a rule, though, it’s wise to trust politicians about as far as you can throw them. You can count the good ones on one hand. Full trust is for solid marriages, for life partners and guard dogs. For brothers-in-arms and chosen family. For best friends and comrades you’ve been through hell and back with, and for. And who you know, deep inside your heart, would do the same for you. Politicians? Don’t make me laugh. They’re the most narcissistic peopel around — everything they do is measured, calculated for maximum effect. No good deed they ever do is unreported, no bad deed without a spin. They crave attention, and they love the sound of their own voices. Even the good ones are kinda shitty on a personal level. Oh and this isn’t just an American thing, please get real. You think politicians in Europe are more trustworthy, or in China, or Africa or Latina America? Don’t make me laugh. If you fully trust a politician, any of them, then you’re just gullible and naive. But do ask yourself — which politician would you trust with your wife or children when you’re not around?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was Hitler really 5.9" tall?
Answer: Yes, he was. People like to pretend he was much smaller, or that he was a weak or boring guy who couldn’t get laid or whatever, but that’s just a coping mechanism from people who feel compelled to demean Hitler from the great beyond. Below, we see him with Paul von Hindenburg. Von Hindenburg was a very tall man for his era and stood about 6′4″ in his prime. In the photo above, he likely lost some height — Von Hindenburg is, after all, already in his eighties and by the time we reach our eighties, we have typically lost a few inches of height. And while Hitler is noticeably shorter, he’s not that much shorter. Looking at the height of both men’s shoulders, the height difference is at best a few inches. I’d say Hitler was definitely around 5′9″, at least at this point in life. By the time he died he was stooped over, feeble from bad medications and Parkinson’s disease and likely a bit shorter, maybe around 5′8″ or even as short as 5′7″. I’d say Adolf Hitler was about 5′9″ at his peak. Not a tall man, but not a short man for his era, either. Mao was about 5′11″ in his prime. The whole “dictators are tiny insecure men” spiel is kind of… bullshit. Julius Caesar was a tall man, even Napoleon was perfectly average for his era. It’s silly to try and reduce people to stereotypes like “haha he was a gay midget with one testicle”. Doesn’t help anyone.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you provide some examples of cyclical events in human civilization?
Answer: A leader starts a war. His country performs badly. Loses international prestige. Eventually, the leader loses power. And, ultimately, his head. Below we see a picture of Vladimir Putin. Behind him, the stern gaze of Tsar Nicholas II. Nicholas couldn’t defeat Japan. Couldn’t cut it in WWI, either. History has deemed him a loser. And for this he met a gruesome fate. Likewise, Putin started a war he felt he could easily win. Take Kiev, Blitzkrieg-style. A “decapitation strike”, causing the government to flee and enemy lands to quickly fall into his hands. We all know this did NOT happen. Things didn’t go his way. So, two-and-a-half years into the war, Putin has captured less than 20% of Ukrainian territory. An abysmal result. The areas he did capture, are largely reduced to rubble and he can’t even afford to rebuild them. Now he’s resorting to acts of terrorism, like bombing a children’s hospital. Regular tactics clearly no longer work, and he’s running out of men, having to beg for ammo and manpower in North-Korea of all places… Tsar Nicholas II looks down on Putin. Perhaps with a bit of a wry smile — he sees Russia’s new Tsar, and he sees him failing utterly. As is tradition. As Mark Twain said: “History does not repeat itself, but it often rhymes.”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: I want Hezbollah to win the war against Israel and occupy the land. What should I do?
Answer: Instead of joining Hezbollah, like a loser, join Hasbulla, like a King. Hasbulla is a cool dude. He’s a dwarf from Dagestan, Russia, and he’s friends with all the major fighters in the area. And he’s not dreaming of destroying Israel and driving the Jews into the sea like the losers of Hezbollah… Hasbulla is too busy beefing with other midgets, chilling with Tyson, play-sparring with Khabib Nurmagomedov… Don’t join Hezbollah — join Hasbulla. Instead of shooting rockets into residential areas like a coward, spar with hardcore Dagestani fighters. Drink vodka. Fight other dwarfs. Use your tiny fists and your adorable grumpy face to win the hearts and minds of the world… not terrorism.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the benefits of facial recognition?
Answer: A lesbian dating app made headlines in June 2024 for using facial recognition software to exclude transgender women.[1] There had been an issue with women using the app complaining about transgender (male-to-female) women chatting them up, sometimes refusing to disclose their status as former men. The dating app claims to be able to “clock” a male-to-female transgender with supposedly 100% certainty. I suppose this would count as a benefit — it makes it harder for people to hide the truth from others. I can only hope the same software will soon be applied to those who use filters, or makeup. And show the “real you” even when you try desperately to hide it. To prevent disappointment, people really should be straight-forward about this sort of thing. As in all things, honesty is the best policy. Too many people hide who they truly are — their gender, the appearance, what their actual face looks like without makeup, or they hide their weight by posting old photos or photos that are neck-up only. When it comes to dating and online catfishes, AI might just save the day!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some of the greatest examples of the Horseshoe Theory?
Answer: In the year 1939, Hitler and Stalin agreed to attack Poland together — the Nazis took the Western part, the Soviets the Eastern part. Victory parades were then held in Poland. Joint parades, in which “victory arches” were carried, like the one seen below. Adorned with both the Communist “hammer and sickle” logo and the Nazi swastika. People like to pretend, now, out of some sort of historical revisionism or perhaps a coping mechanism of sorts, that Hitler was the sole bad guy of WWII. He started it all, planned it all, it’s all his doing. Stalin, every bit as murderous and cruel, was “rebranded” during the war as “Uncle Joe”, and became (briefly) an ally to the West. What we often forget is that he, too, started the war. The greatest example of “horseshoe theory” (the theory that the far-left and far-right are uncomfortably close together, touching almost like a horseshoe) are these victory parades… Nazis and Soviets, marching arm in arm under the same banner. Russia does NOT like to be reminded of this. So I say, lets remind them some more as they excuse their war on Ukraine as a “denazification campaign”. What’s that about those living in glass houses?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the story of American history?
Answer: A single gravestone tells it all. The man buried here was called Stacey A. Stewart and he died in WWII, aged only twenty. Stewart had enlisted in the American army at an early age. He gave his life for his country, a gunshot wound to the belly taking him out as a young man in full bloom of his life in Assam, India. Shipped away far from home, to a place he’d never been, returning in a box. The remarkable thing is Mr. Stewart’s backstory — his great-grandfather was none other than Chief Sitting Bull. The same Chief Sitting Bull who fought so very tirelessly against the United States Army. The same Chief Sitting Bull who was KILLED by the United States Army in 1890… and then, fifty years later, his own great-grandson gave his life for that same country, after joining that same army… That’s the “story of American history”. It’s in the gravestones. Among the descendants of Chief Sitting Bull we find men who fought in WWI, in WWII, and in Vietnam. And yes, some of them died. Died for the very country that killed their ancestors. American history is built by family trees and carved on gravestones.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What actor/actress is easy to love?
Answer: There’s something about a man like Jack Black. It must be freeing to be so unapologetically yourself, all the times. The man doesn’t give a shit. Yes, he’s fat. He has a beard like Karl Marx just had a baby with a Bronze Age cavewoman and it was raised in the mean streets of Moscow. And he doesn’t care. He just doesn’t. At no point does the guy pretend to be better than he is, more than he is. It’s just a vibe, I suppose. An aura. There are men who have to do a ton of charity stuff to be liked, to come across as likable, wonderful. People who have to make real effort to be seen a certain way… and it just kind of happens, with Jack Black. He walks into a room and you’re entertained. Instantly. He’s not a dumb guy. Could have been anything. He’s a musician, he’s an actor. His mother was literally in NASA and created the guidance system that saved the Apollo 13 astronauts. But he won’t brag about it. Won’t brag about a damn thing. No, he’ll just crack jokes at his own expense. Be his worst or his finest self. It’s a quality I also see in men like Danny DeVito. Jack Black’s kinda like DeVito, only 3D-printed to 1.3 times the size of the former. It’s to love a guy like Jack Black. Sometimes he’s a little “too much” but, I don’t know. He just sort of makes me happy. I’m glad he exists in this world. Puts a smile on my face that he’s here.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the coolest historical photo you've seen?
Answer: It’s a photograph taken in 1954. Pakistan’s Prime Minister Mohammad Ali Bogra was in Cut Bank, Montana, smoking a peace pipe with Blackfoot Chief Theodore Last Star. Eastern leaders, from India, to Pakistan and even Iran, had a bit of a fascination with Native American culture, with cowboy stories and with the stories of unbroken tribes, refusing to bend the knee to their overlords in Washington. At some point, even the Shah of Iran invited a Native American chief to celebrate his birthday, back in 1971.[1] This particular chief caused somewhat of a stir when, unaware of court protocol, he asked the Shah to “stand with him in brotherhood” as he delivered his speech. The speech was then cut short — the Shah, as it just so happened, was NEVER asked to stand up for anyone. Such a request had not been made in 2500 years. Chief Earl Old Person, however, had asked him to. And yes that was his literal name… Chief Earl Old Person. It’s amazing. Just as far as visuals are concerned, however, nothing quite beats the photograph of Mohammad Ali Bogra smoking a peace pipe with Chief Lone Star. Squint your eyes and, amidst the smoke, Bogra and Lone Star are brothers of one tribe. In a sense, the descendants of America’s first rulers and the rulers of the newly free post-colonial world were kindred spirits… born worlds apart and yet both, for most of their lives, oppressed by the same powers that be.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who do you think is or was the most bizarre person in the world?
Answer: Perhaps not the most bizarre, but definitely a wonderfully eccentric contender to the title… a Japanese general by the name of Count Nagaoka Gaishi. Gaishi was known as a great military leader, some having dubbed him the “father of Japanese aviation”. Above all, he was known for his enormous moustache — it was reportedly the largest moustache not only in the Japanese imperial army, but in all of the world. In 1933, Gaishi did the very thing that all men must one day do — he died, aged 74. Bladder cancer did the magnificently moustachio’d generalissmo in. The family got together and decided to take a rather unusual step; they built not one, but two graves. In one grave on the traditional burial mound, his family buried the old general. His eldest son then carefully removed the count’s enormous moustache with clippers. And the moustache was buried in another grave, nearby.[1] One of Count Gaishi’s graves, above. One contained his ashes — he was cremated, as per his wishes. The other contains a smaller casket with, in it, the mighty ‘stache. It is wrapped in white silk for posterity. Those who wish to pay hommage to the greatest moustache of Japanese history but refuse to honor its military, may travel to Fujiyama and do so.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did Tsar Nicolas II deserve his fate during the Russian Revolution of 1917?
Answer: Had the Soviets properly put Tsar Nicholas II on trial and executed him after, they may have had a point. But they didn’t… they bayonetted and shot to death the Tsar. And not just the Tsar, but also his children. There really is no excuse for this. Just, look at them. They’re adorable. What sort of absolute animals would shoot, stab and bludgeon to death a whole family just because their father happened to be head of state of a rather repressive state? It’s the kind of historical cruelty that simply boggles the mind. People always repeat the same old mantra… “Orders are orders!” they say. And sure, orders are orders. But does that justify anything, really? I can definitely see how a revolution may take place, and the former leaders of the country are put on trial and executed. Allowing the nation to start anew with a clean slate. But the children? Such needless brutality. It is unforgivable. The argument that “the Romanovs may have rallied in exile and tried to return!” is nonsense, too — many dynasties have fallen, and its members were allowed to live. The Last Emperor of China, Puyi, was allowed to live out his days as a simple gardener in Communist China. The state used this forgiveness towards him as a propaganda tool. Tsar Nicholas II wasn’t a bad man, as far as monarchs in his era go. He was far less militaristic than the Kaiser, for instance, who loved the army to almost fetishistic levels. In some ways, Nicholas was even a reformer. The Soviets could have allowed the man into exile. Or could have even kept him around and tried to use him and his family as propaganda tools, the way the Chinese later did with Puyi. Brutal murder was the most stupid and short-sighted “solution” to the Romanov problem.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is the word "Naqba" when used in reference to Palestinian history considered offensive by some?
Answer: It’s the day the Palestinians were evicted from Israel, and Israel was founded. Palestinians today call it Naqba, or al-Naqba. Which means “catastrophe” or “disaster” in Arabic. Because for the Palestinian people, it was a disaster. The Arabic nations responded rather unkindly, it should be said — many of them subsequently kicked out their own Jewish citizens. Below we see a group of Yemenite Jews, being airlifted into Israel in 1949. The government of Yemen decided to expel them in retaliation to Israel’s expelling of the Palestinians. It’s pretty damn tragic because these people had nothing to do whatsoever with what Israel was doing in the region — they were just citizens of Yemen who happened to be Jewish. They had no affiliation to the Jewish state, no special connection to it, or loyalty towards it. They hardly knew of Israel’s newfound existence, and considered themselves Yemenites first and Jews second. That’s the tragedy of history — one disaster invites another disaster. One bad act invites other bad acts. And innocent people, hundreds of thousands, sometimes millions of them, are caught in the crossfire. People are vindictive, and needlessly cruel.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was Robin Hood a revolutionary?
Answer: It kind of depends on where he was born, and into what class. In some tellings of the legend, Robin Hood was a humble and poor man himself. In other tales, he was a nobleman who, returning from the Crusades, had fallen on hard times. In such versions of the story, he isn’t so much about redistributing the wealth in a manner he saw fit, as much as he’s on a quest for vengeance — he wants to take back what is his, and in the process, harm the greedy elites who have stolen his birthright. It should be noted that, throughout history, there have been poor men who rose to positions of great wealth. And they would often perpetuate the very systems they had fought so hard to escape. There are many stories, for instance, of former slaves who freed themselves, acquired fame and fortune and then, as soon as they were able to afford it, would buy a plantation and acquire slaves of their own to work on them. History has seen very few “revolutionaries” who not only overthrew a violent despot, but did so without turning into violent despots, themselves. In most of the historical tales of Robin Hood, he seeks out to rid the land of the evil Sheriff of Nottingham. All ends well when the “Good King Richard” (Richard the Lionheart) returns to the land. Robin Hood doesn’t seek to overthrow Richard — he merely wants to get back his lands and rule over them kindly and fairly. But he will still rule, he’s still a member of the noble class and while Robin and Richard will be far kinder to his subjects than Nottingham… they’re not about to dismantle the whole system.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are all Republicans against abortion?
