Answer: One very prominent Republican just caused the whole party to soften it’s stance on abortion for the first time in over four decades — and his name, ladies and gentlemen… drum rolls please… Donald J. Trump.[1] This is a historic first as, traditionally and going back as far back as the 1970s, the Republican party has been strongly opposed to abortion. The stance used to be that the GOP supports a nation-wide ban of the procedure. Now Trump has gotten them to soften this — it should now be left entirely to individual states, and there should not be any federal ban nor any federal protection of the procedure. This is pretty huge. It’s clever from a political point of view, as Trump needs female voters to win and having a rather bad personal track record when it comes to respecting women and their personal space (he’s been quite a Chester the Molester over the years), this is the sort of thing that does well with the female vote. So are all Republicans against abortion? No, they are not. Some of them are smart enough to realize that a full-on ban is bad optics, and bad politics. And the sort of thing that loses elections. Trump is one such pragmatist. In doing this, he removed perhaps the final hurdle to victory in November — took the Democrat’s wind straight out of their sails.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some good examples of kindness?
Answer: During the Holocaust it was customary for the Nazis to kill off the weak, young and sickly first and allow the older, stronger Jews to live and work slave labor. The exact procedures weren’t known to those newly imprisoned… but when Ottla Kafka, sister of famed author Franz Kafka, arrived in Auschwitz, she was selected in a “work group”. A nearby group of orphaned children were set aside to and seperated from the adult prisoners… Ottla, a strong woman, couldn’t stand to see the children crying so she insisted on joining them — the Nazi officer in charge of the selection process allowed her to join the frightened young ones. The children, with Ottla in tow, were brought straight to the gas chambers. She died with them, the very same day. Did she know where she was going, did she have any notion of what was to come? Part of me thinks she did. She wasn’t a stupid woman. There were stories being told, there were whispers. And I doubt a man as clever as Franz Kafka himself would have a sister unaware of the darkness of this world. Volunteering to join a group of orphans sent to their deaths and keeping up their spirits in their final moments on earth, is a great act of kindness. Ottla Kafka’s own daughters were born to her former husband, who was Christian. Hence her children were spared. Still, she chose to spend her last moments alive being a mother to those who had no mother or father.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do you think Robin Hood was moral? Is there such a thing as a moral thief?
Answer: Yes, some thieves can be moral. Or, at the very least, do things that are intensely moral. A man named Charles Arthur Floyd, better known as Pretty Boy Floyd, was such a man. He was a bankrobber — not a very friendly profession. But whenever Floyd would rob a bank, he would do something rather nice… he would find mortgage papers and burn them. In doing so, Pretty Boy Floyd saved hundreds of dirt-poor people from property debt, wherever he went… yes, he robbed banks. And he caused rich people to lose money. But in an era without computers, he also helped people down on their luck in a pretty major way. As a result, the public loved this man as much as they would any Robin Hood-esque figure. These were the days of the Great Depression. Times were hard. And sometimes it took hard men who didn’t play by the rules, to get people a lucky break and some breathing space… The FBI chased Floyd, tracked him down and riddled his body with bullets. He died at thirty. But he helped far more people than he hurt in life. While the act of theft is never really ‘moral’, sometimes a compassionate thief can do genuine good. And there’s a big difference between robbing a poor man and robbing a rich banker — the target of your thievery matters, too.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: "Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts." (Marcus Aurelius) What kinds of thoughts tend to dominate your mind from morning until night?
Answer: Yesterday I had a wonderful conversation with a friend of mine from Quora. We talked on Discord, a long distance call as he’s residing on the other side of the ocean. He said something that stayed with me… “I feel what we seek most, you and I, is continuity…” And that’s precisely it. Continuity. Ever since I was a kid, I hated to see my creations disturbed. The knowledge that my tower of blocks couldn’t stand forever, upset me. Why put effort into creating something beautiful if, after hours of work, it could simply be knocked over callously and hidden away in a box? Life’s kind of like that. Death knocks over all of us, every bit as callously. And like those building blocks, we end up in a box. And that’s the end of us. What I often do, is count. Count the time I already spent on this earth. And think about how much time I might have left. Notice how I use the word “might” — nothing really is given in this regard. There’s no absolute certainty that any of us will still be around tomorrow. Let alone ten, twenty of fifty years from now. Will I ever publish that great novel, will I ever build that empire, will I ever create something truly lasting in this world? And does anything really last, when even that world itself couldn’t last? That’s what I think about, most. Well that, and getting laid. Or what to cook tomorrow — good food is balm to the soul. But continuity. My legacy. How I’ll be remembered. And how I’ll look back on my life, when I’m on my deathbed. Will I be satisfied? I sure hope I won’t reach that end soon… because I’m nowhere near satisfied yet.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the definition of a political opportunist?
Answer: It would be a leader who says one thing in public, and does another in private. A fine example would be former British Prime Minister Liz Truss. She presented herself as a foreign policy hawk, a staunch nationalist, and fiercely anti-China.[1] Truss was pro-Taiwan, was critical of Chinese human rights violations… meanwhile, behind closed doors? She was lobbying with British defense companies to sell weapons to China.[2] And not just ANY weapons, mind you! — it was material aimed to remove mines that she was selling… in other words, exactly the type of stuff China needs more of to successfully invade Taiwan. In the meantime she publicly declared China a “threat to world peace” and “the most dangerous country around”… her rhetoric was fiery, aggressive, and she came across as a firm ally to Taiwan.[3] All the while secretly arming the very country she so publicly denounced… The definition of a political opportunist is someone like Liz Truss, who will warn how [insert country] is a dangerous for world peace and should not be allowed to invade a neighboring island state… only to secretly arm the very country she’s railing against. The cynicism is baffling. Had a Chinese politician done what Truss did, she’d have been put before a firing squad.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you name some actors who have given accurate portrayals of real people or characters in film?
Answer: A special mention goes to Timothy Dalton, who did only two James Bond flicks in the 1980s before being removed. Dalton’s Bond was cold as ice, much more stoic and didn’t have the twinkle in his eye Roger Moore’s Bond had. Nor was he the rogue Connery’s Bond had been. The odd thing… quite a lot of people weren’t pleased with Timothy Dalton’s portrayal, which was quite far from the movie character Bond as played before. But he was much more close to the original book-version of the character, compared to Connery and Moore’s take on the fictional spy. Because in the books, Bond isn’t all that charming… he can be, if he must be. But first and foremost, he’s a cold-blooded gun-for-hire, callously killing for King and country. Timothy Dalton was James Bond, as Ian Fleming had conceived the character. And while Daniel Craig came rather close, as well, Dalton looked the part far more, too. He acted, and looked, exactly as Fleming had envisioned. He was the most accurate portrayal and still only got two movies. A criminally underrated performance.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which historical event or story left you most amazed?
Answer: One of my favorite stories is probably that of Theodore “Teddy” Roosevelt. A small, sickly and asthmatic child, he wasn’t expected to live long or amount to much. And through sheer force of will, he molded himself into a tough guy — he took up boxing, wrestling, horseback riding, shooting. Left his comfortable, well-off New York lifestyle to become a cattle rancher at 20. If you saw the lad at ten and saw him again just ten years later, you wouldn’t believe how much he changed, and kept changing. He called his lifestyle “The Strenuous Life”, and summed it up thus: I wish to preach, not the doctrine of ignoble ease, but the doctrine of the strenuous life, the life of toil and effort, of labor and strife; to preach that highest form of success which comes, not to the man who desires mere easy peace, but to the man who does not shrink from danger, from hardship, or from bitter toil, and who out of these wins the splendid ultimate triumph. Roosevelt was a conservationist, founder of national parks, protector of nature and while he was a fighter, a warrior, a brawler and a military man for much of his pre-presidential life, he would later brag with some pride that during his time in office “not a single shot was fired”. Every week, even as a governor and president, Roosevelt would spar with random people in private boxing matches. Once he got hit so hard he lost sight in his left eye — he didn’t tell a soul. Another time someone tried to assassinate him during a speech. Roosevelt was hit in the chest and still finished the speech. Going from a sickly rich boy in New York to the absolute beast of a man he ended up becoming is one of history’s most amazing transformations.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some scary history facts?
Answer: Once, the Roman Emperor Domitian invited a group of powerful senators to a dinner. The dining hall was rather dark. And directly behind the couches on which they would sit and eat, there was a row of tombstones. On each, there was a name. All the names of the senators present were on the tombstones. The food served was very simple — it was the type of food that would typically be given as offerings to the dead. The whole ‘party’ had an eerie, strange, almost ethereal atmosphere… it was more like a wake, or a funeral, than a fun get-together. The Emperor, too, was unusually quiet. The noblemen wondered, terrified: “Did we displease the Emperor?” No answer came. No explanation was given. Domitian just ate his food, silently. Then sent the senators home. Each dinner guest expected to be summoned or taken from his home soon. They expected to be executed for crimes, real or perceived. But no execution came — Emperor Domitian merely wanted to prove a point: “Your life is mine. I can take it any time I see fit.”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How do we fight racism?
Answer: You want to kill racism? I’ll tell you how. Just remind people that racism is for losers. It’s a loser ideology. I’ve never know a cool, admirable person, someone confident, happy, satisfied with life… who was also racist. Below we see Arnold Schwarzenegger, one of the world’s most successful people. A man who optimized his potential in every way imaginable. He’s pictured on a boat in the 1970s with a black model. And he’s living his best life. He’s too busy working out, screwing, pumping iron, pumping models, actresses. Do you think he goes around doing or saying racist shit? No way. He doesn’t have time for it — he’s too busy making life his bitch. He’s too busy taking the world by the hips… and mounting Mother Earth. He’s too busy, squeezing pleasure, enjoyment, fun, out of life. Too busy dominating. Too busy winning. Too bushy crushing his enemies, driving them before him, the lamentations of their women like sweet music to the ears of the Austrian Beast. What is racism, anyway? Insecurity. You’re not good enough. You’re nothing. So you cling to your racial background. And think this elevates you. That just because some members of your race were great, once, it makes you “great by association”. It doesn’t — you’re a loser.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What actors in a film have the strongest resemblance to the actual people depicted?
Answer: Billy Zane will portray Marlon Brando in an upcoming Brando biopic called Waltzing with Brando. Zane will portray the famous actor, activist, inventor and Lothario in the late 1960s and early 1970s, when he starred in the Godfather and acquired his tropical getaway in Tahiti. The resemblance between the two men is incredibly strong — Zane looks nearly identical to a middle-aged Brando, in the years before the massive weight gain of his later life. I’m quite interested in the film, because the figure of Brando is quite compelling… he lived quite a life. Even in the biographies of other famous people, he’ll often show up out nowhere. Such as Keith Richard’s Life, where Brando briefly ‘steals’ his first wife from Richards and “reads poetry to her” (wink-wink) before returnijng her to the Rolling Stone guitarist. Even the way Brando acquired his island, Tetiaroa, is fascinating — he purchased it from an elderly lady who lived on the island alone. She had inherited it from her father, a dentist who helped out the last reigning King of Tahiti, Pōmare V. It was during the shooting of “Mutiny on the Bounty” that Brando felt paradise on earth was to live in a tropical island, be by the beach, and just never leave. He was King of his domain, there. Had quite the harem going, too. In a Playboy interview, in the 1970s, Brando takes a reporter snorkeling. A giant shark approaches — Brando turns around, punches it on the snout and it takes off in a hurry. I’ve been waiting for a biopic on this man for ages. It’s high time he gets one, and in Zane we find a fine lookalike, who also happens to be an excellent actor. Will be good!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the one thing in life that you will never quite understand?
Answer: A lovely event took place in Mali on July 3, 2024 — a couple was getting married. And as the whole family gathered to celebrate this joyful moment, trucks full of strange men arrived, carrying AK-47’s, machetes and knives. The strangers surrounded the family, allowing for no escape as they closed off all exits. And then they began shooting and stabbing people randomly. Slitting the throats of those who appeared dead, for good measure. By the time the terrorists left, 21 people lay dead, some nearly beheaded by this extreme act of barbarism. The group responsible for the brutal mass murder of an innocent family is an Islamist group linked to al-Qaida.[1] Twenty-one men, women and children. Simple people who had saved a long time for their dream wedding. Now they’re dead. I’ll never understand being so brainwashed, so misguided and hateful that you would kill innocent people just because they’re the “wrong faith”. The wedding in Mali was a Christian ceremony. These people were brutally murdered for their religion? Why? Why on earth would someone do such a thing? And most of the world is quiet… because it’s “just in Africa”. But mark my words — they’re coming for you, too, my fellow Westerners.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you name some famous individuals who have been criticized for taking their "woke" beliefs too far?
Answer: The best example would be Demi Lovato. In 2021 she got into this whole feud with a small frozen yogurt company in California — because it offered too many diet options and low-fat, sugarfree products. Which, get this, triggered Lovato. She said it was “fatphobic” of the company to offer so many options for people who wanted to lose weight. Aside from this, there’s this whole spiel with Lovato’s gender identity — she switched pronouns more often than a runway model switches outfits during a show. Over the years, Lovato went from she, to “they/them”, back to ‘she/her’ again. Several times. She finally dropped it about two years ago, all-but admitting it was a cry for attention when she shared how it had become ‘confusing and exhausting’ even to herself. I try to be considerate and kind, however — Demi Lovato is literally brain damaged after an overdose caused her to fall into a coma several years ago. Her “wokeness” is a symptom of mental illness. I wonder how common brain damage or mental issues are with people who hold extreme opinions. Probably more common than you’d think; normal, mentally healthy people don’t become over-the-top ‘woke’.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: If Trump wins, would his presidency be a challenge not only for Ukraine, but for Russia too?
Answer: Lets assume for a moment that he wins. And he does somehow end the Ukraine war, like he said he would. End it in such a way that is advantageous to Russia more than to Ukraine. Now here’s the thing — the ‘eternal war’ scenario kind of causes Russia’s economy to boom somewhat. A war economy makes for many new jobs in weapons factories.[1] Other areas, meanwhile, are severely neglected. Now let us assume Trump was sworn in. Forces Ukraine to the table. By December, the war is over. Russia now has to rebuild its economy. But it is still under sanctions. Putin and his cronies are still war criminals who cannot travel much of the world. And millions of young Russian men that left during the first year of the war out of fear of being sent to the trenches, are now comfortably living and settled abroad. Will they come back to Russia, a land with an economy that’s largely dying aside from their military industrial complex? Doubtful. If anything, the ongoing war keeps Russia afloat economically and masks just how bad things have gotten. A sudden end to the war would very likely mark the end of Russia itself, as well. And unlike Ukraine, Russia would not be able to count on the world’s sympathy in rebuilding itself. Honestly, for now and the foreseeable future, the status quo of ongoing warfare and increased war-time production is as good as it gets for Russia.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are your thoughts on Trump's immunity?
Answer: People have this tendency in life to worry a lot. And I get that. But there are some things we simply cannot control. Some people desperately want to see Trump behind bars… others desperately want him not to be behind bars. And at this point, I fully expect the man never to be in prison. I fully expect him to just, walk away scot-free. Like he always has. There have been scams, in the past. Investors he screwed over. Legal troubles he’s weaseled his way out of. He’s started his own university, which was a scam. Ran casinos. Bankrupted them. Got bailed out. He’s molested some woman in a changing room. Was found liable of it, ordered to pay damaged. Slandered her. Said she “wasn’t his type anyway”. Once he said: “I could shoot a man on Fifth Avenue and I wouldn’t lose a single vote over it!” and he wasn’t even lying, nor was he bragging — he was simply stating a fact. You want to talk about immunity? Sure, I can discuss immunity. But there really is no point — this man is untouchable. And there is a sense of peace in accepting things. In not denying the cold, hard facts of life. Some people are just born lucky. And others aren’t. Like a wise man once said: “Life’s unfair… and then, you die.”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why should you respect a veteran?
Answer: There’s a whole holiday dedicated to veterans in America, Veteran’s Day. It is celebrated every November 11. It was signed into law in 1926 by President Calvin Coolidge. Veterans will be honored with parades, and sometimes they will go to schools and meet children. In the photo below, we see a veteran breaking down at a school while telling of his wartime experiences. The girl in the photo, holding her face with her mouth, is the man’s granddaughter. She’s never seen her grandfather cry before. It shocks her. The look on her face says it all. During many wars, especially large scale ones like WWII and the Vietnam War, young boys are drafted and sent out at early ages. They train together, camp together, sleep together, go into the field of battle together. Very frequently, they lose young men that are as close as brothers to them. The memories and scars of their loss stays with them for their entire lives. You may be a pacifist. You may hate war — and with good reason! — or disapprove of the actions of your country, and their involvement in various foreign conflicts. And all those are perfectly reasonable concerns and feelings to have. But let none of those feelings distract you from one utterly unchangeable fact of life: these people are brave as hell. I tend to respect anyone who’s been to hell and returned to tell the tale. Only a fool with no empathy wouldn’t.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: In any animal breed, the male is generally more attractive than the female. Why is it the other way around in humans?
Answer: I’m concerned you would even speak of animals in terms of “attractive” versus “not-attractive”. You’re not supposed to find ANY animals attractive, you absolute degenerate. There’s a whole subgroup of people who do — they even dress up as animals to get their rocks off. They’re called furries. The internet has quite a few of them. And now, this isn’t a good look. Animals can look majestic. They can look hilarious. They can look magnificent or hideous. But attractive, as a word, implies ‘attraction’ or lack thereof. It’s not a word you should ever use when discussing animals. I mean how does that even work, you go to an animal shelter and they show you some dogs… and you’re like: “Nah, I don’t want that one.” They’ll ask you why not, you say: “Well it isn’t very attractive is, it? Doesn’t really have that oomph, that X-factor.” No, you monumental failure of a human being, you chromosomally impaired retrobate, you absolute waste-of-space nincompoop… animals are not “attractive”. Human beings are. The only thing attractive about an animal is how nicely their meat chars on the grill.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is saying "okay" considered to be unintelligent?
Answer: No, it isn’t. But when you’re having a conversation with someone and, after a lengthy message, your only response is “okay” then that’s kind of rude. It’s okay when it is an elderly person doing so — my grandfather would always respond to messages, no matter how long, with a simple thumbs-up. And even for that he’d have to use a pencil just to send a single emoji response as his fingers were too large for the keyboard. He was a very intelligent man. Just not built for eloquence in electronic portals. Letter writing was more up to his speed. Context is everything. Sometimes, an “okay” can convey a simple “sure, fine”. But sometimes “okay” can signify disinterest. Then there’s the even shorter ‘ok’, which may be used to expressed displeasure in a chat. The even shorter “K” or even the dreaded dotted “K.” are different beasts altogether — used only when the person responded to kind of screwed up. I’m not a fan of using the word “okay” in a chat, unless followed by an explanation or elaboration. Like when someone proposes something I find rather absurd… I might respond: “Okay, but [insert explanation]”. But never just okay and leaving it at that. Unless, of course, the conversation is exceptionally uninteresting to me and I do not particularly care for the person talking to me. The word “okay” has nothing to do with intelligence, or lack thereof. But it has everything to do with how interested you are in a conversation. Accompanied by other words, inside a proper sentence, okay is a fine word. By itself, “okay” is a rather ominous word in written form.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Whos your favorite athlete of all time?
Answer: For me, it’s Mike Tyson. Not just because of how he dominated the ring. Not just for his sheer brutality, the force of nature that he is. But for the enigma of a person that Tyson is. There’s a lot of lived experience within him. There’s wisdom, too. One Tyson quote often replays in my head: “A man who is a friend to everybody is an enemy to himself.” That’s a beautiful quote. And it’s true — you CANNOT be kind and friendly and a friend to everyone, because you’ll get walked over and you’ll lose yourself in the process. Another fine Tyson quote that’s worthwhile: “Everyone that you fight is not your enemy and everyone who helps you is not your friend.” And then there’s another that lives rent-free in my head. This one isn’t particularly deep, it’s just hilarious as far as social commentary goes. Tyson on social media: "Social media made y'all way too comfortable with disrespecting people and not getting punched in the face for it." On top of these quotes, his little insights into life and how he sees it… he’s pretty damn hilarious, too. Loved Mike Tyson in the Hangover movie. He’s pretty much the best part of it. Primarily because if anyone in the world would have a pet tiger, get it stolen and be super chill about the whole thing as long as it’s returned to him? It’d be him. Because he’s kind of wild like that. Mike Tyson. Another quote, to end it all with: If I have to live at the top of the world, I also have to live at the bottom of the ocean. I don't know how to live in the middle of life." Mike Tyson, who could not live in the middle of life. Who made and blew tens of millions of dollars over the years. Who was on top of the world, and on the very bottom. And needed to see, experience and feel it all. Have, win, and lose it all. To be who he is, now.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the toughest jobs in the world?
Answer: If done right? Leading a country. Below we see two photographs of Abraham Lincoln — the first was taken in 1861, the second in 1865, shortly before his death. Four years of leading his country through a brutal civil war had aged Lincoln considerably; though only 56, his wrinkled face could have belonged to that of a man in his seventies. There are many jobs that are physically tough and demanding. But mental exhaustion is a thing, too. As anyone who’s been a single parent, or the partner of someone suffering from mental illness will tell you — it’s ROUGH. Abraham Lincoln suffered on multiple fields, we should add. Besides leading a country through a war, his wife was also rather troubled. He frequently went days and nights on end without a single moment of sleep, or any real rest. This is brutal on both the human mind as well as the body. Every decision, every small choice, everything you do, or fail to do, it all has impact. And it all affects the lives of tens of millions if not hundreds of millions of people, either directly or indirectly. It’s a lot to live with for anyone. When someone leads a country and doesn’t visibly age during his tenure, you can bet your life savings he’s not doing all that much, nor all that concerned with the state and future of said country. When you look upon the face of a man who carries the weight of the world on his shoulders, trust me — you’ll know. It’ll be written all over his face.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who is the most good-looking historical figure ever?
Answer: There’s this test in psychiatry called the Rorschach test. You’re shown various shapes and are asked to interpret them a certain way. And the psychiatrist will then determine, based on what you see in the shapes, what your state of mind is. The Swiss psychiatrist who invented the test was a man named Hermann Rorschach. A rather dashing man with a square jaw, the small squinted eyes of a Western gunslinger and a haircut that’s hip even by today’s standards, Mr. Rorschach rather resembled Brad Pitt. There are quite a few historical characters who, even if you transported them by time machine to the present era, would have been seen as rather attractive. Mr. Hermann Rorschach is such a figure. Had he been born in 1984 rather than 1884, the man could have been in movies or on the cover of magazines.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do you think people were smarter in the past?
Answer: An awesome photo came to my attention the other day — it shows dancers in a New York night club in 1958… playing chess. In the year 2024, beautiful young women in barely-there outfits are more likely to be glued to a smartphone screen, taking selfies, maybe going on OnlyFans and chatting people. They wouldn’t play chess. In 1958, however, there were no such distractions. So even ladies whose profession it was to shake their money-makers for cash before an adoring audience, would do things like play chess behind closed doors. Women like Marilyn Monroe were interested in things like racial justice or politics, and even models could be found lounging in the sun, reading a book about psychology or ancient history. There’s this impression people have of beautiful models, dancers, actors, ladies and lads of the night, as being vapid, vain, what-have-you… Yet there’s a level of focus even the ‘influencers’ of their era had before, that we no longer see in ours. Memes, short videos, the dopamine rush of a barrage of incoming likes… all those have left too many of us with the attention span of a goldfish. Sixty years ago, even the showgirls played chess and people’s attention spans and focus were 100% better than ours.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How many presidents are even worse than Trump?
Answer: What is a President, ultimately, other than a vehicle for the views of those who back him? Trump is a vehicle, just as much as Biden is. And so were all those who came before them. Right now, I feel Biden may even be worse. In a recent interview he just said he would be “at peace if he lost to Trump because he gave it his all”.[1] No man who is THAT low energy should run for the highest office. And it dawned on me, very strongly… Biden is Ruth Bader Ginsburg. He’s the male RBG — too old, too tired, sickly, and too stubborn to let go. Ginsburg could have comfortably retired during the Obama administration. She refused because her ego was too strong. She wanted to retire ‘under a female president’, under Hillary Clinton… Trump won. And Ginsburg soon died, allowing Trump to further stack the courts. The courts that now gave Presidents immunity and power of a level never before seen. Above, we see some Project 2025 tenets — a platform on which Trump rules, funded by those who back and support him. He is very likely to fundamentally change the fabric of his nation by rubber-stamping whatever proposals the Heritage Foundation puts on his desk. And Biden will be okay, sure! He’s an almost 82-year-old man. What does he have to fear, on a personal level? It’s his voters he’ll be letting down. They will have to live with the consequences of his hubris. I’m beginning to think that Biden, for his hubris, may be worse than Trump at this point. He’s in denial, too. Polls are fake news to him, and he knows best, even when he doesn’t. He’s “at peace” with losing… bumbling slack-jawed and feebly into oblivion and dragging everyone to hell with him by his stubborn refusal to step aside for a better man. And no, I still think Trump is worse — but to recognize him as bad for the country and the world and STILL insist on running a race you cannot win? That’s just heinous.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What do you think about the far right gaining popularity in Europe?
Answer: The pendulum just always swings one way, or another. Someone wiser than me once said: “People more often vote against a party than for a party.” And this is true — a LOT of votes are protest votes. Take for instance Keir Starmer, who just became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom following a landslide victory. He’s a former socialist, now head of Labour. Economically and pretty much everywhere else, pretty left-wing. No, Mr. Starmer is NOT far-right. Very damn far from it, in fact. And yet he’s won. Simply by being different. He’s the boring guy, the ‘responsible man in the room’, the one who’ll fix things, or so his supporters hope. Mostly? They’re not left-wing, or right-wing, those voters. They’re just fed up with whoever is in power. In this case, that’s the Tories of Rishi Sunak, Liz Truss and Boris Johnson. Fourteen years of right-of-center rule, and people grew wary of it and wanted to return to left-of-center rule. Could have just as easily have been the far-left, or the far-right, that’d carried the day. But it wasn’t. It was milquetoast Mr. Starmer. Whoever is currently in power and isn’t already far-right, is at risk of being voted out and replaced by the far-right. And whoever is in power that is pretty right-wing, is at risk of being voted out by the regular left, or even the far-left if they manage to appear reasonable enough. All you need to swing the pendulum is NOT be the party in power. With most of Europe not in far-right hands, in theory any country whose populace gets worked up enough and fed up with the status quo, is at risk of a far-right takeover.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What’s an example of honor?
Answer: In the Kargil war of 1999, the Indian army fought against Pakistan’s military — the war began in May and ended by July… India won decisively. Pakistan, humiliated, refused to accept the bodies of their fallen soldiers; their government, instead, tried to deny Pakistani troops were ever involved in the hostilities. They claimed they were mere “insurgents”. The Indian soldiers, however, felt that the Pakistani men they had fought, had fought bravely and honorably. So when Pakistan refused to claim the remains, the Indians buried the fallen Pakistani fighters. They did so with full Islamic funeral rites, and full military honors. That’s honor, to me. To respect your enemy, even in death, and give them a decent burial cowardly denied to them by their own government… Honor is doing something righteous and just, something decent and humane, even when it isn’t expected of you. Because those whose responsibility it was to give that honor, refused to do so. Honor is respecting a dead enemy when even the government they died for won’t acknowledge their sacrifice. Even when these men were out to kill you and your comrades.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you share the saddest pictures of the day?
Answer: A photo from 1940 comes to mind. It features a young Anne Frank and her older sister, Margot Frank, at the beach in Zandvoort, the Netherlands. The Germans have not yet invaded the Netherlands, and at the time the photo is taken, all is well in the life of the Frank family. They aren’t in hiding yet. Anne had not yet started writing her diary — she was too busy, living her charmed little life. Swimming, playing with friends, having sleepovers. All innocent, good-hearted fun, the way kids are supposed to be. The heavier subjects that plague the human heart, the hatred, the ‘othering’ of one’s fellow man… none of that crossed her mind yet. She’s just a little girl, smiling. The way millions of little girls smiled before, and since. She has no clue that soon, she’ll be forced into a life of secrecy, at the risk of death. She doesn’t know she has only five years left — she smiles like a girl with big dreams, unaware of how they’ll never be realized.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What should I not do to a man as a woman?
Answer: The worst thing a woman can ever do to a man is lie about a child’s paternity. Not only deliberate lies but also “lies of omission”. Like when you aren’t certain your current partner is the biological father of the kid you’re carrying, because you had a bit of a “wild phase” or you and him were briefly broken up and you had a little fling with someone else… And the easiest thing in the world, for some dishonest women, is to simply keep quiet. They see a man. He’s not a bad guy. They’re together. She just found out she’s pregnant. And he’s probably the father. But it’s not certain. Not a 100% certain, anyway. Does she tell him? And risk him asking for a DNA test that may end up negative and cause him to walk away? Can’t have that, now can we… so she says nothing. It happens more often than you think. About five percent of children are — unknowingly — not fathered by the men who raise them. That’s one in twenty. So each classroom has one or two such kids. And one or two such deceived fathers. It’s one of the most beautiful, powerful bonds you’ll ever see. That of a father and his children. But one that is, sadly, sometimes based on a lie. I know life is messy. And sometimes we just do what’s easiest. But if you’re a woman, and you have any heart at all… ALWAYS be 100% honest about these matters. And when in doubt, suck it up and get that paternity test, anyway. Even if you dread whatever the outcome may be.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who are some forgotten old Hollywood stars that you believe should receive more recognition?
Answer: One of the earliest Hollywood comedians to receive megastar status in his era was a man named Roscoe “Fatty” Arbuckle. At the peak of his success, he made an astonishing one million dollar per year — an enormous sum for post-WWI Hollywood. Arbuckle threw a party in the early 1920s, at the height of his fame. An actress named Virginia Rappe suddenly fell ill and died after said party. One of her friends accused Arbuckle of raping and murdering Rappe. Arbuckle denied, strongly. And the woman who accused him had a rather lengthy legal history of her own — extortion, prostitution, blackmail… despite zero evidence linking Arbuckle to the crime, he was put on trial. Thrice. Twice, a hung jury. The third time, acquittal. At this moment, the jury took an unusual step: they gave the dogged star a written apology for his mistreatment at the hands of the justice system… Fatty Arbuckle’s career never quite recovered for most of his life. Then, in 1932, he made somewhat of a comeback… he got married, starred in some films again. In 1933, he celebrated his first wedding anniversary with friends and loved ones. “This is the best day of my life!” he reportedly told his nearest and dearest. He died that same night in his sleep, aged only 46.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did the Biden-Trump debate matter to you?
Answer: One of biggest Democratic party donors Reed Hastings, CEO and founder of Netflix, just spoke out in a recent interview. He said: “Biden needs to step aside to allow a vigorous Democratic leader to beat Trump.” This is a man who has donated over twenty million dollars to the Democratic party over the years.[1] Other donors have expressed similar concerns. Would Mr. Hastings have expressed this opinion so vocally, so publicly, had the debate never happened? Doubtful. Yes, of course it mattered. It’s not every day that you see history being made. All that MAGA rhetoric, all the “Biden is senile” jokes and memes over the years. All the gaslighting. So, so much gaslighting… our eyes were blind, our ears were deaf, we were mistaken — Biden was okay. He was fine. He was up for the job… and all of a sudden, the Emperor had no clothes. He was exposed before the world.[2] Because you can doctor images. You can doctor footage. You can endlessly replay, on loop, a video of Biden stumbling or tumbling down a flight of stairs… or falling off a bike. And it doesn’t mean much, necessarily — it’s just his motor skills. And the fact that he’s riding a bike in the first place at his age is somewhat impressive. A debate is difference. Because you HAVE to perform on the spot. Have to have your answers ready. And you have to bring your A-game. Above all? You cannot come across the way they portrayed you; as frail. Biden did. There is a lot of talk lately about Biden stepping down. He should, if the Democrats want to win the White House in November. Major donors are stepping away. Political allies are outwardly quiet, or express their support in studied, cliche ways that feel… lacking. Something big is brewing. I would not be surprised if Biden announced he’ll step down within a week.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What actor was also a great director?
Answer: A good example would be the great Clint Eastwood. In fact as of me writing this answer, Mr. Eastwood is 94 years old and directing what he’s already said will be his final film. Eastwood is a fine actor. He’s also a fine director — very no-nonsense. Other actors will shoot for a long time, and endlessly retake scenes as actors improvise lines and try to get their best performance out. Not Eastwood. You get ONE take. You either get it, or you don’t. Maybe, if you’re lucky, you get two takes. If the first one went wrong. You will say all the lines, exactly as written. You will NOT deviate from the script, at any point. You won’t get cute with Mr. Eastwood — he has a vision, and he doesn’t compromise on that vision. Ever. Tom Hanks did a movie with Eastwood a few years ago, and says the actor has a peculiar way of running his sets; he’ll talk very softly, gently, almost a whisper at times.[1] He does this because he’s used to working on Western flicks and horses would bolt when a director loudly shouts “action!” at the beginning of a scene. So Clint Eastwood made this habit of being quiet on set. Even if the movie he’s shooting has nothing to do with horses whatsoever — old habits die hard. Anyone working on an Eastwood production will typically work normal ‘office days’, no crazy overtime, actors and actresses are expected to show up on time, without diva-behavior, say their lines and be on their merry way after.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why do people think that diversity is good?
Answer: If it weren’t for diversity, I’d have a much less interesting culinary experience. Too much of European cuisine consists of rather bland things like boiled potatoes. A lot of pasta, a lot of bread. A lot of empty carbs that just fatten us up for winter and leave us feeling unfulfilled. When I was a kid, my father once took me to a small restaurant in London. It was an Indian restaurant… and I was never the same again. My eyes opened to the wonders of this world. God, how I loved that food! I’ve gone from just Butter Chicken, to Tikka Massala and Vindaloo… chicken, lamb, veggie versions, doesn’t matter. You name it, I got it. And butter. Oh sweet, creamy, devine butter! Diversity is spoken of in these awful terms of racial quotas and unfairness and rising immigrant crime… and that’s all fine and dandy and I get how awful that is, sure. But the food! Don’t forget the food. Diversity, immigration (and to an extent, colonization!) gave Europe spices we never had before. Flavors we never tasted before. I love food. I love exotic beauty. I love literature taking place in faraway lands I’ve never been to, and that make me long for them by the time the story ends, despite never having set foot there… Some may hate diversity. But if I had to go through the rest of my life without Indian or East-Asian cuisine? I’d jump off a bridge.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How can I get better in bed?
Answer: It’s incredibly simple. Be fit. Everything becomes more enjoyable when you’re fit. But especially night-time bedroom gymnastics. Be fit, so you have the strength, stamina and flexibility to go that extra mile. To switch positions and play naked Twister games like a champion. To really go out of your way and excel. There’s hardly any sexual problem in the world that cannot be achieved by eating healthier food and building healthier habits. For the men — drink a lot of water, and take vitamin supplements, especially those that contain zinc. Make sure at least 10% of all the food you consume daily consists of protein. You are what you eat. And you become how you live. If you want every part of yourself to be at its finest condition, you have to care for yourself the way you would care for a million dollar race horse. Too many of us are kinder to antique chairs or collectible items we own than we are to our own bodies. Hence, we deteriorate.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who are the most mysterious people in history?
Answer: There are several images of him, none of them particularly clear. He went by 58 aliases during his life. His birth name, birth date and place are unknown, as are his birth year or the day and year of his death — he disappeared into thin air in 1934. He’s most famously known as Wallace Fard Muhammad and he showed up, out of nowhere, in Chicago in 1930. Mr. Fard claimed all sorts of different backgrounds… for instance, he claimed at some point to be half-white, half African. He also claimed at some point to be part-Spanish, or part Native American. Some said he was Pakistani. Others said he was Egyptian. He founded his own church — the Nation of Islam (NOI). The NOI is a strange faith… it’s basically Scientology mixed with the KKK, but for black people. Because Fard went to Black churches and households, and told people that the purest race was the black race, and that humanity was created by a “Black Scientist” in His image. And that, therefore, the superior beings were black people. Fard’s church grew rapidly. And then, as suddenly as he’d appeared… he disappeared. The FBI kept a file on him, and when it was released decades after his disappearance, their best bet seemed to be that he was a Pakistani immigrant born in 1877. Why on earth a Pakistani immigrant ended up in America, claiming to be black and starting a cult for black people? Nobody knows. Nobody but the Black God of Mr. Fard and the Nation of Islam, I reckon.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which African country has the most beautiful women?
Answer: Taste when it comes to beauty is highly subjective. But for me, personally, I find women from Ethiopia and Eritrea absolutely gorgeous. The Habesha women of Ethiopia, in particular, are stunning. The first picture is a Habesha girl from Ethiopia. And below, I’ll show you a woman from Eritrea. Also incredibly cute to me: I’m a man of eclectic tastes. I’ve always had a thing for all things exotic, faraway, unique. Whether it comes to dishes, or partners. Africa is an incredibly rich continent, in terms of beauty, and the diversity of physical features. My own preference is for women with more sharp, defined features. Clear, light-brown to dark-brown skin. Full lips, strong white teeth. Plus, we’re all drawn instinctively towards partners in life who could give us healthy and attractive offspring. I have seen a few people who had one Eritrean or Ethiopian parent, and one white or Arab parent. And all of these kids were gorgeous. I’ve been looking for a wife for a while now. Habesha girls are high up on my list, if I were blessed enough to find one!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Should the world accept the "non binary " gender?
Answer: It’s just the sort of non-issue people want you to argue about… the Supreme Court in America just made the office President into that of semi-King…[1] Meanwhile? The man most likely to win in November according to all polls, is compromised by both China and Russia and may well be a foreign asset.[2] And here you are… asking about “non-binary” genders… Gender is… a very personal thing. I used to argue about it, from time to time. Even get into debates about it. But all this “culture war” nonsense really is nothing but a distraction in the grand scheme of things. The world is teetering on the brink of WWIII. Environmental protection laws are at risk of being hollowed out, corruption is at an all-time high and at risk of becoming even higher in years to come. There’s plastic in EVERYTHING, and it’s literally slowly making us all infertile.[3] And yet here we are. Talking about made-up gender identities that help no one, and honestly harm no one, either. Just, live and let live. And focus on those things that are killing us, rather than allowing ourselves to be distracted by silly nonsense while a gathering storm approaches…

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is the need for a third, left-wing party in the US obvious?
Answer: Living in Europe, one thing I always loved is how one man, one party, can just come up and appear out of thin air. Just like that, in the snap of a finger. And they can dominate public discourse. And threaten the established order. The Netherlands had this happen, in 2002 — his name was Pim Fortuyn. A former professor, Fortuyn wrote a book about the disastrous neo-liberal policies of recent years. He warned of the influx of immigrants, the growth of radical Islam. All things NO ONE at the time spoke of. They labeled Pim Fortuyn a fascist. A Neo-Nazi. The devil incarnate. He was ridiculed. Physically attacked at rallies. But through it all, he kept a cool head. He would salute his audiences in a mocking gesture… “At your service!” he would say with a wry smile. It was his slogan. In the polls, he was leading. Big time. It seemed he was headed for victory in the 2002 parliamentary elections — and in a multi-party system, the party that has the most seats, even if it fails to get an absolute majority, will form a coalition government with other likeminded parties. This way, as much as possible, the voice of the people will be heard… One far-left activist named Volkert van der Graaf did NOT want to wait for the ‘voice of the people’… he got a gun and assassinated Pim Fortuyn outside of a radio studio, nine days before the elections. Fortuyn died on the spot. He wasn’t some far-right boogeyman — he was a reasonable, well-educated alternative to the establishment. America seems determined not to allow a genuine third party option to ever appear; genuine change scares the ‘powers that be’, wherever and whoever they may be.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was Obama the best president ever in the US history?
Answer: No, of course not. But he did have one thing other Presidents since haven’t had since… insane charisma, and considerable energy. He could do things ‘on the fly’ that I’d never see a Trump do, let alone a Bush, or a Biden. In the picture below, we see Obama having an impromptu dinner with celebrity chef and writer Anthony Bourdain, in a tiny cheap eatery in Hanoi, Vietnam. Obama had the “I’d have a beer with him!” factor down to a T. He could eat simple food, dress down, and get down on the level of whoever he was speaking to. And yes, he was ‘polished’, and calculating, like any good politician is. But he was an excellent actor — he made it feel real. And that’s a remarkably rare quality to find any politician the last couple of years. In the last twenty years, America has Bush, presidential son, child of nepotism. And then there have been Biden and Trump; bickering elderly men, one of them needlessly aggressive and crass, the other senile. Part of Biden’s appeal in 2020, aside from being not-Trump, was having been Obama’s former Vice President. No, this man was another level. Sure, a lot of people hated the man’s guts. But compared to what came after, the difference is night and day. Put this man in a debate with Trump or any other adversary and he’ll wipe the floor with him. If there weren’t term limits, he’d win big time in November. But then again, so might a syphilis-riddled koala at this point if he ran for the Dems.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who in history, is an unsung hero, and deserves more credit?
Answer: I’ll just use the example of one war-time nurse, June Wandrey Mann, but she’s a stand-in for the bravery of ALL war nurses, everywhere. She wrote a book about her experiences during WWII, “Bedpan Commando” it’s called. One thing she shared is a rule. The number one rule: "We all cry in private. But not in front of the boys. Never in front of the boys.” The full quote, in Mann’s own words: “An eighteen year old boy is carried into the shock ward, and he looks up at me trustingly asking, “How am I doing, nurse?” I just kiss his forehead and say, “You are doing just fine soldier.” He smiles sweetly and says, “I was just checking,” then he dies. We all cry in private. But not in front of the boys. Never in front of the boys.” We always make movies about the warriors, the fighters, the great kings and generals riding off into the field of battle, towards eternal glory. The brave men who duck enemy fire and succeed at all odds. And following them, we find many young men. Some mere boys. So many of those boys get wounded, badly. They’re brought in, in horrific pain, more dead than alive. And they look at the nurses and doctors in their final moments on earth. They’re scared. They’re suffering. Nine out of ten times, it’s a nurse who gives them comfort in their last minutes. Tells them it’ll be alright. Knowing it’s nowhere near alright.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the best thing Donald Trump has done?
Answer: An interesting piece of commentary I read recently by the actress Kerry Washington came to my attention… it has to do with the word “felon”. I’ll post an excerpt of what she said down below because it’s very poignant: There are a great number of people inside America today, who fail to get hired for jobs because they, too, are “convicted felons”. Now you may be pro-Trump and believe that the charges leveled against him are bogus. Or grossly exaggerated — and they may be! But still, he’s given special treatment. Given a level of consideration not given for, say, the man who was once caught smoking weed 20 years ago or the kid who beat a bully in self defense and got arrested for assault, and now loses out on a job because of that word, “felon”. Too many people suffer their entire lives because of one indiscretion, one mistake they made, often when young and stupid. Political preferences aside — it’s awesome that the word “felon” is becoming somewhat normalized now by the simple fact that Trump is one. Hope employers think of this the next time when they refuse to hire a person based on a past felony… why would a felon not be good enough for Wallmart, but be perfectly fine to run for President?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is there so much forced diversity in movies these days?
Answer: While a lot of it IS forced, a funny thing I learn more and more, the more I read history, is that actual history was sometimes more diverse than we expect or give it credit for. The woman below was a lady named Cattelena. All we know is that name. Was it her first name, her last name? We don’t know. But she died in England, in 1625. And she was a free woman. She owned property, was unmarried, had a house and a cow. And she milked that cow and sold dairy products for her livelihood. Meaning that one could, in theory, make a history movie taking place in Tudor England and, get this — have a “proud independent black woman” type character show up. And people would groan and roll their eyes and complain about “forced diversity” and yet… it’d be 100% accurate within that particular time period. There were only a handful of black people in Tudor England. And medieval Europe, too, had relatively little diversity… …but not zero diversity. Just, little. So if you keep the diversity in historical movies at a minimum, you’re actually not THAT far off the mark. If you overdo it, you screw up. If you ignore it altogether, you’re also hanging on to a fantasy version of a 100% homogenous past that never happened. History is super complex — a good movie will reflect this.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some rare celebrity photos we can’t take our eyes off?
Answer: A photo from 1989 comes to mind… it’s Jackie Chan at a benefit concert in 1989, in support for the protesters killed at Tiananmen Square in Beijing. It is a rare photo, because it’s not something Jackie Chan likes to be reminded of. Today, Chan has very close ties to the CCP. He’s best buds with the government in Beijing. A government that pretends, until this very day, that the massacre at Tiananmen Square in 1989 never happened… Tank Man, who so bravely stood in front of a tank? Never existed. It’s all been scrubbed off the internet in China. And Jackie Chan very much toes the line, in this regard. He does now, anyway… but in 1989? He had the heart of an activist, too. He cared. The lady next to him on the photo at the concert is Anita Mui — she helped smuggle many protesters out of Mainland China to safety after the massacre. Jackie Chan cared, once. Then he sold out big time, for profit. But he doesn’t like to be reminded of that. He hates this picture. Which is why sharing it matters all the more.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the most controversial topics in today's in the Wrold?
Answer: Without a doubt, politics. There was a fellow who followed me on Quora for years. Lovely chap. Virtually everything I wrote, he’d upvote. Frequently he would comment, too. Until some day, I wrote an answer that wasn’t critical enough of a certain politician he particularly hated — a certain orange-hued, messy-haired gentleman from New York with particularly small hands. It was at this point that my once-loyal follower promptly blocked me. It’s odd. The answers before it had his ‘upvotes’ still on them. And all of a sudden, I was the devil personified. Because I hadn’t towed the line. Because I had given an opinion that was a little too… kind, perhaps, to a group of people this individual found deplorable. Must have happened around 2022. Or maybe last 2023, I don’t recall. It’s just funny, and a little bewildering. On the hand, I have some of the best conversations here on Quora with people I frequently disagree with. Hell, the moderator of one of this site’s largest feminist ‘spaces’ was a good friend of mine, after we had an initial (rather public) feud. We talked a lot, on private messages… …until some day, we didn’t. Because she blocked me, too. I must have said the wrong thing again, in one of my answers. Maybe about men. Maybe about women. Or about whatever woke topic-du-jour is ‘hip and happening’ right now. People are strange, weak, weird, thin-skinned creatures. They continue to bewilder me with their mental fragility. With those made of sterner stuff, I’ve had marvelous friendships on this site.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do you agree that Rishi Sunak's politics are the result of a particular and subjective experience?
Answer: He’s not elected, first of all. I mean, within his party, he has been. But Rishi Sunak never had to court the votes of the population as a whole. You speak of experiences? His has been a rather charmed life… a former Goldman Sachs banker and hedge fund manager, Sunak has never been broke. His wife’s a billionaire heirress. And the couple lives lavishly in a rather fine mansion. Only the very best of food, the very best of suits — Mr. Sunak is practically royalty. And sure, he’s of Indian heritage. But with the type of background he has and the charmed life he’s lived, Sunak might as well have been a Sultan or Maharaja. The “experience” on which Rishi Sunak’s policies are based, are those of a man who has it all. A man about as far removed from common people as any given member of the Royal Family. All that’s missing is a mistress, some scandals and an interview on Oprah and Sunak is practically a brown-skinned second cousin to the Windsors.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is Donald Trump so successful despite ignoring social norms for respectful behavior?
Answer: Because this world belongs to assholes. Assholes built the world, assholes built civilization, started and won wars, gained empires and lost them again. That’s always been the way of the world. And before, the assholes-in-charge needed this thing called decorum. They’d pretend to NOT be assholes to get the support of the people. Trump, in 2016, decided to break with this age-old tradition. I’d say the moment he mocked a physically disabled reported at a press conference was likely the final straw that broke the camel’s back… a lot of people, sadly, never moved beyond their “high school bully” phase. They still love cruel jokes, rough off-color humor and getting laughs off the backs of people that are “different”. Such a man appeals to the basest instincts of the human psyche. A deep, dark and rather sinister part of our mind that’s cruel, and often hidden away. The rapey, taunting, genital-grabbing nasty demon inside too many of us. The average person knows it isn’t right, to act like that. Knows there will be social repercussions for such behavior. And the average person, too, knows this thing called shame. They’d be embarrassed to act in such a way. Trump doesn’t really have shame. He’s free of it. Free of shame. Free of guilt. Which is why the average president ages a LOT during his time in office. Look at pictures of a young Obama in the first year of his presidency. And compare that to how he looked in his final year… he’d aged massively in just eight years time. Looked easily fifteen years older. Biden, meanwhile, was broken by just one term. Compare 2020 presidential debates to the 2024 debate — the man has declined spectacularly. And Trump? It’s water off a duck’s back to Trump. Stress affects him less than it does other people. Because he takes pride in being an asshole. Gets off on it, even. Nothing he says or does, however heinous or misguided, will ever keep him awake at night.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Will Donald Trump and Joe Biden be marked as the greatest presidents in American history?
Answer: Oh, you want to mention the word history to me? Let us look at a historical precedent, then — the world has danced this dance before. With Sulla and Marius in Rome, over 2000 years ago. The two men even looked a little like Biden and Trump, going by their busts, as seen below. Marius, to the left, was an elderly statesman who refused to accept he was past his expiration date as a politician and general. And Sulla, likewise, was an overly ambitious general and politician. Both men wanted the top spot of consul — Marius had already held the position six times before. Guess what happened? Marius assumed power in Rome when Sulla was away on a foreign campaign… Sulla came back, marched troops into the city (a historical first!) and kicked out Marius using force. Then when Sulla was away once more, Marius resumed power. Had himself installed consul of Rome for a seventh time. And died, just two days into his final term. He was elderly already and likely suffered a stroke. Then, Sulla came back. Had a bloody revenge on all his enemies, mounted their heads on the walls of Rome and ruled as dictator as Rome for a few years before retiring. The bloody rivarly of these two vindictive elderly men marked the beginning of the end for the Roman Republic. No, Trump and Biden aren’t “good presidents” or even great — they’re the Sulla and Marius of our day and age. Their hubris is larger than their love for their country. And neither man has the courage to step aside and let a better man take over.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who’s the smartest Hollywood celebrity?
Answer: One thing I recently learned — Tommy Lee Jones went to Harvard. And he was roommates with none other than future Vice President Al Gore. Jones was in debate clubs, wrote papers, finished with high honors and right after graduating cum laude, abandoned his field (English literature) and decided to pursue acting, instead. This was a guy who very much had the “keys to the castle” — wickedly smart, well-connected, well-educated. He could have gone places. But the only place he wanted to go? Hollywood. People have this impression of actors as being not all-that-smart. Just, some good-looking people who recite lines adequately and with conviction and know how to work their angles. This really isn’t true for a lot of them; actors are a diverse bunch. Tommy Lee Jones didn’t go into his acting career impulsively or willy-nilly, either — he already befriended some agents even during his Harvard days. When he graduated in 1969, he made some calls. And that very same year, he made his debut on Broadway. This guy was incredibly determined, so of course he got to be exactly where he wanted to be.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you give some examples of social norms and expectations that have changed over time or continue to change today?
Answer: In 1906, 20-year-old Australian swimmer Annette Kellermann was tired of the old-timey, uncomfortable Victorian era swimsuits most ladies were still expected to swim in… so she had a swimsuit custom made — it was more form-fitting and somewhat more ‘revealing’ than what ladies used to swim in. People considered it “indecent”. In fact authorities even fined Kellermann for her choice of attire, fearing the innocent public’s eyes would be scandalized by “the sudden appearance of her outlined breastesses when wet”. Once, at Revere Beach, she was even arrested for “public indecency”. Kellermann, rather than back down, used the notoriety thus received to promote herself — and launch a swimwear line of her own, to great success! Kellermann died a rich woman in 1975, aged 89. She managed to squeeze a career as a movie star out of her swimwear controversies and had a long and successful life. The swimsuits and bikinis women and girls wear today are far more scandalous than anything this swimwear pioneer ever could have thought of — and yet none of it would have been possible without her.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is it true that Kanye West is now in Moscow?
Answer: Yes… the famously eccentric Kanye West is currently in Moscow. It’s not sure if he also brought along his wife, whom he keeps either naked, or on a collar like a dog. For privacy, West covers his face with what appears to be a pantyhose… after Steven Seagal and Gerard Depardieu, Kanye is the biggest name to grace Russia with his — ahem! — special presence.[1] Seagal. Tucker Carlson. And now… this guy. It’s pretty funny, in a sad sort of way. Seems like every dictator has his own eccentric Westerner — Kim Jong Un has Dennis Rodman. Now Putin has Kanye? I wonder what he’s up to. Is it a concert, is he merely sight-seeing… or is he, perhaps, relaying a personal message from his close personal pal, Donald Trump? We live in a ridiculous world. A world full of “useful idiots” to be used by the PR machines of despots the world over. The Nazis famously had half of every British aristrocrat including a former King on their side before WWII broke out, lobbying for “peace in our time”. And Russia now has these inglorious heroes — Seagal, Obélix, Tucker and Kanye. Yes, Kanye West is in Moscow. What he’s up to, no one knows. Chances are, even Kanye doesn’t know at this point… last I heard of the man he was caught in a public indecent act with his wife in a rowboat in Venice. How does a mad misunderstood genius top that one? Visit Moscow!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do you expect Donald Trump to win the presidency?
Answer: The latest polls are in and… it’s still pretty much a tie.[1] It looks as if the much-talked about June 27 debate didn’t move the needle that much.[2] Which surprises me, because I had expected more people would perhaps move away from Biden after his shockingly frail appearance. Turns out people have really strong opinions about both candidates already. So if you hated Trump before the debate and thought he was unfit for office before the debate… you likely still feel that way after. Chances are you’d rather vote for a manatee or a corpse than Trump — even if Joe Biden has these “Weekend At Bernie’s” days. That’ll be the narrative from here on out — Joe Biden is pretty much a zombie, taken care of, prodded and sometimes drugged by his “handlers” to campaign. Is it an effective narrative, for the pro-Trump side? I’m not sure. The polls do not seem to reflect the type of seismic shift many, myself included, were expecting. And in a way? That makes sense. Because even in 2020, few people voted “for” Biden… and a LOT of people voted against Trump. For what it’s worth, presidential historian Allan Lichtman, who correctly predicted the outcome of 19 out of 20 elections (except the Bush v. Gore debacle) still insists Biden will win.[3] As for my own personal take? I’d say there is still a non-zero chance Biden could win. I’m leaning more towards a Trump victory, right now. But it’ll come down to the “swing states” and how both will perform, there. There’s also wild card candidate Kennedy — he’s crazy enough to steal some anti-vax votes from Trump, and too crazy to steal Democrats away from Biden voters. So far, Trump has the “energized base” and genuine enthusiasm among his followers going for him.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why does society hate men so much, especially the nicest ones?
Answer: Society does not hate “nice men”. And the men who describe themselves as nice aren’t typically all that nice. You know what they are? Non-assertive. And very little about being non-assertive appeals to people… you are shouting out to the world: “Here I am! I’m a good guy! I’m decent, I’m friendly, I’m cool. I wouldn’t hurt a fly!” Okay, cool story, dude. Does your niceness pay the bills? Does it make people laugh, does it entertain them, does it help you in your career or your personal life? No, it doesn’t. It does no such thing. Truthfully, all it does is make you a doormat. A pushover people fuck with for fun, someone who gets walked all over, ignored, pushed aside. You’re not a viable romanic prospect, you’re not considered for that promotion at work you’d love to have and may even deserve — because you’re invisible. And you think keeping your head low and keeping quiet is some sort of virtue… …and it isn’t a virtue. It isn’t a good quality. It is just you, screwing yourself out of opportunities day in, day out, because you’re so desperate to be seen as kind, polite, sweet. In nature, the ‘sweetest’ lion doesn’t take over the pride. The ‘nicest’ water buffalo doesn’t get to mate. They get their balls chewed off and die in a puddle of misery. Grow a pair. And get yours.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What if Marine Le Pen could be the President of France?
Answer: It would be pretty bad. Because Marine Le Pen wouldn’t just be President of France… she’d also be a Russian asset. Le Pen, whose party crushed Macron in yesterday’s elections, has close ties to Putin.[1] She received dubious Russian loans to the tune of millions a few years back. She’s good pals with Putin, visited Moscow several times. There are proven financial ties between the Kremlin and Le Pen’s party. And in 2014 when Putin invaded and annexed Crimea as part of Russia? She defended him. Loudly, and publicly. For over ten years now, she’s been defending Russia fiercely. Even last year, a year into the Ukraine war, Le Pen declared: “Crimea is Russian!” and stood by her views.[2] She wants France to leave NATO, too. Is fiercely anti-Brussels.[3] It should be noted that Marine Le Pen talks a great deal about values and her patriotism, and her dislike for immigrants and Islam. But her love for France pales in comparison to her love for Russia… and Russian bribes. I pray to God a bolt of lightning strikes down this goon if the people of France aren’t smart enough not to elect a blatantly obvious Russian shill.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why are you some of those who think about Rome every day?
Answer: In 2007, something bad happened to me that kind of stayed with me for the rest of my life — Rome was cancelled. Rome, the show by HBO. I was young, then, but that show made me a man. Watching the adventures of Titus Pullo and Lucius Vorenus traveling throughout the ancient world, Caesar’s rise and fall, the Roman civil war, Pompey’s demise, the Ides of March, Cleopatra and Mark Anthony, Octavian… God I just LOVED that show. The atmosphere, the scenery, the writing. It was excellent. It just lived, and breathed. This was HBO’s first major, expensive, movie-esque show with long episode and ambitious scope. Turns out the sets, the weapons, all of it was just too damn expensive. HBO couldn’t afford it, then. Years later when Game of Thrones came around the corner, they could. And don’t get me wrong — the first few seasons of GoT were excellent, too. But it wasn’t Rome. There’s not a day that goes by where I don’t think about HBO’s Rome. I find myself in a rough spot, a predicament, a devilish dilemma… instinctively, my right hand reaches for my trusted spatha. And I ask myself: “What would Titus Pullo do?”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the most powerful and profound quote?
Answer: There’s one that has more energy, and carries more power, than any other quote. It is by a Native American chief called Low Dog. He fought at the Battle of the Little Bighorn and many other battles against the American army. “This is a good day to die… follow me!” That’s what Low Dog reportedly said to his men before he went into battle ahead of them. He didn’t die — he survived all his battles, and eventually retired to a reservation where he remained chief. And while he didn’t die fighting in the field of battle, it wasn’t for lack of trying… countless daring raids, and suicidal last charges went before him and he came out of it all alive, against all odds. His men said Low Dog was “like a thunderbolt”. There’s something insanely powerful about looking out to the field of battle. Enemies all around. Things do not look well, and your people have been badly beaten in many previous battles. And you look at the odds. They’re not good. And in defiance, you say with a smile: “This is a good day to die!”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Macron has called for a new election in light of his party's election defeat in EU elections in 2024. Will Marine Le Penn become the French President, and what will its repercussions for France and the rest of the EU?
Answer: The breaking news right now — the far-right won in France. Emmanuel Macron’s high stakes gamble did NOT pay off, and his party massively lost in the snap election he called to re-establish his grip on power… the far-right won handily. Second-highest number of votes went to the far-left, instead. And Macron’s more centrist liberal party got demolished. To say the outcome of this election is a complete and utter political earthquake of historical proportions, would be an understatement. France’s Macron was Mister Europe, very strongly pro-European Union. The far-right is NOT. Neither is the far-left. There will be another round, on July 7. But this is huge. France is a firm supporter of Ukraine, one of Europe’s strongest military forces and a major player within NATO. The new guys? They hate Ukraine, love Russia, hate Brussels and are of the Brexit-variety… These guys who won? They’re like the Nigel Farage’s, the Wilders’ of France. Or for you Yankees out there — the French MAGAs. Given the pivotal role France has historically played inside the European Union, this election result will cause a seismic shift within Europe. The consequences of this election will be felt the world over. Europe’s far-right has never been this powerful in decades.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which U.S. presidents were LGBT?
Answer: Many people would point out some of the more peculiar sleeping arrangements of Abraham Lincoln as possible evidence for him having been not entirely heterosexual. It wasn’t uncommon during his era for men to share beds and sleep together at night — it wasn’t typically regarded as a romantic thing the way it is, now. But there was one man Lincoln was unusually fond of — his bodyguard, Captain David Derickson. Whenever Lincoln was away from his wife, Derickson would share the bed with him. This caused some gossip to spread about the two men… Elizabeth Woodbury Fox, wife of Lincoln's naval aide, wrote in her diary on November 16, 1862: “Tish says, 'Oh, there is a Bucktail soldier here devoted to the president, drives with him, and when Mrs. L. is not home, sleeps with him.' What stuff!" Does the wife of a close companion of Lincoln making an insinuation about the President’s sexuality make good ol’ Honest Abe gay? I don’t think it does. I’ve read somewhere else that Abraham Lincoln and his wife, Mary Todd, had a rich and fulfilling sex life, Lincoln once bragging in private writing how in “oversized Mary Todd he had found a match for his massive staff”. They spaced out their children carefully, each a few years apart — the Lincoln couple was aware of crude forms of birth control available at the time and made use of them. Abraham Lincoln had a wife, four kids, and was passionate towards with his wife. In private, he was a highly sexual man. Captain Derickson was married twice and had ten kids. So I’d say, at most, Lincoln *may* have been bisexual. Truthfully? We’ll never know. It wouldn’t make the man any less of a legend if he did sometimes dip in the pond of gentlemanly love.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Have you ever been homophobic or met somebody who was?
Answer: Yes, I have been. In fact I was making a LOT of homophobic jokes when I was in high school and college. I didn’t actively hate gay people at any point. But they were an odd, almost alien ‘other’ to me that was hilarious to poke fun at… I didn’t know, at the time, that my own brother would soon come out of the closet. Nor did I know my best friend in college was a gay man — he didn’t give me any indication of it, either. In fact he made quite a few homophobic jokes, himself. The atmosphere in college and high school was one of “anything goes”, humor-wise. The more raunchy and over the top, the better. Getting your whole class into a state of uproarious laughter was the highest social victory you could make. What better way to get them there then to say something super racist, super homophobic or — when particularly inspired — both? After college, my best friend and I never had any sort of falling out. But I got married young. Moved away. And we barely talked anymore. A few years ago I found out online that he now has a boyfriend… He never felt comfortable enough to tell me, himself. So he laughed at the same jokes everyone else loved at. Made some of his own. Pretended to be cool with it all. And then, our friendship just died. I loved that man like a brother. And I feel like my careless jokes killed what we had. I remember the roadtrips, the drunk nights, the great talks. The time I cried on his shoulder over a girl. I hate myself for what I did. And have always tried to be kind to my gay bros ever since.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some mind-blowing facts about Ukraine?
Answer: Here’s a scary fact about Ukraine — it has a fertility rate that may be the second-lowest in the world.[1] The year before Russia’s 2022 invasion, the fertility rate of Ukraine stood at around 1.1 child per woman. By now, it’s at about 0.7 child per woman. By contast, the country with the lowest fertility rate in the world, South Korea, is at about 0.65 child per woman. In other words… war or no war, Ukraine is dying out. By contrast, Russia’s fertility rate is hovering around 1.5, which is low enough for Russian officials to practically beg Russian mothers to have more babies.[2] The situation is dire for Russia already.
