And yet, Ukraine’s women have about 50% fewer children than Russian women. And even before the war broke out, their numbers were already significantly worse... A nation without a young generation to take over, is a nature without a future. Yes, it’s bleak. But why lie and beat around the bush with pointless coping mechanisms and mental gymnastics? Ukraine is in an incredibly rough spot and has been for decades with no end in sight. One of the most mind-blowing and tragic facts about Ukraine is that it’s a nation that was already in a very dark place long before the Russian invasion. It was plagued by scandals, corrupt officials, and it’s people were in a hopeless situation. Now they’re fighting for their lives, and fighting valiantly. But few people seem aware of just how dire things have been for Ukraine, and how much worse they are, now.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the worst error in judgment in America's military history?
Answer: Probably the unholy alliance with Islamist forces in Afghanistan to kick out the Soviets. Young Muslim men from all over the world helped fight the Russians alongside the Afghan people. Regional warlords, religious fanatics, socialist revolutionaries, Afghan nationalists… you name it, they got it. From all over the world they entered Afghanistan — the Mujahedeen. Freedom fighters. Martyrs. Brave men who even had a Rambo movie dedicated to their valliance… And yes, one of them was the gentleman above — Osama Bin Laden. Scion of a fabulously wealthy Saudi family. No one in America at the time saw it as anything other than righteous… helping these brave souls kick the asses of their Godless heathen enemy, the Soviets. Even the rich kids wanted in on the action, potentially laying down their lives just to stick it to Mother Russia? Great! The more, the merrier. America smuggled in billions of dollars worth of weaponry. Missiles and guns, launchers, AK47s, from China, Israel, Europe, all carried not-so-secretly through the Pakistani-Afghan border with the support of Pakistan’s President Zia-ul-Haq… And America did succeed, initially — the Russians got their asses handed to them and had to leave Kabul with their tails between their legs. The guns smuggled in, remained. The Taliban used them. Regional warlords kept them. And Al-Qaida did, too. Osama and his comrades had the best possible war training, fighting for over a decade in the mountains of Afghanistan. The “War on Terror” was a beast entirely of America’s own making.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why do people get angry when someone decides to never get any tattoos and keep their skin pure?
Answer: They don’t get angry at you for not having tattoos — they get angry because you’re being a dick about it. Because when you speak of “keeping your skin pure”, you’re essentially saying those who have tattoos have “impure skins”. It makes you sound like a creepy serial killer who loves to skin his victims and is now upset that his lampshades won’t look as neat. I don’t have any tattoos myself and don’t ever call my skin “pure”. It’s just, a skin. Get over it. Just, don’t have tattoos in peace and don’t make it into the vocal point of your existence. It’s like those people who have no kids and call themselves “childfree” but rather than just live ‘freely’ won’t ever shut up about other people’s kids and how “awful” they are — don’t let the subject of your ire live rent-free in your head.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some of the craziest laws around the world?
Answer: Recently in North Korea, a 22-year-old man was publicly executed. His crime? Listening to K-Pop music. As in, South Korean pop music.[1] Watching South Korean shows, or listening to their music, is illegal in North Korea. And yes, it can get you a death sentence. The thinking of dictator Kim and his cronies is simple enough — South Korean shows and music videos are full of glitter and glamour. They show the North Korean audience a world entirely alien to their own drab, grey and depressingly dystopian society. The South Korean stars are healthy, young, tall and well-dressed. They have all the newest gadgets, all the newest phones and cars. None of them live in apartments anywhere near as sad and broken down as those of North Korea’s population… Kim really doesn’t want anyone getting any ideas. While South Korea has many issues of its own, they’re not reflected in most of their lighthearted entertainment. Seeing just how advanced South Korea is goes against all of the Northern propaganda. And it may just give people ideas. So if you’re caught listening to K-Pop? It’s the firing squad for you.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can someone be considered a hero if they are not brave?
Answer: No. Not if we look at all heroes as being strictly heroes in the epic, legendary sense of the word, that is. And that is how most of us are conditioned to see the word hero. It’s like the beginning of 2004 epic Troy. A little boy asks Brad Pitt’s Achilles if he isn’t scared to fight the champion of the other army. It’s the biggest man the boy ever saw — he wouldn’t want to fight him, no way in hell. He’s a clever kid, actually; most of us would be absolutely demolished in a fight with a giant soldier. Achilles keeps a cool head. He tells the boy his name will not be remembered — Achilles is kind of a dick in the 2004 film. But he’s right… the ones we remember, are the ones who did the unthinkable. The ones who took the risks, and lived to tell the tale. Or at least, accomplished enough amazing acts witnessed by others, for those others to live and tell their tales. There are a LOT of brave people we don’t remember — they’re every bit as brave as Achilles was. They, too, go and fight the impossible fight, against the impossible opponent. And 99% of them get slaughtered immediately. We never hear of those heroes. That boy? He probably lived to a ripe old age and was a hero in the eyes of his family. We don’t know his name. Does it matter?

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is “toxic masculinity” a scam to turn men into beta males?
Answer: First of all, no truly “manly man” will use terms like “beta males” without a hint of irony. So please, drop that… it’s unbecoming of a gentleman. Makes you look like a whiny little no-lifer. Now as for this whole toxic masculinity business, it’s largely bullshit. I mean sure — some of the expectations we have of men aren’t fair, and are hard to live up to. We should go a little easier on men, at times. Go a little easier on ourselves, too. But does showing kindness to men mean we should coddle people, that we should embrace weakness, overly emotional responses, and hysterics, and label them a virtue? Because not keeping a cool head under pressure isn’t a virtue. Getting down and dirty to earn a living and taking a beating and fight back like man, THAT is a virtue. Life chews us all up, and spits us out. And yes, it sucks. But what goes ever did crying about it, to anyone? No, I’m not of the belief that “everything used to be better”. Because objectively, that hasn’t been true for most of history. But there’s way too much posturing, too much hysterics, too much whiny attention grabbing and too many “think pieces” from people who never had an original thought pop up into their heads — and half of them contain buzzwords like “toxic masculinity” or “the patriarchy”. Much of the ‘social commentary’ today from people who studies this type of thing (yes, there are studies…) boil down to “straight men bad, especially white ones, everyone else pitiful and oppressed”. It’s tiresome as hell. The constant hammering on “toxic masculinity”, the constant complaining about “men are trash”, the constant barrage of feminist buzzwords all across social media by people who couldn’t coherently explain even a third of their theories… it’s too much. Men are amazing. We’re glorious, powerful creatures. We are half of this earth’s population, most of our leaders are men, our great and powerful historical figures, our icons, the authors of our holy books. Enough with the neverending quest to shame men for being men — all that does is drive them into the ‘other camp’ where they’ll embrace false Gods like Andrew Tate.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is it true that the Japanese emperor is the only current emperor in the world?
Answer: He is. The Japanese Emperor Naruhito is the only man with the title Emperor in the world. No other country still has a similar titled ruler or figurehead — he’s the “last man standing”. The Kaiser is long dead, the Tsar is, too. Naruhito stands alone, the sole head of a family tree that first entered recorded human history 2600 years ago. So the ancestors of Naruhito, 64, were already ruling Japan 600 years before the birth of Christ. And the bloodline is fragile. The family tree small. Only the direct male line matters — any female member of the family has to leave the royal family and the line of succession upon marriage. Only the sons of sons can apply. Naruhito, for the record, has no sons, only a daughter. His brother only has one son. His nephew, therefore, is the only heir to the throne. Should Naruhito’s nephew only father daughters, like Naruhito himself and some of his uncles, the Japanese imperial bloodline in direct male line will die out. There is only one Emperor in the world — and only one heir to his throne. A legacy of 2600 years never before looked so fragile.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was Trump right when he said the debate was rigged?
Answer: Yes, it was. In the sense that CNN organized the debate in such a way that they thought their set-up would help Biden come across better. They were also betting on the mic-off rules startling Trump and possibly causing a meltdown… The problem? CNN and many in more liberal spheres — myself included — have fallen for a trap. As Tony Montana used to say, “Never get high on your own supply!” They bought into the fairy tale of Trump, the raving, ranting madman. Versus calm, collected, has-his-wits-about-him Biden. Biden, who since 2020 only does well on strictly scripted performances. With the world hyperfocused on the issue of Biden’s age and frailty, all Trump needed to do was appear “presidential”. And CNN helped him do it by enforcing strict time limits on questions. Trump kept his cool, spoke clearly and relatively coherently. And Biden, without an earpiece, autocue or script? Bombed. CNN had expected Trump, instead, to bomb. They forgot he always talks shit confidently on the fly — it’s his biggest selling point. The debate was designed to cause Trump to lose his shit, to become frustrated and angry. To shout and try to disrupt Biden’s answers, to act aggressive and nasty, much like Trump did in the 2020 presidential debate which he came out of looking badly. And then… he didn’t. Faced with a whispering, frail Biden frequently losing his train of thought, Trump must have known from the very first minute that this was his night. That the stage was his, and that victory was all-but certain. Truth matters little when it’s a faint, confused whisper… and lies, presented with gusto, carry the night. Instead of attacking Biden on a personal level, Trump at times almost seemed to pity his opponent… he felt no need to be vicious, because the debate was the verbal equivalent of Mike Tyson fighting a sweet old grandpa.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Will a narcissist go out of their way to hurt you?
Answer: A lot of the people answering this question do not seem to know narcissism very well. Because “the narcissist”, as in a monolith, does not exist. There are different types of narcissists in this world, as you will see with any mental disorder — there are the low functioning, and the high functioning. Will a high functioning narcissist feel compelled to go out of his way, just to hurt you? Really go that extra mile, make revenge into a major priority, overruling all other needs until the thirst for it is quenched? Maybe. But it’s far from certain. Does revenge benefit the narcissist? A high functioning narcissist knows when to “tone down” this vengeful nature, the way a high functioning alcoholic still loves to drink, yet knows when not to. And how to handle the liquor. A narcissist, when he or she perceives you as having “wronged” them, may commit an act of revenge. But it will be calculated. There may not be any “lashing out”. Most of the pain the narcissist inflicts, isn’t inflicted purposely — it is inflicted carelessly. “Will doing X hurt my partner?” isn’t a thought that would pop up into the head of a narcissist. Unless it’s an ex-partner, and the act of vengeance, however petty, is easy to pull off. Low effort, high reward. In this case, some nastiness may occur. The narcissist wants closure, wants to see the impact the relationship has had on you. How you need him madly, and will never be the same again. You have to give something. In short, will narcissists go “out of their way” to hurt you? Yes, at times. But not necessarily. Causing pain wherever the narcissist goes is part of the deal. It goes with the disorder. Sometimes there’s sadism involved. And sometimes obsession makes a narcissist go to extreme lengths. Sometimes. But it’s just as likely you’ll just end up tossed to the trash like a used towel and forgotten about as soon as a new target appears.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What's the last song you listened to?
Answer: The full title is: cassö, RAYE, D-Block Europe - Prada (Extended to 8 minutes) It’s a remix from the British singer Raye, who goes by Rachel Agatha Keen. The song is catchy, the beat tickles my bone and even the singer, herself, is rather easy on the eye. Lately I have been getting into various different types of music — drum and bass, house music, and a shitload of remixes. Here’s the song, btw: Now there’s one other song I adore, it’s by Vangelis — The Drums of Gaugamela. It’s the soundtrack of the defining battle scene from Oliver Stone’s epic movie Alexander. An underrated film, one I would recommend you only watch in the extended edition because it’s far superior to the theatrical cut. I’m a man of eclectic tastes. One moment Raye sings “I got strippers tits in my face” to the beat of a house remix and the next moment, Vangelis musically accompanies one of the most epic battles in all of Antiquity. Music has great power. It pumps you up, inspires you. It makes you hungry for life, eager to move. Eager to lift weights, to exercise, to dance, to make love. Music is life. I forget it sometimes. And then, I remember. And I’m always grateful whenever I do.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is President Biden likely to drop out of the 2024 presidential race?
Answer: It’s too early tell. But honestly, he should. Joe Biden just got absolutely massacred in his first televised debate with former President Trumo. That’s Biden’s wife, Jill, helping him off stage after the debate in the picture below. On November, Joe Biden turns 82. And he’s old. Old, and tired. His voice is raspy. Yes, he can give a scripted speech well enough on a good day — his State of the Union address was excellent — but it isn’t enough. It’s nowhere near enough. Within minutes after the debate ended, news articles started popping up suggesting Biden should step down. Forbes is now profiling other potential presidential options that could take over the reigns… Before the debate? Trump was the one who seemed scared. His party was going on about how Biden would be “drugged up” and at times it appeared as if Trump would weasel out of the debate altogether… truthfully? They had no idea how bad Biden had truly gotten, cognitively. Because you always see the man behind an autocue, and he does well enough with that. A long televised debate before the eyes of the world? It was too much for Biden to handle. His team says “he had a cold”… spare me the excuses. The man is old, and his mind is gone. I lost my own grandfather to senile dementia just three years ago — I know the symptoms. There’s no spinning this. If the Democratic party cares one iota about winning in November, or losing with any dignity left — they’ll replace Joe Biden with someone young, energetic, coherent and charismatic. Not because Joe Biden has been a terrible president — I quite like his administration — but because there’s no way an audience will believe him capable of running the nation for another four years after this disastrous performance. Let the old man mercifully retire, live out his days amidst his children and grandchildren, like any old man after a long life of service to his nation.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is Joe Biden afraid to debate President Trump?
Answer: No… he wasn’t afraid to debate Trump. But he should have been. I’m watching a livestream of the 2024 CNN presidential debate right now. And I’m watching Joe Biden just dying on stage. It’s painful. It’s tragic. Anyone who has read a substantial number of my answers over the years knows I’m a “ridin’ with Biden” type of guy. But holy shit! He’s being butchered. Trump speaks much more clearly, much more coherently. And Biden just… whispers. Sometimes his whispering makes sense. Sometimes it doesn’t. But he’s hard to hear, hard to follow at times. I’m just, watching the man fall apart. So many media outlets keps saying this debate would be a “game changer”. And I’m starting to feel they’re right… whenever it’s Trump’s turn speaking, I just see Biden looking dazed, confused, his facial movements seem off. His voice seems off. He tries, he struggles, and it’s uncomfortable. No way he’s winning votes or changing minds here — not in a positive way, anyway. I mean sure, Trump bullshits. He always does. But he does it confidently, in a clear voice and he’s remarkably coherent tonight. Meanwhile all I can think of whenever Biden is talking is “please drink some water, Sir.” This is painful. Just thirty minutes in and I’m already wondering how Biden’s presidential campaign will survive this massacre.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What would Emperor Meiji have thought of the Me Too movement?
Answer: This is the weirdest question I have been asked since I joined Quora. But I’ll answer it anyway, because it intrigues me. I reckon Emperor Meiji would be sitting on a comfortable chair in one of the rooms of his palace, fidgeting with a sword or doing some calligraphy. A purple-haired time-traveller with a nose ring enters his chambers, asking him what he thinks of #MeToo and the Emperor raises a bushy eyebrow in surprise — he has no clue what the strange fellow is saying. “What does this person want of me?” the great Emperor demands to know, his booming voice a mixture of intrigue and annoyance. “He’s from the future, Your Majesty,” a servant responds, “but his language is foreign. I think it’s the language of the big-nosed people from America…” “Hmmm,” says Meiji, frowning, “go and get me an interpreter that speaks their tongue!” An interpreter is brought in, with some delays. He explains what #MeToo is. The Emperor continues to frown throughout the explanation, at times amused, but increasingly more annoyed and somewhat depressed by the end of the explanation… “So THIS is what people worry about in the future?” asks Meiji “Yes, Your Majesty… They worry about people fondling actresses against their will…” “Ha! I fondle actresses for breakfast…” booms Meiji, “what nonsense! Ask him something useful! Ask him what became of my beloved Japan!” The interpreter asks the strange visitor what became of Japan in the 21st century. Upon hearing the explanation, Emperor Meiji no longer frowns. Nor does he smile. He weeps. Then, the Emperor calls for his son, Taisho. “Listen, about this son of yours…” he starts.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What's the worst thing about the current society?
Answer: An American man named Jeronimo Guerra was fixing his wife’s car in the first week of June, 2024, when it collapsed on top of him. Pinned beneath the vehicle, Guerra yelled for help… none came. Several bystanders saw he was in distress and simply went on their way. One man went to Guerra and, rather than helping him, reached into the pockets of the man’s jeans and took out his wallet, stealing it. Jeronimo’s daughter came to collect her father and found him dead and robbed. No one had come to his aid, no one had alerted authorities, and by the time she reached him, the weight of the car had crushed and killed him. Guerra was only 57. He leaved behind a son, a daughter and two young grandchildren who will now never get to know their grandfather. There’s something intensely cynical about life, when the first thing people think when they encounter a man fighting for his life isn’t the urge to save his life… but to rob him, instead. The worst thing about our society? People are heartless, and callous. They mind their own business, and only make your business theirs when there’s profit in it for them. There are still good people in this world, sure — but if you’re ever in trouble and none of those good people are around, you’d be shocked by the amount of bystanders who would simply let you perish and go on their merry way, ignoring your plight or even robbing you as you struggle for breath.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can you name any siblings of famous historical figures who achieved fame alongside them but not to the same level?
Answer: I didn’t know that Jesus had a brother, but apparently he did. He’s called James, or “James the Just” because he was such a fabulously swell and righteous guy. Wikipedia even has a whole page on James, and the page is literally titled “James, brother of Jesus”.[1] James was an early Church leader and was eventually martyred for his faith, dying by the hands of his enemies — they threw him off the roof of a temple and beat him to death. Catholics and Orthodox Christians have this strange obsession with the Virgin Mary having always remained a virgin… just having been chaste before conceiving Jesus alone wasn’t enough, no, she had to have never been touched by poor ol’ Joseph. In their tradition, James isn’t a full brother of Jesus, but rather a half-brother from Joseph’s first marriage. I can’t believe I’ve gotten through 32 years on God’s green earth and never having known until today that Jesus Christ had a brother. And that his brother was called James, and that this James was a church leader, a preacher and a martyr. Must be hard to live in the shadow of a brother of the caliber of Christ himself.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the most well-known or controversial cover of TIME magazine?
Answer: One well-known example would be the 1943 cover when Stalin was named “Person of the Year” by TIME Magazine. It’s remarkable, knowing all that we now know of the man… and knowing what he would later do, and what would be done in his name. Stalin, the tough guy, the hero who “stood up to Hitler”… Historical amnesia is a very real, and powerful affliction. People all too easily forget that it was Stalin who, together with Hitler, started WWII by invading Poland — Stalin taking the Eastern half, Hitler the Western half. In Katyn, Stalin marched tens of thousands of Polish military officers, civil leaders, clerks and politicians into a forest and had them summarily executed and buried in the frozen snow. In 1939, Stalin was a villain… by 1943, he was a hero, standing up to the ‘greater’ evil that was Hitler. Speaking of interesting choices for a cover… Hitler, himself, was “Person of the Year” in 1938. Now of course, some will defend TIME by claiming the person of the year isn’t a wholesale endorsement of the man on the cover — the person is merely the ‘most consequential’ person of that year. Still, the controversy continues. And given the tens of millions of victims of both Hitler and Stalin, understandably so.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Can sculpture be funny? And what is an example of a hilarious sculpture?
Answer: Oh, absolutely they can be! Like the wax statue someone placed in Washington DC over the weekend in late June 2024. It was a statue depicting the legendary president Abraham Lincoln. And sure enough, he started off looking mighty regal as always… The problem… the wax statue was made and placed in a public square right before a historic heatwave hit the American capital. And the heat caused the statue to melt, as tends to happen with wax when it heats up… The result were hilarious. Because all of a sudden, good ol’ Abe Lincoln no longer looks quite as regal. He went from ‘presidential figure posing sternly’ to ‘Mr. Lincoln having a private moment with Mary Todd’ real quick.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which historical figures deserve veneration?
Answer: The biggest issue I have with historical figures… so many of the great Kings and Emperors of yore didn’t lead from the front. They commanded far behind enemy lines, away from the action. Not Alexander! Alexander the Great was ALWAYS in the thick of it. When his troops wanted to desert him, Alexander spoke to them. His words are immortal, forever etched in my mind. He stood before his men. His battle-wary, tired, exhausted men. And he showed them his body in perhaps the most epic, chilling power move in history. All across his skin, scars. Scars from every weapon known at the time — daggers, swords, spears, arrows, clubs, rocks. His whole body was covered in them from head to toe but he was still standing, muscular, powerful and mighty as he always had been. Nothing could slow this man down. “Notice this,” Alexander said, allowing for a dramatic pause as all eyes were on him, “all these scars are ONLY on the front of my body. For I never deserted you, I never retreated, I never sent you anywhere I didn’t go first myself. Never asked of you anything I wouldn’t ask of myself!” The mutiny ended right there.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is the Dutch far-right leader Geert Wilders quite all there?
Answer: He’s a fascinating chap, Geert Wilders. He was a firebrand anti-establishment leader for almost two decades, head of the opposition in the Netherlands. Then, in 2023, he won a shitload of seats in the Dutch parliament and his party was able to assume power — sort of. See Wilders had to… tone down his rhetoric. He couldn’t go around calling hijabs “head-rags” and insist those who wear them must pay “head-rags-tax”. Nor could he go around giving speeches, asking his followers if they want “more, or less Moroccans in the country?” and them chanting back: “Less! Less! Less!” as he looks on in adoration. No, Wilders couldn’t do that. The Dutch followers of them man jokingly call him “Geert Milders” now — a pun on the word “mild” because he’s milder now. One of Wilders’ new ministers even had to explain recently how “white replacement theory” is “Neo-Nazi rhetoric” and “dangerous”. This wouldn’t have happened a year ago. Geert Wilders is a calculating politician. So he changed his tone. Became Geert Milders. A neutral politician from an allied center-right party (Schoof) was pushed forward as Prime Minister, with Wilders’ party providing some of the ministers. And Wilders rules from the shadows, it is assumed. Is he “quite all there”? I’d say he is. He’s a very savvy politician.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is life too hard for us?
Answer: A picture I saw yesterday stayed with me… it’s the wife and two sons of Julian Assange, waiting for him outside of prison. Assange made his own life hard through the choices he made — and in a sense, we all do. In his case, he did it because he felt a higher calling. He wanted to inform the world of things governments do in the shadows. Including war crimes by the Americans in Iraq and Afghanistan. For his efforts, Assange spent years in a foreign embassy as an essential prisoner, followed by several years in jail. Those little boys in the photo only ever saw their father briefly during “visiting hour” in jail, a few times a year. And yes, he could have gone the easy way. Lived an easy life. He was a man of considerable skill and talent, after all. But he made a choice not to. A choice to inform us and ruin his life in the process of doing so. He’s free, now, going to Australia to recover with his family in peace, following a plea deal with the American government. Why is life hard for us? We make life hard. Through our choices, and our actions. But the irony is that if we didn’t make choices that made our lives hard, at times, we’d make life even harder for others. Change isn’t born in comfort, and truth isn’t revealed without a price.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What were the unorthodox treatments Adolf Hitler received from his personal doctor?
Answer: During 1944, ill health and stress caught up with Hitler in a most unexpected way… he could no longer make his little Führer properly salute Eva Braun at night. Theodor Morell, Hitler’s personal physician, came up with a rather strange concoction — he created a potion using the semen and part of the prostate gland of bulls, and injected Hitler with this primitive viagra.[1] Whether the concoction actually was effective or if it was placebo effect, we’ll never know, but apparently Adolf and Eva continued to wrestle at night just fine after this — Morell’s remedy was successful. He had Hitler on a shitload of medication, for the record… among them, crystal meth. He also administered small doses of the poison strychnine to help with his chronic flatulance (likely another side effect of the 28+ medications Morell had him take daily)… it’s kind of funny how details such as these kill the mystery and appeal of Hitler; he was merely a horny old man who farted a lot, rather than the evil genius enigma many make him out to be. Theodor Morell was such a terrible quack and destroyed Hitler’s health so terribly that some of the Allies later speculated he may have been a secret agent out to slowly poison and destroy the German dictator — personally I’m just of the opinion that he was merely a very, very bad and rather immoral doctor who turned Hitler into his personal guinea pig for weird experimental treatments. Had Hitler not killed himself in 1945, then Morell surely would have, sooner or later.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did God create homosexuals as a means of population control?
Answer: Scientifically proven, studies have found that the mothers, sisters and aunts of gay men have more children on average than the mothers, sisters and aunts of straight men.[1] So the relatives of gays are more fertile than those of straight people. This is kind of the opposite of population control — it would seem that there is an evolutionary benefit to having a gay relative. Strictly anecdotally speaking, but I lived in the Philippines for a while. And just about three thirds of all hairdressers were gay men. The men working in the salons, and those doing the cutting. It’s a poor country, and these are respectable business owners. Some earned quite decent incomes from their work. They’d have no kids of their own — the Philippines has no gay marriage — and would put numerous nieces, nephews and younger siblings through college. If all a gay person ever did was chase bed partners and be a hedonist, there’d be no evolutionary purpose to homosexuality. But since quite a few gay men (and lesbian women) are rather generous to their blood relatives, this generosity is more likely to boost the fertility rates of their relatives, rather than lower them. At least it does in tight-knit families and communities.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are modern movies woke propaganda?
Answer: Some of them are. Especially when they turn white characters into black, asian, gay, just to force “representation”… Just take EXISTING heroes from history that are already a ‘minority’ and give them their time in the sun. Dedicate films to men like Nana Asamani. See in Accra on the coast of the African country of Ghana, in the year 1693, a legendary man named Nana Asamani appeared at the gates of Danish trading post Christiansborg Castle. Asamani was a simple man dressed in simple attire — he claimed to be a trader, and wanted to “buy cannons” from the Danes. The Danes let the trader into the castle, where he joked around with them, bantered and asked to “see the goods”. They showed Nana Asamani the guns. He inspected them. Got some of his assistents to inspect them, too. The mood was friendly, jovial. At some point Asamani requested to fire one of the cannons. One of the Danes showed him how it was done. Asamani’s assistens then revealed guns they carried under their robes — they took over and loaded the castle’s guns and aimed them at the Danes. The leader of the Danish trading post fled for his life, jumping out the window to his death. At which point the others surrendered the arms and gave Nana Asamani the keys to the castle. For one year, from 1693 until 1694, Nana Asamani ruled as governor of Christiansborg Castle in Accra. He ran the trading post and traded with the English and the Dutch on equal terms. Then, in 1694, he allowed the Danish to buy back their trading post for a hefty sum. And Nana Asamani, the man on the statue above, rode into the sunset a rich and satisfied man, like the absolute legend he was. Now these are the films I’d like to watch — films where the non-white main character is a hero, not a victim, and he or she actually existed.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What did Michael Jackson mean by “Jew me”?
Answer: In a lyric from his 1995 song “The Don’t Care About Us”. In it, Michael Jackson sings: Beat me, hate me You can never break me Will me, thrill me You can never kill me Jew me, sue me Everybody, do me Kick me, kike me Don't you black or white me “Jew me, sue me… kick me, kike me…” It caused a major controversy. People called Jackson “antisemitic” for it. He defended himself, saying the song was meant to “denounce all racism” and that he “loves all races”. In his song Jackson assumed the role of various groups… “I am the white man, the black man, the Jew, the skinhead, all in one song,” he explained. It wasn’t meant to be malicious. But was taken that way, anyway. Jackson also explained he “has many Jewish friends” who loved the song. He explained it well enough, but the controversy still continued. Director Spike Lee famously came to Jackson defense saying many rappers used the N-word and even John Lennon did in a song, so why could Jackson not use “Jew me” and “kike” in a song? Jackson eventually changed the lyrics quietly.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the most emotionally powerful paintings?
Answer: It has to be the beautifully haunting painting below, named Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan by Russian painter Ilya Repin. The expression on Ivan’s face is just remarkable. He’s completely in shock and disbelief over what he has just done — beat to death his son and heir in a fit of anger. Ivan had several sons, but all died young except for two — his eldest, Ivan, and feeble-minded Feodor. Killing his only strong heir and namesake, leaving only intellectually-disabled Feodor to take his place, Ivan the Terrible knew that he doomed his bloodline and dynasty forever. He cradles his dying son in his arms, fully aware of how one brutal blow just ended his entire legacy and wiped out everything he’s worked for all his life… Anyone who is a parent, and has held a newborn baby in his or her arms, knows the powerful surge of love that bursts through the core of your very being… that’s your little boy or girl, right there. Oh, you die for that baby! Crawl to hell and back for it. Here, we see Ivan Senior cradling Ivan Junior… in his death, the son is once more a baby, helpless, vulnerable in his father’s arms — but it is the father who made him that reduced him to this state.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why does the Democrat party hate America?
Answer: A very telling image is the one below — two older gentlemen at a Trump rally, about eight years ago. On their shirts, we read the words: “I’d rather be a Russian than a Democrat!” What would you say of the patriotism of these men? Personally, I find it rather… lacking. These men aren’t Democrats, evidently. One of them has a MAGA hat on — Make America Great Again. In Soviet Russia, they would call such men “useful idiots”. Vladimir Putin is banking on people like this to get Trump elected in November.[1] A Trump victory would weaken the NATO alliance significantly, cut support for Ukraine and give Russia a much better chance at ending the war on terms favorable to Moscow. A geopolitical victory for Russia, not to mention China and other American rival powers. The question that pops into my head now is this… who really hates America the most? The party of “bleeding heart progressives” who, at times, seem tiresome and pandering? Or the party openly praising genocidal fascist dictatorships and being proud of it because “at least they’re not Democrats”? You tell me.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Does a man of God need to work?
Answer: The finest priests I have known were men’s men. They weren’t afraid to roll up their sleeves and get down and dirty when they needed to. They would give a sermon in different communities — some of them quite remote. And they would get on their motorcycles and cross rough terrain, climb mountains, brave rough weather conditions, just to speak the word of the Lord to those people. Who do you think builds the churches in faraway places? It’s priests like this. These priests, they didn’t have clean hands. They were rough, calloused. In the evening after a hard day’s work, tending to the ill, comforting the dying, joining festivities and funeral rites… they would have a drink. Some brandy, for courage. A late night call would call them away from bed, once more. Someone nearing the end, in need of solace. Finally, bed. Rest. Sleep. Only a few hours, and at the breaking of dawn, another brutal day… Yes, a man of God needs to work, if he’s any good at his job, he’ll work like a mule and still get complaints and criticism all around. There are priests who are abusive, lazy, nasty, decadent… their clothes are perfectly fitting, clean, tidy, just as their rooms are. And they’re not “Godly” at all. The best priests and pastors are simple, hard-working men. Like Jesus, the carpenter. Hard men with soft souls.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: ? What is more socially acceptable today, than forty years ago?
Answer: Forty years ago there would NEVER be an article written about how “Drag Queens in the Classroom Teach Inclusion and Fun, Offering a World of Imagination”… and no, I’m not kidding. This is a genuine article with that actual title. By “Teen Vogue”.[1] Draq queens in classrooms, “offering a world of imagination”… and nightmares, I reckon. It’s a famous conservative talking point lately, especially in America — haven’t seen much of it in Europe, thankfully. But yeah that’s… not something people would be even remotely cool with forty years ago. They write about wanting children to be “okay with inclusivity” and influence them in a “playful way”. The article: People change. Times change. But more than anything, people become passive. They are still bothered by many of the same things they woudl have been bothered by forty years ago. But the response is different… weaker. Subdued. We complain, but we don’t act. Forty years ago, things that are being done now, ideas being normalized by authorities and advocacy groups, wouldn’t even have been considered. Let alone take place. There’d never be a debate about whether or not drag queens should be reading to children at schools — it simply wouldn’t occur.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the anti-immigrant movement in Europe? Where and why did it start?
Answer: As good a starting point as any, in recent history, would be British politician Enoch Powell giving a speech in 1968.[1] The now legendary and oft-despised “Rivers Of Blood” speech… As I look ahead, I am filled with foreboding; like the Roman, I seem to see 'the River Tiber foaming with much blood'. The speech as a whole is fascinating: “Here is a decent, ordinary fellow Englishman, who in broad daylight in my own town says to me, his Member of Parliament, that the country will not be worth living in for his children. I simply do not have the right to shrug my shoulders and think about something else. What he is saying, thousands and hundreds of thousands are saying and thinking—not throughout Great Britain, perhaps, but in the areas that are already undergoing the total transformation to which there is no parallel in a thousand years of English history. We must be mad, literally mad, as a nation to be permitting the annual inflow of some 50,000 dependents, who are for the most part the material of the future growth of the immigrant descended population. It is like watching a nation busily engaged in heaping up its own funeral pyre. So insane are we that we actually permit unmarried persons to immigrate for the purpose of founding a family with spouses and fiancées whom they have never seen…” People sometimes think this “anti-immigrant movement” is recent, when it isn’t — it’s been around for well over half a century, if not longer. Many of these statements made by Powell in 1968 could be seen repeated through the years by current-day politicians… albeit much less eloquently. Sentences such as “watching a nation busily engaged in heaping up its own funeral pyre” are quite above the pay grade of the likes of Nigel Farage, Wilders or Le Pen. There has been for a long time a movement of people in Europe that are wary or even terrified of the effects of mass immigration. It is NOT a recent development at all. It’s just that the consequences the likes of Powell warned of in 1968 weren’t exactly around the corner just yet… now, they’re here, and the movement has reached new heights. Even in America, nation of immigrants, the subject of immigration may yet decide the 2024 elections and the fate of the world.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Will the white European population really be replaced by Muslim, African, and non-white immigrants in general?
Answer: According to virtually all available statistics, the birth rate of European-born women continues to decline year after year. Whereas the birth rate of non-European born women inside Europe does not — it’s largely stable.[1] So is the European population being replaced? Yes. Yes, it is. It isn’t some “racist dogwhistle”… it’s facts. Cold, hard facts and statistics. European people, the ones born in Europe, born into the culture, are suffering from ever-dwindling birth rates. The same cannot be said of many of the new arrivals… and while it is true that people from immigrant communities often do see a significant decrease in their own birth rates within a generation or two, they also remain slightly higher overall. So yes, are white people being “replaced”? It seems that way. What you can argue about is who is doing the ‘replacing’. Some would blame grand conspiracy theories involving bad actors among the world’s elites… others like myself believe that we, ultimately, “replace” ourselves. You can’t love others if you don’t love yourself, after all. Can’t sustain your own population if you have no love for your own population.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is convicted felon Donald John Trump capable of kindness, mercy, and empathy?
Answer: In 2018, Donald Trump gave a posthumous pardon to famous black heavyweight boxer Jack Johnson. Johnson had transported a white woman across state lines “for the purpose of prostitution or debauchery, or for any other immoral purpose.” A Jim Crow era law designed to criminize black people from sleeping with whites.[1] That’s mercy, isn’t it? Kindness, too, I’d say. Because sure enough, Johnson was long dead… but justice is important, even when it’s delivered mighty late. Even a century later, to Johnson’s surviving relatives, however distantly removed from the man… things like these matter. A cynic could see them as mere theatrics to get the “black vote”. And who knows, maybe that really is all there is to it… But yes, any man is capable of kindness. Even Donald J. Trump. You may question the motivation behind any act of kindness or mercy from a demonstrably unkind person. But a kind act is a kind act, anyway you cut it.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the most disturbing image you saw today?
Answer: A man named Homer Peel kisses his wife, Geneva Peel, in 1937. She was just ten years old, and an oprhan. Peel lied to authorities initially and told them Geneva was twelve… child marriage had just been made illegal in the state of Tennessee — but Homer Peel claimed he had “saved” Geneva from the poor house, and that to annul the marriage would be to return her to a state of poverty. The picture above is Homer kissing Geneva after a judge agreed them his reasoning, refusing to undo the marriage and returning Geneva to her husband, twenty-four years older than her. He had reportedly “promised her a pretty new hat” for her loyaly. It was quite common in the 1930s for children to marry… they would typically marry men considerably older than them. It wasn’t until 1937 that a law prohibiting it came into existence, and even then, the practice continued. The photograph is jarring and unsettling for numerous reasons. Homer and Geneva Peel entually stayed together until 1975, when they got divorced. Homer died in 1991 and Geneva lived on until 2017, dying at 92. The couple had six daughters and a son together, and eighteen grandchildren.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the greatest real revenge story in recent history?
Answer: A friend of mine told this story far better than I hope to do… but a man named Udham Singh comes to mind. He waited 21 years to assassinate Michael O’Dwyer, lieutenant governor of Punjab. O’Dwyer was responsible for a massacre in 1919 in which as many as 1500 Indians were killed. Udham didn’t forget… he fled abroad and planned his revenge well. In the 1920s, Udham lived in America. He took a Mexican wife, Lupe, and had two sons. In 1927, he went to England and married an English woman. He lived a quiet life and kept to himself… then, in 1940, he used his wife’s name to purchase a ticket for an event in London at which O’Dwyer was said to appear. “He wanted to crush the spirit of my people, so I have crushed him!” yelled out Udham as he fired two fatal bullets… He wanted to crush the spirit of my people, so I have crushed him… powerful words, from a powerful man. Twenty-one years he waited for his vengeance. He married for it. Lived across different continents for it. And obtained it at last, in 1940. Udham Singh was hanged the same year. He died defiantly, saying he was sad he couldn’t take out more of his enemies.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Answer: Europe is NOT racist. More like the opposite — Europe loves other ethnicities almost more than it’s own local populace. Below we seen an overjoyed migrant posing for a selfie with Angela Merkel, former German leader. Merkel loved foreigners. The more, the merrier! Where from, who, how many? Doesn’t matter. All were welcome. Europe cannot afford to be “racist”… because Europe doesn’t produce anywhere near enough children to sustain it’s nations. When your birth rates are low, your people are largely dying out… what do you do? You try to entice your people to reproduce. Failing this, you import people. Migrant workers, to fill in the gaps. You can’t be picky, either — any pair of able hands is welcome. Of course the immigrants you so carelessly let in, come from cultures often vastly different from your own… and there will be tension. Some criminals slip through the cracks. Not everyone you let in is going to be an “upstanding citizen”. And some are incredibly conservative, don’t really see women as people and wipe their foreign asses with all your liberal and progressive European values… If anything, Europe hates itself. Answer: You know how much money the American defense industry made in 2023 alone? An astonishing 298.68 billion(!) dollars. It’s a business. All other potential rivals have been playing catch-up ever since — and as of 2024, none come even remotely close to taking over the spot of Top Dog.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What’s the biggest double life you’ve ever personally seen revealed?

With three other children Fritzl also fathered there by his own daughter. Fritzl was arrested in 2008, at the age of 73. Because he had brought one of the “dungeon kids” to the hospital along with Elizabeth, his captive daughter, who then alerted authorities. Josef Fritzl remains in prison in Austria of this writing. He believes he should be freed, famously telling a judge: “I am just one man. But look inside the basements of other people… you would be surprised what you find!”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are myths based on truth or are they purely for entertainment purposes?
Answer: People in the past came up with various legends to explain things they couldn’t quite comprehend fully. They were awfully practical people and so their explanations were of a practical nature. Myths entertained, too, and telling stories was a great way to kill time. Greek mythology featured a race of giant one-eyed monsters called the Cyclops. They were massive, had an enormous head and matching gigantic bodies… on their faces, a single eye in the middle of their forehead. Have you ever seen an elephant skull? Below is an elephant skull: It’s a giant skull. And in the middle of the forehead, we find a hole. It wasn’t an eyesocket — but it sure looks like it could have been one, especially to the untrained eye. Most Greeks would never have ventured far from their villages. Wouldn’t have traveled to Africa and encountered actual real-life elephants. Nor would they have seen their skulls. But ancient skulls of mammoths and primitive extinct elephant species were still buried in the grounds of ancient Greece. The bones were interpreted as being those of giant one-eyed monsters. Dragons were invented in medieval Europe and ancient China in a similar fashion — dinosaur bones were interpreted as the remains of fire-breathing monsters.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What fundamental differences, if any, must there be between human and artificial intelligence?

ChatGPT writes like a miscast high school film with 30-year-olds playing teenagers.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What puts a smile on your face?
Answer: More than 85 years ago, a young woman had earned all her credits at Stanford University. Her name? Virginia Hislop. Unexpected motherhood and marriage put an end to her educational career… Hislop devoted her life to her family, raising her children. But she still had all the credits. Fulfilled all the requirements. And it played in the back of her mind, always. That eternal “what if?” question. And today, at age 105, Virginia Hislop marched with the “fresh graduates” at Stanford. She wasn’t the freshest of them… but I dare you to find any face on that stage smiling more brightly. In attendance to the ceremony were Hislop’s family. Including her first daughter, the daughter for whom she gave up her initial graduation ceremony. Her grandchildren and even her great-grandchildren were present, too. All of them grown and aware of how special the moment was. This is the sort of thing that puts a smile on my face. People who defy the odds and embody so perfectly “never say never”. Age really is just a number when you’ve got the right attitude.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who is the longest-reigning female leader in European history?
Answer: It was this badass little lady below — Queen Elizabeth II. She was on the throne from 1952 until her death in 2022, never slowing down during her 70-year reign. In her free time, she rode horses, hunted and was a pretty cool person. Her family survived countless dramas and scandals, and she guided her nation through numerous historical struggles. She did it with style, and with grace. Even before she ascended the throne, she volunteered for the war effort in WWII and served as a truck driver and mechanic. While in the public eye and facing scrutiny and numerous scandals involving her children and grandchildren, the Queen maintained a steady marriage with her husband, Prince Philip, for 74 years. It’s been two years now since the Queen passed, and I still sometimes find myself missing her reassuring presence. She perfectly embodied that old saying: “They don’t make ’em like that anymore!” And certainly, they don’t.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is it true that gay pride month is evil?
Answer: It is kind of silly in a general sense to take pride in something you have no control over. According to religion, “pride” is a sin. One of the seven deadly sins, in fact. Now you can take pride in your work, of course… I mean maybe you just built a house. That’s neat! Go be proud of that. It took blood, sweat and tears to build that house, after all. Maybe you won a boxing match, or a marathon! Again, this took real effort. And this is a great and understandable source of pride. You could have written a novel. Or climbed a mountain. Raised a successful family and seen your children graduation university with flying colors. Pride without effort is… empty. For pride in something to be worth anything, there needs to be effort. Now you may argue — there’s the struggle to come out of the closet, to own up to being LGBT, this could in itself be seen as a struggle. It’s a fair point. But there’s still the fact that sexuality is innate, like the color of one’s skin, or nationality. So gay pride kind of opens the door to other ‘innate’ sources of pride — like being proud of your nationality, being proud of your race, etcetera. If you’re okay with one innate personal characteristic being a source of pride and given its own month… you should have the balls to provide ‘pride months’ to various other groups, too. Even those not marginalized. The fact that this isn’t done makes the whole thing appear hollow and disingenuous.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Do humanity really need gay people?
Answer: If you ever find yourself gazing at the beauty of the Sistine Chapel, remember… a gay man painted that. When you’re a Western European or British person and struggling to speak German, be grateful for Alan Turing — had he not helped win the war, perhaps you’d have spoken German now. Turing, a gay dude. You may watch any great movie, a movie that touches you, a movie that breaks your heart or inspires you to be a better man… and chances are there’s someone in the cast, an actor, actress, screenwriter behind the scenes, who’s gay. I absolutely love the Lord Of The Rings trilogy, for instance. And Gandalf is played by Sir Ian McKellen — a gay man. And God, do I love the hell out of those movies! There’s a lot of wonderful gifts we’ve been given over the years by gay people. “Oh but they cannot reproduce!” you may say. Sure they can — some just choose not to. Sir Isaac Newton wasn’t, to my knowledge, gay. Neither was Nikola Tesla. And yet neither of the two men had kids, either. So what is it, then, that excludes a gay man from the Pantheon of Greatness? Humanity needs good people of any background, any race or sexuality. It just needs them to be creative, hardworking, active and forces for good. It needs them to pursue whatever higher calling they may hear. And excel in their fields. Some of these people will be gay. Why on earth should this bother you? Even the greatest haters of gay people have, knowingly or unknowingly, benefitted from science invented or art created by someone gay.

Question: In your experience, how do sociopaths typically dehumanize other people? What's the underlying psychological process that leads to their apparent lack of empathy and ability to inflict harm without remorse?
Answer: It’s a case-by-case thing and depends on the situation. The sociopath would analyze the situation. And ask a question: “Does this person serve my needs?” It’s a very simple yes-or-no question. Either there is a benefit to be gained from interacting with someone, or there isn’t. The benefit can be anything, be it amusement, sex, financial gain or a boost in status. But there has to be benefit. People aren’t individuals so much as they’re walking, breathing “harvesting grounds”. They have value within — but this value relies solely on what they can do or give to the sociopath. The sociopath does not need to dehumanize others… they’re already dehumanized. There’s no specific thought process required, no mental gymnastics needed. For someone with empathy, it comes more or less natural. You have it. It’s there. And some people have more of it, sure. Some less. But there’s empathy. Not for the sociopath. For the sociopath, empathy has to be learned. Learned, or mimicked. It isn’t innately there. A normal, emotionally healthy person will have to justify bad behavior to him or herself. There needs to be a reason, an excuse, to act like a dickhead. The sociopath feels no such need… the sociopath will only formulate a reason for harm caused internally in case of being confronted by someone else — just to have something to say. They don’t need it for themselves.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why aren't we seeing gay themed war or hero movies?
Answer: I don’t know, honestly. There are plenty of candidates that would make fine movies. One is Neil Munro Roger, better known as Bunny Roger. Just look at the magnificent, square-jawed fellow he was! Bunny Roger wasn’t some wilting flower — he was all man. He just happened to be gay. Before WWII, he worked as a couturier and fashion designer in London. As soon as Germany attacked, he immediately signed up for the army. Roger was a dandy, always dressed to the nines. He was known for his wit and his courage under fire… he served in North Africa and Italy. Even with bullets flying around him, he’d cheer up his comrades, keep their spirits high. “When in doubt, powder heavily!” was one of his famed sayings. More than once he saved the lives of his fellow soldiers, dragging one from a burning building at the risk of his own life. In 1943, Roger was captured by the Germans after the Battle of Salerno. The Gestapo tortured him. One interrogator who spoke English asked him: “What are you doing here, Major Roger?” Bunny Roger spat out a tooth and said defiantly: “Shopping!” He managed to survive enemy captivity. After the war, Bunny Roger continued his career as a designer. Among his biggest contributions to the world of fashion we find the popularization of “Capri pants”. Why doesn’t this man have a movie? No idea. He probably doesn’t confirm to the stereotypes we tend to have of gay men — he was masculine as hell. And also gay as hell, being expelled from Oxford University as a young lad for “homosexual activities”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are celebrities actually nice?
Answer: Some of them are, some of them aren’t… kind of like with ‘normal people’. James Gandolfini is a fine example of a celebrity who was a genuinely nice in real life. While playing on The Sopranos, he was fiercely protective and paternal towards his on-screen daughter, Jamie-Lynn Sigler. She was diagnosed with muscle disease MS on the show, and it devastated her. Sigler didn’t tell any of her castmates of the diagnosis, and no one asked… she would have dizzy spells, muscle pains, and have to take many bathroom breaks during scenes as the disease affected her bladder — no one would bothered to ask, everyone just got grumpy as her health interrupted filming. Gandolfini was the only person who asked “are you okay?” and Sigler told him of her illness. She asked him not to tell anyone — and he didn’t.[1] He just quietly helped her get through it. It wasn’t until Gandolfini’s death, ten years later, that Sigler found out something else about him… for over a decade, without telling anyone, he had been giving generous donations to foundations aimed at fighting the disease his co-star suffered from. A genuinely good person does good quietly — kindness requires no accolades.

Question: What are the red flags of online dating?
Answer: The general rule that applies for journalism applies for online dating, too: “Trust, but verify.” When you are talking to someone in another country, you will want to make sure IMMEDIATELY that the person is legit and not some Nigerian dude pretending to be your sweetheart. They’re crafty — but webcams don’t lie! Aside from scammers, there’s also the issue of people not being as attractive as they appear in a profile picture — there’s makeup, there’s also filters. And then there is the surprisingly common habit of people using OLD PICTURES where they still looked young and fit, to hide weight gain or hair loss. To combat this? Tell the person you talk to upfront that you want to see them on camera. Tell them you’re not some pervert, you don’t need to “see the goods”. You just want to verify that the person you think you’re talking to is the actual person they claim to be. In my experience, most people will agree to a video call almost instantly. It also puts them ease to know that I am the man I claim to be, myself. Those who refuse for whatever reason are better left alone. If someone acts dodgy and makes excuses not to call? Cut your losses and move on. Be ruthless — time is precious, too precious to waste of flakes and fakes.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some of the most unforgettable moments in history?
Answer: In Accra on the coast of the African country of Ghana, in the year 1693, a legendary man named Nana Asamani appeared at Danish trading post Christiansborg Castle. Asamani was a simple man dressed in simple attire — he claimed to be a trader, and wanted to “buy cannons” from the Danes. The Danes let the trader into the castle, where he joked around with them, bantered and asked to “see the goods”. They showed Nana Asamani the guns. He inspected them. Got some of his assistents to inspect them, too. The mood was friendly, jovial. At some point Asamani requested to fire one of the cannons. One of the Danes showed him how it was done. Asamani’s assistens then revealed guns they carried under their robes — they took over and loaded the castle’s guns and aimed them at the Danes. The leader of the Danish trading post fled for his life, jumping out the window to his death. At which point the others surrendered the arms and gave Nana Asamani the keys to the castle. For one year, from 1693 until 1694, Nana Asamani ruled as governor of Christiansborg Castle in Accra. He ran the trading post and traded with the English and the Dutch on equal terms. Then, in 1694, he allowed the Danish to buy back their trading post for a hefty sum. And Nana Asamani, the man on the statue above, rode into the sunset a rich and satisfied man, like the absolute legend he was.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the lowest recorded IQ in history and how was it tested?
Answer: There are people who are profoundly mentally disabled — you cannot test them. They do not comprehend the test. Human language is alien to them. I have met such people… it was tragic. Once, a couple me and my former wife were friends with had to give birth. So they went off to the hospital and had us take care of their two oldest children. The first of whom was profoundly mentally retarded. It wasn’t pleasant. The boy couldn’t talk, at all. Couldn’t communicate. He mostly just uttered a stream of gutteral, caveman-esque sounds. Whatever popped into his mind would do — take a dump on the street? Sure. Piss against a car? Yup. Drop his trousers and start to masturbate in a crowded street? Why the hell not. I could have argued he was almost like a monkey in human form, but that’d be un unfair comparison, as Coco the Gorilla and her impressive sign language vocabulary definitely would put the fellow to shame. I was in awe of the parents — twenty-four hours of caring for the kid and I was exhausted. For them, it was a life sentence. I don’t know if his IQ was thirty, or sixty. Or below zero. I just know it can’t have been high. Or I hope it wasn’t, because if it was, it’d be a truly cruel and unjust punishment to be imprisoned in a mind so profoundly unfit for life.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is considered the biggest medical scam in history?
Answer: It costs between 2 and 4 dollars to produce a vial of Insulin. Yet it has always been sold for way more — in 1996, one vial sold for about 25 bucks. And as of now, one vial costs, on average, about 250 dollars. This stands in stark contrast to the creator of the drug, Sir Fredrick Banting. Who famously refused to patent his invention because it belonged not to him but “to the world”. There’s something intensely cynical about this to me. A drug that’s literally vital for the survival of millions of people suffering from diabetes. And yet to some pharmaceutical companies, it’s just another way to make a buck. Literally over the dead bodies of patients — there are cases of people in the past without insurance in America dying because of this. I can’t imagine in what way, in what world, this is anywhere moral or just. And how the CEOs of such companies justify this blatant cruelty. The same can be said for various other medicines — they’re often relatively cheap to make. But sell for much, much more than they cost to produce. I understand that companies need some profit. I understand you have to keep your head above water financially. But the insane rise in prices of drugs without which many would perish is deeply, deeply immoral.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What shocked you last week?
Answer: The police came to my door. Asked me if it was true that I had the key to my neighbor’s house. I said I did. They then asked me if I would please open her door for them — they had been called by one of her friends and were alarmed by what she had said. So I did. The whole house was dark. All curtains were drawn. She was on the sofa, on the edge, it’s a large sofa shaped like the letter L. A blanket draped on her. Yes, she was breathing. Turned her head really slowly but wasn’t really seeing anything. She was drowsy. There were medicine wrappers on her lap and on the floor. She tried to kill herself. And she didn’t succeed, because she had called a former partner right before she took the pills. When I entered the room, followed by the police, she recognized me. And said my name. There was a strange tone in her voice. Almost one of betrayal. I’m conflicted, now. Did she want to die, and did she hate the fact that I interrupted her? Or did she send those dramatic text messages with the explicit desire for the police or someone else to come to her rescue? I’m still not sure. It could be an elaborate cry for attention. It could also be a genuine desire for help. It could be both suicidal ideation and desperation, both, at once. The morning she made her suicide attempt, she had been in my house. This same neighbor. Drunk, crying, at eight o’clock in the morning. Telling me she’ll never be a mother, a grandmother, that her life is “effectively over” and asking me what’s the point. She has given me the same exact talk before. Nothing about it made it feel different, this time around. But it was. Because she took an overdose that same day. An ambulance took her away and I haven’t seen her since.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What's your worst habit that you can't get rid of?
Answer: Ignoring people. I don’t do it purposely… I’m just a terrible procrastinator. Someone sends me a lengthy message, on Quora, Messenger, Whatsapp, and I am a little daunted by all the words on my screen. I gloss over it. Even read the whole thing. And I put off a response. For an hour. A day. A week. About two months ago I was talking to a girl from Pakistan. She wanted to be my wife. She wasn’t really “doing it” for me. But rather than saying it to her outright? I just… disappeared. It’s a shitty thing to do. I just lost a follower over this — a guy I had some wonderful conversations with since last year. In recent months, contact lessened. I saw him as a friend, a brother even. But my responses were too brief, took too long to arrive. A few days ago he gave me another long response. I should have replied. But I didn’t. Now he doesn’t ever want to hear from me again, and I get that. It’s just, shitty. He’s a writer, a philosopher. Has a published book under his belt, on the meaning of life. I promised him I would read it. I promised him that LAST YEAR. Now we’re a year later… and nothing. I didn’t read jack-shit. I’m a chronic “ghoster”. It’s a shitty thing to do. People pour their heart out to me, and I pay them dust. Am I some evil asshole? I don’t think so. But I’m negligent as hell. The way a beautiful garden needs watering from time to time, any friendship or relationship needs attention. It can dry out, starve, and wither, just like any garden. And you’re left with a life that’s as barren as a dead garden.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the greatest love story of all time?
Answer: The other day I was talking to my friend from Pakistan. We discussed the story of Layla and Majnun. It touched me deeply… Layla was a woman whose beauty was beyond compare in the eyes of her beloved, Qays. Qays was driven insane, in fact, with his love for Layla. So insane that he began to exhibit strange behavior… her father then decided he was “too weird” to marry Layla. So she was given by her family to another man. Layla loved her Qays, however, and he loved her. They called him “Majnun”, the madman, for he acted like a madman. He became a wandering poet, banished by his family out of embarrassment. As a poet, he achieved enough fame for the mighty and powerful to hear of his tales — one powerful ruler called Qays before him, and demanded to see this great Layla. He was the great Caliph, and when he saw her, he found her ordinary. Rumi recalls this meeting: The Caliph questioned Layla, saying, “Are you truly the one For whom Majnun lost his sanity and became deranged? You are not more beautiful than many others.” Layla responded, “Stay silent; you are not Majnun!” If you possessed Majnun’s eyes, Both worlds would be unveiled to your sight. You remain in your senses, while Majnun is lost in madness, For in love, to be fully awake is treason. The more one is awake, the more one surrenders to sleep (of love), Such wakefulness is more burdensome than slumber. Stay silent, you are not Majnun… a brave response to a mighty man. The Caliph could not see in Layla the beauty, the kindness, the powerful desires she gave rise to within Qays. He could not feel this passions, could not comprehend them — they were between Layla and Majnun, only. Layla was married, a mother, banished to another land as her Majnun wandered the earth, leaving sad and longing poetry in his wake. Soon Layla’s broken heart gave up on her and she died. Majnun disappeared and his body was later found at her grave, eyes closed as if asleep. He was at peace only by her side, and in death.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is human so fragile?
Answer: Some of us are. Some of us are not. Below is a photograph of another wrestler comparing his hand to that of André Roussimoff. André’s bone structure was so enormous that his hands and the circumference of his wrist where similar to those of an average male silverback gorilla. He wasn’t fragile, physically. The men comparing hands with André are wrestlers — they’re already larger and stronger than the average man, and likely have larger hands, too. And yet they look like toddlers high-fiving their father after he comes home from a long day at work. Compared to an African elephant bull on the savannah, however, André is fragile. And the same elephant, compared to a humpback whale, is fragile, too. That said? We are fragile, as a species. And we’re working hard towards the apparent common goal of erasing ourselves from existence, and all life with it.[1]
